- <a id="ev-EV-1023"></a>**22 am Màrt, AE 2** — *The keeping of the word-list given to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair* (Cathair dhearg). The humans' priests ask Cuan shean for someone to trade words with them at a table, and Cuan shean sends to the capital. Tormod mac Ailein calls Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, who sits on the council for Clann Fhearchair and writes the best hand in the hall, and the council gives her the keeping of the island's side of the list. Her niece Muireall is to make the fair copy.
- <a id="ev-IV-0008"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 2** — *The first attempts at speech*. For a whole season clerics of the humans' Church and custodians of Dia-thìr labour to make a store of words in common. Neither side's account of what was agreed survives whole.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1005"><em>Wren and the priests come up to Cathair dhearg</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 2</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1023"><em>The keeping of the word-list given to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1024"></a>**24 an t-Iuchar, AE 2** — *Wren sets his months against the moons* (Cathair dhearg). Wren draws the twelve months of the humans' sun-year as a wheel, and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives him the island's moons from Samhnas round to the stags' moon. He writes each moon's name beside the month it most nearly matches. For Eadrach, the between-moon, he finds no place, and writes it outside the wheel with the humans' mark of a question.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0008"><em>The first attempts at speech</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1023"><em>The keeping of the word-list given to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1025"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, AE 2** — *Wren names the fuel of his own country* (Cathair dhearg). Over a brazier of peat in the long room Wren shows by signs that his people burn peat too, and also a black stone dug from under the ground, which they burn in every house. Gormshuil nic Fhearchair writes his word for it and, in the Dia-thìris column, the black stone the humans dig in their own country and burn on their hearths.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1024"><em>Wren sets his months against the moons</em>, 24 an t-Iuchar, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0009"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2** — *Wren's word-lists* (Cathair dhearg). The human cleric Samuel Wren and the custodian Gormshuil nic Fhearchair keep word-lists side by side through the season of speech-making. Wren's list survives in the Administration's letter-books. Gormshuil's is lost; only its first leaf, with forty words for the colours of broken coal, is known from a copy.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EV-1024"><em>Wren sets his months against the moons</em>, 24 an t-Iuchar, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1006"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2** — *Muireall copies the first leaf* (Cathair dhearg). In the gap-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives her loose sheets to her niece Muireall to copy fair into a book for Clann Fhearchair, and orders the colours set first, before cup and bread, alone on the first leaf with room left at the foot. Muireall copies the forty words in her young, careful hand and stops at the right-hand column, where the humans' side has one word to give.
- <a id="ev-EV-1026"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2** — *The basket of broken coal on the table* (Cathair dhearg). In the wolf-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair takes a double handful from the capital's measure for the shrines and tips it on the table before Samuel Wren in the winter sun. She names forty colours at the breaks. Wren writes some of them, then stops, turns a piece in the light and gives one word for the whole heap. She waits for him to ask for hers; he holds up a candle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0009"><em>Wren's word-lists</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1006"><em>Muireall copies the first leaf</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0010"></a>**23 an Giblean, AE 3** — *One word for the coal* (Cathair dhearg). The humans have a single word for the coloured coal, and it is their word for the black fuel they burn at home. Gormshuil's copyist notes that no Dia-thìris word in either list answers to it, and that the humans did not ask for one.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1025"><em>Wren names the fuel of his own country</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, AE 2</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1006"><em>Muireall copies the first leaf</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1026"><em>The basket of broken coal on the table</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1027"></a>**23 an Cèitean, AE 3** — *Gormshuil nic Fhearchair begins the humans' letters* (Cathair dhearg). Since Wren cannot learn her colours, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks him by signs to teach her his letters. He writes them across a sheet of his white paper, large and small, and her name beneath as he hears it, and she copies it stroke by stroke. By the end of the spring she can spell out a line of his word-list, and finds his one word under her colours.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0009"><em>Wren's word-lists</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1026"><em>The basket of broken coal on the table</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0011"></a>**24 an Cèitean, AE 3** — *Trade begins*. At first the trade is fair on both sides: the goods of Dia-thìr for tools and knowledge the lonely island lacks. For a few years it seems it may last.
- <a id="ev-EV-1028"></a>**26 an Cèitean, AE 3** — *The first bargains entered in the council roll* (Cathair dhearg). At the moon of the bright fire the strangers' iron, glass, lamp-oil and paper come up to the capital's market, and wool, hides, salt fish and dyed cloth go down to Cuan shean. Comhairle a' Chùraim enters the first bargains in its roll, fleece for knife and cloth for glass, with both prices in the island's reckoning. The measure is good on both sides.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0011"><em>Trade begins</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1027"><em>Gormshuil nic Fhearchair begins the humans' letters</em>, 23 an Cèitean, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1029"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3** — *The copy of the list sent to the loft at Muileann chaol* (Cathair dhearg). Having watched the humans burn their spoiled paper, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair has Muireall make a second fair copy of the whole list, the colours first and the note at the foot of the first leaf. She seals it in an oak chest with the seal of Clann Fhearchair and sends it east with the carriers to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais, where nothing is burned.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <em>The loft at Muileann chaol</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_IV/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Sundering.pdf#ev-III-0221">→ An Aois Scaraidh, LE 1,699</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1028"><em>The first bargains entered in the council roll</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0012"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3** — *The trading post at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The humans set up a trading post at Ros dhomhain, the capital's harbour, and give iron tools, window glass, lamp-oil and paper for wool, salt fish, hides and dyed cloth. The first tally-book of the post, kept by the trader Thomas Pike, balances evenly through its first year.
- <a id="ev-EV-1030"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3** — *The custodians' clerk keeps a slate beside Pike's book* (Ros dhomhain). The custodians of the capital shore set a clerk on a stool by the door of the humans' post at Ros dhomhain. He keeps his own tally of the day's goods on a slate in the old strokes, and each evening he and Thomas Pike read their two counts aloud and find them level.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0012"><em>The trading post at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1031"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, AE 3** — *Goods carted from Cuan shean to the post* (Cuan shean). In the first weeks of the post every bale and cask goes between the strangers' ships at Cuan shean and the counter at Ros dhomhain by cart over the moor road, two days each way. The carters of Cuan shean charge by the creel, and Harrow goes to the pilots of Caol leathan for a way by water.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0012"><em>The trading post at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1030"><em>The custodians' clerk keeps a slate beside Pike's book</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1032"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, AE 3** — *The pilots' double toll entered as fair* (Caol leathan). The pilots of Caol leathan go over the smallest of Harrow's hulls and name twice the toll of a Dia-thìreach boat for bringing her up the Abhainn gheal. Harrow is angry. Pike enters the price in the post's tally-book and writes beside it that it is fair, since the pilots know the shallows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1031"><em>Goods carted from Cuan shean to the post</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0012a"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, AE 3** — *The first hull on Loch chrom* (Abhainn gheal). Pilots of Caol leathan bring the first of the strangers' ships up the Abhainn gheal into Loch chrom, towing her with boats through the shallows below Baile ghlas, and she anchors off Ros dhomhain. Thereafter the humans' goods come to the capital shore by water, and the pilots charge a stranger's hull twice the toll of a Dia-thìreach boat.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1031"><em>Goods carted from Cuan shean to the post</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, AE 3</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1032"><em>The pilots' double toll entered as fair</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0013"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, AE 3** — *Cathair naomh sends its wool* (Cathair naomh). Cathair naomh, the city above Seann Toll on the northern coast, sends its first wool south to the humans' post by coasting boat. Its custodians take their payment in paper and ink, and with them begin the town's roll afresh.
- <a id="ev-EV-1033"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, AE 3** — *The gift of paper to Cathair naomh* (Cathair naomh). Paying the custodians of Cathair naomh for their wool in paper and ink, Pike adds a quire of his own writing-paper uncounted. It is the one line of the post's first tally-book that he does not balance, and he marks it as a gift.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0013"><em>Cathair naomh sends its wool</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1032"><em>The pilots' double toll entered as fair</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1034"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, AE 3** — *Harrow sails north-about with three hulls* (Cuan shean). At the end of an Lùnastal Edmund Harrow sails from Cuan shean for an Tìr Thall with all three hulls, north-about, carrying hides and dyed cloth. He leaves Thomas Pike at Ros dhomhain with four men, the loft, the tally-book and the goods not yet traded.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1033"><em>The gift of paper to Cathair naomh</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0014"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 3** — *Iron in the smithies* (Cathair dhearg). The smiths of Cathair dhearg take the humans' bar-iron gladly and learn to temper it in a winter. Within a few seasons the old bronze hoes are melted down for bells.
- <a id="ev-EV-1007"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, AE 3** — *The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). A smith off Harrow's ships, sent up by Pike, comes to the smiths' lane below Drochaid Cathair dhearg and works through the autumn at the forge of Gilleasbuig Gobha. Having no words in common, the two smiths agree on the colours of hot iron.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1035"></a>**6 an Dàmhair, AE 3** — *Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade* (Cathair dhearg). In the last days of an Dùbhlachd Gilleasbuig Gobha tempers his first blade alone at his forge in Cathair dhearg, a knife of the humans' bar-iron drawn to the straw next the brown. It cuts hide that the old bronze knives only bruise. He gives it to his wife Sìne.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1007"><em>The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1036"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, AE 3** — *Iron hoes on the capital's fields* (Cathair dhearg). Through am Faoilleach and am Màrt the smiths of Cathair dhearg forge iron hoes, and the farmers above the lake pay for them with their old bronze hoes, brought down in sacks. Some of the bronze hoes bear the marks of the fields they worked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1035"><em>Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1037"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, AE 3** — *The bells of Cathair dhearg cast from the hoes* (Cathair dhearg). At the asking of the custodians, Gilleasbuig Gobha and two smiths of the lane melt down the bronze hoes in a mould-pit behind his forge and cast four bells. They hang in the market gate, at the bridge and at the temple of Cathair dhearg, and are first rung together at Lùnastal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1036"><em>Iron hoes on the capital's fields</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0015"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, AE 4** — *Dyes for Baile Mòr mhòr* (Baile Mòr mhòr). The weavers of Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern coast trade their cloth for the humans' dyes, a red and a blue brighter than any the island could make. Within a few years the old madder fields about the town go back to grass.
- <a id="ev-IV-0016"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, AE 4** — *Harrow's second voyage* (Cuan shean). Harrow sails for home with hides and dyed cloth and comes back with four ships in place of three. He brings carpenters, a surgeon, and a letter from a trading house in an Tìr Thall asking what else the island has.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1034"><em>Harrow sails north-about with three hulls</em>, 15 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1038"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, AE 4** — *The trading house's letter read at the post* (Ros dhomhain). Toward the end of an Dàmhair Thomas Pike reads at his counter the letter Harrow has brought from the trading house over the sea, aloud in both tongues. It asks what else the island has: timber, tin, copper, lead, and what the rocks hold. Gilleasbuig Gobha hears it read.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0016"><em>Harrow's second voyage</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1037"><em>The bells of Cathair dhearg cast from the hoes</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0017"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, AE 4** — *The shipwrights of Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). The shipwrights of Inis mhòr come to look at the humans' hulls and measure them with knotted cords. Their guild had built nothing greater than a coaster since the fleet of the Sundering, and the old craft of building for deep water was half forgotten.
- <a id="ev-IV-0018"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4** — *The surgeon Jonas Tull* (Cuan shean). The humans' surgeon, Jonas Tull, sets the broken leg of a fisherman of Cuan shean who had been given up as lame. The town's custodian enters it in the roll as the first debt owed to a stranger.
- <a id="ev-EV-1039"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4** — *Oighrig nic Leòid witnesses the setting of the leg* (Cuan shean). Old and ill, Oighrig nic Leòid, custodian of Cuan shean, is carried to the fisherman's house to watch Jonas Tull break and set the crooked leg again. Told he has done it eleven times and nine have walked, she says that nine of eleven is more than the island has, and writes the debt in the roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0018"><em>The surgeon Jonas Tull</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1038"><em>The trading house's letter read at the post</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, AE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0019"></a>**30 am Màrt, AE 5** — *Salt from Seann Warr* (Seann Warr). The salt-pans of Seann Warr begin to sell to Pike's post by the barrel. They are the first goods of Dia-thìr that the humans come back asking for twice.
- <a id="ev-EV-1040"></a>**4 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Pike's first two years balanced* (Ros dhomhain). In the first days of an Giblean Thomas Pike closes the tally-book of the post at Ros dhomhain on its second year. Over two nights he and the custodians' clerk go through every line of both years, book against slate, and the two counts stand level.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0012"><em>The trading post at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0019"><em>Salt from Seann Warr</em>, 30 am Màrt, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1039"><em>Oighrig nic Leòid witnesses the setting of the leg</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0020"></a>**14 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Wool at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The walled harbour of Caol leathan sends its first wool-ship to the humans' post. Its merchants will be paid only in iron by weight, and the tally-book of the post names them the hardest bargainers on the island.
- <a id="ev-EV-1008"></a>**15 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Pike writes home of the island's coal* (Ros dhomhain). Answering the trading house, Thomas Pike writes of the island's timber, salt, wool, hides and smiths, and that it has copper, tin and some silver. Having held a piece from a custodian's hearth to the window, he writes that the island has coal of a middling sort, and much of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0016"><em>Harrow's second voyage</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0012"><em>The trading post at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1009"></a>**16 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Gilleasbuig Gobha forges a hinge for Pike's chest* (Cathair dhearg). Gilleasbuig Gobha makes a new hinge of the strangers' bar-iron for the iron-bound chest under Pike's counter, where letters for over the sea are kept. He tempers it to the blue and will take nothing for the work. Pike's letter on the coal goes over the sea in that chest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1041"></a>**17 an Giblean, AE 5** — *Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). A boat of the humans' post rows down from Cuan shean deep with sawn plank and grounds on the shingle north of the quay at Baile dhìreach. Seven men of Harrow's ships come ashore, the carpenter William Rook and the cooper Samuel Hale among them, seeking a sheltered beach for a slip where the small craft of the post may be mended and built.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0016"><em>Harrow's second voyage</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1042"></a>**21 an Giblean, AE 5** — *The rule of the shingle read to the strangers* (Baile dhìreach). The shingle above the wrack-line at Baile dhìreach is held in keeping for the whole town and may not be sold. Seonag nic Aoidh of the salt-house reads the town's rule to the strangers on the shore: the well drawn in turn, no fire on the shingle in the herring season, no hammer on the rest-nights. Rook says his men will keep it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1041"><em>Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach</em>, 17 an Giblean, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0021"></a>**22 an Giblean, AE 5** — *The first mixed settlement*. A small coastal town takes in both Dia-thìrich and humans under one rule. It is not tried again.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1041"><em>Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach</em>, 17 an Giblean, AE 5</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1042"><em>The rule of the shingle read to the strangers</em>, 21 an Giblean, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1513"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, AE 5** — *The compact written in both tongues* (Baile dhìreach). Through the moons of harvest six sit at the mending-table in the net-loft of Baile dhìreach, three of the town and three of the strangers, and write the town's rule twice. A clerk of Inis thais writes the Dia-thìris book and William Rook the humans'. The net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh and the cooper Samuel Hale are fetched to find the words for the moorings.
- <a id="ev-EV-1514"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *The chair set to turn at the humans' new year* (Baile dhìreach). The six of Baile dhìreach find that the town's year turns at Samhain and is counted by moons, while the humans' year turns in the dead of winter on a fixed day. They write in both books that Iain mac Chaluim holds the chair until the humans' year turns, and William Rook for the year after, and so in turn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1513"><em>The compact written in both tongues</em>, 24 an t-Ògmhios, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0022"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *Baile dhìreach under one council* (Baile dhìreach). The small port of Baile dhìreach on the south-west coast takes Dia-thìrich and humans under one council of six, three of each. Its founding compact is written twice, once in each tongue, the only such compact of the age.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1513"><em>The compact written in both tongues</em>, 24 an t-Ògmhios, AE 5</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1514"><em>The chair set to turn at the humans' new year</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0023"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *The first council of Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). The council is chaired in alternate years by the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim and the human carpenter William Rook. The harbour dues go half to the custodians at Cathair dhearg and half to the humans' post.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1514"><em>The chair set to turn at the humans' new year</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1501"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *Samuel Hale tightens the herring barrels* (Baile dhìreach). The human cooper Samuel Hale takes down the leaking herring barrels of Baile dhìreach stave by stave and makes every one of them tight by the end of summer, beginning with the idle row of the salter Ruairidh. He takes a bowl from the pot for his pay, and asks for Dia-thìris words, which he writes under his own.
- <a id="ev-EV-1502"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, AE 5** — *The first boat off the humans' slip* (Baile dhìreach). On the first evening of Lùnastal the humans' slip at Baile dhìreach launches a small coaster of the strangers' pattern, deeper in the keel than the boats of the south-west. She is built for the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim, paid for in fish and labour and rigged with the town's rope; his wife pours sea water on her bow and asks Manannan to keep her.
- <a id="ev-EV-1503"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, AE 5** — *A stranger's prayer at the lamps of the drowned* (Baile dhìreach). At the dark of the year Baile dhìreach sets lamps along its quay for its drowned, as the harbours of the west do. The humans of the shingle stand in the line, and the cooper Samuel Hale says a prayer to Crìosd in his own tongue for shipmates lost in the northern sea on the voyage out. Eilidh nic Ruairidh sets a lamp for them.
- <a id="ev-EV-1515"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, AE 5** — *The first human house on the shingle* (Baile dhìreach). The carpenters of Baile dhìreach lay a slip of split logs, raise an open shed, and build a house of sawn plank on a sill of beach stones, with a window of glass. Since nothing may be built on the shingle, the town rules that the house is a tent, and calls it so. The humans' book of the town enters it as the first house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0021"><em>The first mixed settlement</em>, 22 an Giblean, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1516"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, AE 5** — *Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). The humans' post at Ros dhomhain writes to ask why the dues of a harbour its own men have half rebuilt go wholly to the custodians at Cathair dhearg. The custodians of Inis thais write to ask by what rule strangers keep a yard on a shingle held in keeping. Iain mac Chaluim says the town must write its rule down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0022"><em>Baile dhìreach under one council</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1515"><em>The first human house on the shingle</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1517"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, AE 5** — *The first dues shared* (Baile dhìreach). At its first sitting the council of six of Baile dhìreach settles a quarrel over a mooring ring and sends the harbour dues out in two halves: one in a sack by a boy up the road to the custodians at Cathair dhearg, the other round by boat to the humans' post at Ros dhomhain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0023"><em>The first council of Baile dhìreach</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1516"><em>Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach</em>, 30 an t-Samhain, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1518"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 5** — *Ruairidh refuses the cooper* (Baile dhìreach). On the night of Samhain, while the town keeps its fire on the headland above the quay and the humans watch from the last cairn, the cooper Samuel Hale comes to the door of the salter Ruairidh to ask for his daughter Eilidh nic Ruairidh. Ruairidh sends him away, saying that a council is one thing and a hearth another.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0022"><em>Baile dhìreach under one council</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1519"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 5** — *The bidding carried to Inis thais* (Baile dhìreach). In the black moon the council of Baile dhìreach sends its compact along the shore to the temple city of Inis thais in both tongues, with a clause bidding any town of the coast sit with it on the same terms. The pilot Murchadh mac Iain carries it by boat and brings back word that the custodian will write.
- <a id="ev-IV-0024"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *Inis thais declines the compact* (Inis thais). The city of Inis thais, whose harbour lies a few miles from Baile dhìreach, is bidden to join the joint council and declines. Its custodian writes that one town may be a trial, but two would be a rule.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1519"><em>The bidding carried to Inis thais</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1520"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook* (Baile dhìreach). On the morning the humans' year turns, in the net-loft of Baile dhìreach, the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim gives up the chair of the council of six and the carpenter William Rook takes it, as the compact bids. Both books enter it in a line, the one by the day and the year, the other by the moon. The letter from Inis thais is read the same morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0023"><em>The first council of Baile dhìreach</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0024"><em>Inis thais declines the compact</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, AE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1519"><em>The bidding carried to Inis thais</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1521"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *Rook's ruling on the dragged mooring* (Baile dhìreach). A boat of the post drags her anchor at Baile dhìreach and fouls the salter Ruairidh's mooring, and her master will not pay. William Rook, in the chair, orders his own countryman to pay the town's rate for rope and ring, in iron by weight, that day, and asks Ruairidh whether the rate is fair.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0023"><em>The first council of Baile dhìreach</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1520"><em>Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1522"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *The storm of the wolf-moon at Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). A three-day storm off the west drives the sea over the quay of Baile dhìreach and up the shingle towards the boats. On the second night the town and the humans haul the boats over the crest together with ropes, blocks and a capstan-bar from the slip. The salt-house chimney and half the roof of the humans' house are lost.
- <a id="ev-EV-1523"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *Ruairidh relents* (Baile dhìreach). After half a moon of the carpenter in the chair, in which nothing in Baile dhìreach has fallen but a chimney, the salter Ruairidh helps the humans roof their house again and sends word by his daughter Eilidh nic Ruairidh that the cooper Samuel Hale may come up to the house for his bowl himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0023"><em>The first council of Baile dhìreach</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1522"><em>The storm of the wolf-moon at Baile dhìreach</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0025"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, AE 6** — *A supply ship lost on the western reefs* (Muir Mhanannain). A human supply ship strikes the reefs off the western coast in fog, and nine of her crew drown. Her master was sailing by a chart drawn from memory, the humans' letter-books complain, on a coast lit only by the old driftwood fires.
- <a id="ev-EV-1524"></a>**5 an Gearran, AE 6** — *The nine drowned buried on the western shore* (Baile fhiadhaich). The nine drowned of the human supply-brig are buried in the dunes above the tide-line at Baile fhiadhaich, on ground the custodian gives. A townswoman wets each grave with sea-water as the coast does for its own drowned. The mason Torcall Clachair cuts nine headstones with a line for the sea, and the ship's mate scratches the names beneath.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0025"><em>A supply ship lost on the western reefs</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1525"></a>**14 an Gearran, AE 6** — *The chart from memory brought to the post* (Ros dhomhain). The mate of the lost brig carries her drowned master's chart, drawn from memory, to the post at Ros dhomhain. It sets the point where she struck a mile too far out to sea and shows no reefs below it. The ships' masters at the post argue over it at Thomas Pike's counter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0025"><em>A supply ship lost on the western reefs</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0026"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 6** — *The beacons asked for*. Human seamen, strange to the coasts of Dia-thìr, ask for standing beacons. The builders of the Dia-thìrich agree, not yet seeing what the beacons will bring.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1525"><em>The chart from memory brought to the post</em>, 14 an Gearran, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1526"></a>**24 am Màrt, AE 6** — *The masters of building answer the strangers* (Cathair dhearg). Comhairle a' Chùraim passes the strangers' asking to the seven master builders of Cathair dhearg. They agree that towers may be raised on the headlands where each place's custodian gives leave, with a Dia-thìreach builder to choose the ground. Torcall Clachair alone asks about coal, and the old ruling that no coal feeds a sea-fire is kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0026"><em>The beacons asked for</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>No coal on the beacons</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0029">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0027"></a>**29 am Màrt, AE 6** — *The beacon headlands walked* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The human navigator James Fenn and the Dia-thìreach mason Torcall Clachair walk the coast together to choose the places of the new beacons, and mark the five headlands of the old fires. Fenn's chart survives; Torcall's cairns for the most part do not.
- <a id="ev-EV-1504"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, AE 6** — *Pike writes of the natives* (Ros dhomhain). Thomas Pike enters in the post's letter-book that the islanders have agreed to the lights without difficulty and without asking what they would cost. It is the first page of his letter-book to call the Dia-thìrich the natives. The custodians' roll sets down the same asking as a request that the old sea-fires be built higher and kept all night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0026"><em>The beacons asked for</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1505"></a>**6 an Dàmhair, AE 6** — *No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair* (Muileann gheal). James Fenn asks for a night fire on the summit of Binnean a' Chlachair, the highest ground of the island. Torcall Clachair and the herders of Muileann gheal refuse, keeping the custom of the hills. Torcall lays one stone on the herders' cairn, and Fenn takes his sights by day to a linen square, four days slower. The two winter at Muileann gheal.
- <a id="ev-EV-1527"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, AE 6** — *Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland* (Tobar dhearg). On the southern cape at Tobar dhearg, beside the old dry-stone fire-tower where the village households burn driftwood and seal fat in turn, Torcall Clachair builds a cairn to mark ground for a new tower. James Fenn writes a name from his own shore on the cape in his chart. Torcall answers that the cape has a name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The beacon at Tobar dhearg</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_II/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Ailean.pdf#ev-I-0164">→ An Aois Ailein, GE 2,420</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>No coal on the beacons</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0029">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1505"><em>No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1528"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 6** — *The second cairn on the eastern cape* (Baile ìseal). At Baile ìseal, whose fire is lit to bring the boats home in a storm, Torcall Clachair and James Fenn sit up with the watch and see a raiders' light on the nearest islet. The watchman says a greater light would bring home more men of both kinds. He helps Torcall lift the capstone of the second cairn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The beacon at Baile ìseal</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_II/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Ailean.pdf#ev-I-0161">→ An Aois Ailein, GE 2,418</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1527"><em>Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1529"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, AE 6** — *The households of Àth dhearg asked hearth by hearth* (Àth dhearg). The custodian of Àth dhearg will not give away the fire-shelf above the rock-cut stair, saying it belongs to the households who cut it. Torcall Clachair and James Fenn go round the hearths for eleven days. Most say yes and two say no. The third cairn is raised at the end of the shelf, and the custodian climbs up with bread.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The beacon at Àth dhearg</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_II/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Ailean.pdf#ev-I-0163">→ An Aois Ailein, GE 2,419</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1528"><em>The second cairn on the eastern cape</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1530"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, AE 6** — *Three yards of ash at Muileann bheag* (Muileann bheag). Seeking the depth for a tower's footing, James Fenn digs beside the old shore-fire on the northern point at Muileann bheag with Torcall Clachair and a boy of the village. They go down through bands of black ash and red earth and find no rock at three yards. Torcall sets the fourth cairn inland on sound rock.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The beacon at Muileann bheag</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_II/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Ailean.pdf#ev-I-0162">→ An Aois Ailein, GE 2,419</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1529"><em>The households of Àth dhearg asked hearth by hearth</em>, 24 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1531"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, AE 6** — *Baile chrom's condition for the fifth cairn* (Baile chrom). The households of Baile chrom, whose headland fire has always warned boats off the water of Uilebheist na Mara, say the old fire cannot both warn and call. They give leave for a tower on condition that the old fire be kept alight beside it on driftwood. James Fenn agrees, and Torcall Clachair builds the fifth cairn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_I/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Ancient_Age.pdf#ev-I-0041">→ An Aois Àrsaidh, VE 3,042</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1530"><em>Three yards of ash at Muileann bheag</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1532"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 6** — *The fire on the north-west headland raised for Fenn* (Baile chrom). At Lùnastal Torcall Clachair keeps a high fire of driftwood and seal fat on the headland at Baile chrom for three nights, burning no coal. On the third night James Fenn, rowed west by fishers of Achadh àrsaidh past Coinneachadh nan Long, sees it sink below the sea's rim at near thirty miles. The sea end of his line is fixed there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0001a"><em>The ships met off the north-west</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 1</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1531"><em>Baile chrom's condition for the fifth cairn</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1533"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, AE 6** — *The cairns of the line laid across the island* (Cnoc bheag). Through the autumn James Fenn sights station after station east from the Baile chrom headland, and Torcall Clachair raises a narrow cairn capped with a white stone on each chosen top. Hired boys carry a chain of iron links between them. The string of cairns crosses the moors south of Cnoc bheag and the hills of the interior.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1532"><em>The fire on the north-west headland raised for Fenn</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0027a"></a>**26 an Giblean, AE 7** — *Fenn's line* (Dia-thìr). On the same survey James Fenn runs a line of sights across the whole island, from the open sea off the north-west, where ships coming down from the north first raise the land, to the water off the eastern cape. He makes it a hundred and fifty-five miles, some thirty of them sea at the western end. It is the first measure of Dia-thìr from side to side, and every chart the Company draws afterwards is scaled to it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1505"><em>No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, AE 6</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1532"><em>The fire on the north-west headland raised for Fenn</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 6</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1533"><em>The cairns of the line laid across the island</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, AE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1534"></a>**5 an Cèitean, AE 7** — *The council asked for a ruling on the marriage* (Baile dhìreach). Iain mac Chaluim writes for the council of Baile dhìreach to the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asking whether the marriage of a Dia-thìreach net-maker to a human cooper may be entered in the custodians' roll, and whether its children stand as a Dia-thìreach mother's. The rider returns with no answer. The council resolves to enter the marriage itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0022"><em>Baile dhìreach under one council</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0023"><em>The first council of Baile dhìreach</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0028"></a>**26 an Cèitean, AE 7** — *A marriage in two tongues* (Baile dhìreach). At Baile dhìreach the net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh weds the human cooper Samuel Hale. The council enters the marriage in both its books; the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asked for a ruling, send none.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1534"><em>The council asked for a ruling on the marriage</em>, 5 an Cèitean, AE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1506"></a>**31 an Cèitean, AE 7** — *Torcall witnesses in the Dia-thìreach book* (Baile dhìreach). At the wedding on the quay of Baile dhìreach no custodian comes to witness. James Fenn signs for the bridegroom in the humans' book, and Iain mac Chaluim calls the mason Torcall Clachair from the crowd to sign the Dia-thìreach book. William Rook and Iain mac Chaluim close the two books side by side.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0028"><em>A marriage in two tongues</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1535"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, AE 7** — *The island's names written on Fenn's chart* (Baile dhìreach). On the night of the wedding at Baile dhìreach James Fenn writes the Dia-thìris names of the five headlands under his own on his chart, as Torcall Clachair tells them: Tobar dhearg, Baile ìseal, Àth dhearg, Muileann bheag and Baile chrom. At the mountain in the middle of his line he writes Binnean a' Chlachair.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027a"><em>Fenn's line</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1506"><em>Torcall witnesses in the Dia-thìreach book</em>, 31 an Cèitean, AE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1536"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, AE 7** — *Harrow asks for the terms in writing* (Cathair dhearg). Edmund Harrow comes up the lake road to Cathair dhearg with Thomas Pike to speak for him and asks Tormod mac Ailein that the terms on which the humans stay be written and signed by both sides. He says that a man is coming from an Tìr Thall to speak for its government, and that he himself has asked for him. The council's leave, he says, stands only in the council's roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0005"><em>The Council of Custodians grants leave</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1537"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, AE 7** — *Tull draws Ceann a' Chùraim's tooth* (Cathair dhearg). Passing through Cathair dhearg on his way to the post at Ros dhomhain, the surgeon Jonas Tull draws a rotten tooth from the jaw of Tormod mac Ailein, which the capital's physician had left to wait a month. Tormod keeps the tooth in a box. It is the second debt owed to a stranger that the custodians know of, and it is owed by Ceann a' Chùraim.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0018"><em>The surgeon Jonas Tull</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1536"><em>Harrow asks for the terms in writing</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, AE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1538"></a>**5 an Gearran, AE 8** — *Pell lands at Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). Josiah Pell comes ashore at Cuan shean from the first ship of the year down from the north, dry-shod on a plank, with a leather case he lets no one carry. He asks for a horse. Oighrig nic Leòid, who gave Harrow water, lends him her own and writes to the council the same day that he did not ask for water.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-IV-0002"><em>Three ships off Cuan shean</em>, 5 an Gearran, AE 1</a> (Harrow's landing).</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1539"></a>**18 am Màrt, AE 8** — *Pell rides to the council hall* (Cuan shean). Josiah Pell rides the twenty-six miles from Cuan shean to Cathair dhearg in a day and, passing by the humans' post, asks at dusk for the council hall and Ceann a' Chùraim. Tormod mac Ailein comes down to him in his house-shoes. With no one to carry words between them, Pell greets him with the island's word of leave-taking, learned on the ship.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1538"><em>Pell lands at Cuan shean</em>, 5 an Gearran, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1540"></a>**29 am Màrt, AE 8** — *The terms asked for in two tongues* (Cathair dhearg). In the talks at Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain, with Samuel Wren putting each sentence into the other tongue, Tormod mac Ailein asks that the terms be written twice, as the compact of Baile dhìreach was. Pell answers that one text must govern before the lawyers of an Tìr Thall, and that a copy in Dia-thìris will follow when there is leisure. Wren gives it as an dèidh làimh.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-IV-0022"><em>Baile dhìreach under one council</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a> (the compact written twice); ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1539"><em>Pell rides to the council hall</em>, 18 am Màrt, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0029"></a>**27 an Giblean, AE 8** — *The first written treaty*. The terms on which the humans stay are first set down in writing, in the humans' tongue only. No one among the Dia-thìrich speaks against it at the time.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1536"><em>Harrow asks for the terms in writing</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, AE 7</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1540"><em>The terms asked for in two tongues</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0030"></a>**7 an Cèitean, AE 8** — *The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The treaty is signed in the council hall at Cathair dhearg by Tormod mac Ailein for the custodians, and for the Administration by Josiah Pell, newly come as the humans' first Commissioner. Tormod could not read the tongue it was written in. Who read it to him is not told.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1538"><em>Pell lands at Cuan shean</em>, 5 an Gearran, AE 8</a>; ○ Same place <a href="#ev-EV-1539"><em>Pell rides to the council hall</em>, 18 am Màrt, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1507"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, AE 8** — *Gormshuil called back from Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, gone east with the season's copies for the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, is sent for by rider when the talks with Pell run fast. She starts back the day the rider finds her, but the rain is on the hills and the fords are up, and she is still on the road when the terms are signed.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-IV-0030"><em>The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 7 an Cèitean, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1508"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, AE 8** — *Gormshuil given a copy of the terms* (Cathair dhearg). Two days after the signing Gormshuil nic Fhearchair comes in from the hills, reads the entry in the roll standing, and asks Pell through Samuel Wren for the terms in the strangers' tongue, since the copy in Dia-thìris is to wait for leisure. Pell's secretary makes one within the week. She begins to read it a word at a time, and does not bring it before the council.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0030"><em>The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 7 an Cèitean, AE 8</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1509"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, AE 8** — *The masons of the capital build for Pell* (Cathair dhearg). The masons of the masons' lane at Cathair dhearg take up Pell's house on the rise, paid in bar-iron by the humans' day, which begins at midnight where the island's begins at dusk. They float grey stone over the lake on rafts and build the house square to Pell's drawn plan, facing the harbour, with its back to the capital. The council does not ask it turned.
- <a id="ev-EV-1541"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, AE 8** — *The clerk leaves the day blank* (Cathair dhearg). Entering Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg in the council's roll, the custodians' clerk writes the year by the count of An Diosal and the moon of Bealltach. The strangers have dated their sheets by their own day and month, and no one in the hall can turn the one into the other, so he leaves the day empty. It is the first such page in the roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0030"><em>The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 7 an Cèitean, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1542"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 8** — *The rise above Ros dhomhain given* (Ros dhomhain). Pell asks the council for the bare rise behind the harbour of Ros dhomhain, where the town's goats graze, to build a house for Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The goat-keepers are paid in iron pots and are glad of it, and the council gives the ground without a vote, holding it a matter of goats.
- <a id="ev-IV-0031"></a>**10 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *The Residency above Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Josiah Pell builds a house of dressed stone on the rise above Ros dhomhain and calls it the Residency. Captain Harrow, needed ashore no longer, goes back to the sea trade.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1509"><em>The masons of the capital build for Pell</em>, 5 an t-Sultain, AE 8</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1542"><em>The rise above Ros dhomhain given</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1543"></a>**16 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *Harrow takes his leave of Tormod* (Cathair dhearg). Edmund Harrow comes up to Cathair dhearg with Thomas Pike to say that Pell will govern now and a ship's master is needed ashore no longer. He tells Tormod mac Ailein that he and Pike are to have a licence to trade, and that the charter will be sent to the council and found in order. He sails north-about from Ros dhomhain two tides later.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0031"><em>The Residency above Ros dhomhain</em>, 10 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0032"></a>**18 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *The Company chartered* (Ros dhomhain). Harrow and Pike found a trading house under licence of the Administration, known on Dia-thìr simply as the Company. Its charter gives it first refusal of "all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield."<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1543"><em>Harrow takes his leave of Tormod</em>, 16 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1544"></a>**30 an Cèitean, AE 9** — *The charter lodged with the council* (Cathair dhearg). A copy of Cairt na Companaidh comes to the council at Cathair dhearg in the strangers' tongue, four sheets under a red seal. The clerk enters its coming in the roll and lays it in the chest under the east window of the hall, beside the unanswered letter from Baile dhìreach, and there it lies a month unread.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0032"><em>The Company chartered</em>, 18 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-IV-0028"><em>A marriage in two tongues</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 7</a> (the letter left unanswered).</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1545"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, AE 9** — *Gormshuil reads the charter to Tormod* (Cathair dhearg). At midsummer Gormshuil nic Fhearchair takes the charter from the council's chest and reads it by night to Tormod mac Ailein at his hearth. In the clause of all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield she finds Wren's one word for the coal, and she shows him that the charter's licence hangs from the line on goods he had asked to hear twice. He asks her to keep it between them.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-IV-0032"><em>The Company chartered</em>, 18 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0030"><em>The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 7 an Cèitean, AE 8</a>; ⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a> (the one word for the coal).</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1546"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, AE 9** — *The shore at Cathair dhomhain sold* (Cathair dhomhain). Thomas Pike buys a strip of shingle and rough grass above the lake at Cathair dhomhain from a fishing family that has drawn its nets there since An Aois Naomh, for a keg of nails, two lamps and a sheet of window-glass. The custodian of the lake shore enters the sale. It is the first ground on Dia-thìr the strangers hold by sale and not by the council's leave.
- <a id="ev-IV-0033"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, AE 9** — *The warehouse at Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). The Company builds a stone warehouse at Cathair dhomhain, along the lake shore from the capital, to keep its tools from the harbour thieves of Ros dhomhain. It is the first building on Dia-thìr the Company owns outright.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1546"><em>The shore at Cathair dhomhain sold</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1547"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, AE 9** — *The warehouse door hung* (Cathair dhomhain). The oak door of A' Chompanaidh's warehouse at Cathair dhomhain comes down the shore road from Cathair dhearg and is hung at dusk on strap hinges forged by Gilleasbuig Gobha in the smiths' lane below the bridge. Thomas Pike locks it with a long iron key. Tormod mac Ailein, who has walked out from the capital, watches it hung; the lake-shore roll calls it a good door.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0033"><em>The warehouse at Cathair dhomhain</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, AE 9</a>; ⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-IV-0014"><em>Iron in the smithies</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 3</a> (the smith's bar-iron); ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1546"><em>The shore at Cathair dhomhain sold</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0034"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, AE 9** — *The strangers' fever* (Cuan shean). A fever comes ashore at Cuan shean with a crowded ship and runs down the west coast. Ninety-one Dia-thìrich die, and eleven humans. The custodians shut the town to ships for a season, and Pell protests in writing.
- <a id="ev-EV-1548"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, AE 9** — *The hill's coal carried to Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). Eleven carriers of the hills bring the measured coal for the western hearths down from the store at Taigh na Fèithe to Cuan shean, five days on the road with ponies and a custodian's clerk. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom goes among them for the first time. Oighrig nic Leòid counts the baskets in by lamplight at the custodians' store.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0034"><em>The strangers' fever</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1549"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, AE 9** — *The carriers kept at Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). When the fever breaks out among the net-sheds, the clerk of the hill carriers and Oighrig nic Leòid forbid the eleven to take the road home, lest they carry the sickness into the hills. The carriers stay in the town through an t-Samhain, carrying water to the fever houses and the dead to their burying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0034"><em>The strangers' fever</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1548"><em>The hill's coal carried to Cuan shean</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1550"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 9** — *Oighrig answers Pell's protest* (Cuan shean). Pell's letter protesting the shutting of Cuan shean is read to Oighrig nic Leòid in the custodians' store by the humans' trader of the quay. It claims the harbour open under Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and holds the town answerable for spoiled cargo. She asks whether it says anything of the dead, and sends back the number, forty-one, and word that the ships may wait.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0034"><em>The strangers' fever</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0030"><em>The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 7 an Cèitean, AE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1549"><em>The carriers kept at Cuan shean</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0035"></a>**9 an Gearran, AE 10** — *The fever at Baile àrsaidh* (Baile àrsaidh). The strangers' fever comes to Baile àrsaidh, a day's walk up the coast, and kills its custodian and both her sons. No humans dwell in the town at all, and the custodians of the west take note of it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0036"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, AE 10** — *The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh* (Cnoc àrsaidh). At Cnoc àrsaidh in the south-west the townsfolk block the road with carts and turn back every traveller for a season, and the fever does not reach them. The Administration fines the town for hindering trade.
- <a id="ev-IV-0037"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *Prospectors in the central hills* (Muileann chrom). The Company sends two prospectors, Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer, into the hills east of the capital. They come back with sacks of broken coal, and word that the black seam runs "further than can be walked in a day."
- <a id="ev-EV-1551"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *The fever dead buried beyond the dunes* (Cuan shean). The custodians of Cuan shean will not lay the fever dead in the old ground by the harbour, and bury them in the sand beyond the dunes, out of sight of the town. The human dead lie in the same ground in a row of their own, read over by their priest. The burying slackens at the dark of the year and ends before Là Fhèill Brìde.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0034"><em>The strangers' fever</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1552"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *The hills keep their roads open* (Muileann dhearg). After the fever at Baile àrsaidh, where no human lived, the custodians of the hills meet at Taigh na Fèithe and talk of shutting the hill roads. They decide against it, since the roads carry the meal, the salt and the lamp-oil. Their roll gives the reason in the words of Seonag Liath of the old cutting: nine years of salt eaten with the strangers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0035"><em>The fever at Baile àrsaidh</em>, 9 an Gearran, AE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0036"><em>The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, AE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1553"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *Cnoc àrsaidh pays its fine in wool* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Cnoc àrsaidh, fined by Riaghaltas nan Coigreach for turning back travellers with its carts, pays the fine in sacks of wool. The hill carters carry the story east and tell it at the mill of Muileann chrom as a jest against the strangers, who have no use for so much wool.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0036"><em>The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, AE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1554"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *The prospectors find no guide* (Muileann chrom). Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer come up the road to Muileann chrom with a letter of A' Chompanaidh asking lodging and a guide into the hills. The miller houses and feeds them, but no man of the hill will lead strangers onto it with a hammer. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill offers himself for a silver coin of an Tìr Thall, against his father's wish.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0037"><em>Prospectors in the central hills</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1555"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *The seam walked with the prospectors* (Muileann chrom). For eleven days Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill leads Stone and Mercer through the hills north and east of Muileann chrom, by the stream-cuts where the seam shows. They break coal at every gully, a sack to each, and Mercer counts the paces between. Raghnall names the colours of the broken coal; the prospectors have one word for all of it. He carries a sack down on his own back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0037"><em>Prospectors in the central hills</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1554"><em>The prospectors find no guide</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1556"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10** — *The custodians write for the coal* (Ros dhomhain). The custodians of the vein send a letter in Dia-thìris to Thomas Pike at Ros dhomhain, asking that all the coal broken on the hill above Muileann chrom without leave be brought back to be laid in the rock with the proper words. They write twice more in the spring before any answer comes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0037"><em>Prospectors in the central hills</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 11 – 20

- <a id="ev-IV-0038"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 11** — *The sacks returned to the rock* (Muileann chrom). The custodians of the vein demand the broken coal back, to lay it in the rock again with the proper words. The Company returns half. The custodians' roll enters the other half as "carried west."<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-1556"><em>The custodians write for the coal</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0039"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 11** — *The first mining contracts*. Trade sours into bargain. Dia-thìrich hands mine the vein on a scale that no reverent custom had ever used.
- <a id="ev-IV-0040"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, AE 11** — *The first pit at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Under the first contract a Dia-thìreach crew of thirty opens a working at Muileann chrom, paid by the ton in iron tools and lamp-oil. The custodians' own cuttings had never been measured by weight at all.
- <a id="ev-EV-1510"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 11** — *Six sacks come back to Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). At the summer's end a human carter brings six of the thirteen sacks back up the road to the mill of Muileann chrom with a paper no one there can read. Asked for the rest, he points west, towards Ros dhomhain and the ships, and turns his cart round.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0038"><em>The sacks returned to the rock</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1511"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, AE 11** — *The first contract read at the mill* (Muileann chrom). Abel Stone brings the first contract of A' Chompanaidh to Muileann chrom with two carts of steel-pointed picks, bar-iron and lamp-oil. It is read at the mill in both tongues. The interpreter from Ros dhomhain can find no Dia-thìris for the ton and calls it "a great load, weighed". Some of the older hewers walk out before the end.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0039"><em>The first mining contracts</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1512"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11** — *Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty* (Muileann chrom). Abel Stone names Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who walked the seam with him, to lead the first crew of the hill. The crew is thirty: young men of the hewers' and shepherds' households, two from the mill and three older hewers of the old cutting. Raghnall's father, a hewer of that cutting, will not join it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0039"><em>The first mining contracts</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0040"><em>The first pit at Muileann chrom</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1557"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11** — *The returned half laid in the rock* (Muileann chrom). At the old cutting above Muileann chrom the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe and Seonag Liath sort the returned coal by colour and by gully, and the hewers lay it back into the clefts with clay while the custodians say the words for a thing taken out of season. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill carries all six sacks up to the face. He gives the clerk the word "west" for the rest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0038"><em>The sacks returned to the rock</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1512"><em>Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1558"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11** — *The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). On the day the first pit is opened below the old cutting, A' Chompanaidh sets up an iron beam on a timber tripod at the pit-mouth. At dusk the clerk adds his figures and Stone calls out one ton, the first coal of the hills ever weighed. The crew cheers, and the figure is written in the pit-book against Raghnall's name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0040"><em>The first pit at Muileann chrom</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1557"><em>The returned half laid in the rock</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-1559"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11** — *The first crew paid in iron and oil* (Muileann chrom). On the first market-day after the opening of the pit, the crew of thirty at Muileann chrom are paid for their tons in picks and lamp-oil at the rate written on the contract, to the last measure of oil. The pit-book of A' Chompanaidh balances to the line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0040"><em>The first pit at Muileann chrom</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-1558"><em>The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0041"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, AE 12** — *A coal quay at Ceann fhada* (Ceann fhada). The Company builds a stone quay at Ceann fhada, a fishing hamlet below the hills, for loading coal into coasting barges. The fishermen are paid for their foreshore in iron nails, by weight.
- <a id="ev-EV-2010"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, AE 12** — *The nails weighed again at Ceann fhada* (Ceann fhada). The river-fishers and pilots of Ceann fhada, paid by weight in iron nails for the foreshore under the new coal quay, carry their nails to the fish-shed and weigh each man's share again on the old beam they weigh salmon on. Every share is true to the ounce. A pilot enters in the roll of Ceann fhada that the weight was true and the men ashamed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0041"><em>A coal quay at Ceann fhada</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2011"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, AE 12** — *The first coal barge goes down from Ceann fhada* (Ceann fhada). Carts from the pit at Muileann chrom tip the first coal into a flat barge moored against the new quay at Ceann fhada. Two pilots of the hamlet, paid by A' Chompanaidh, take her down the Abhainn uaine at the sweeps, since no one else knows the river.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0041"><em>A coal quay at Ceann fhada</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0040"><em>The first pit at Muileann chrom</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0042"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, AE 12** — *Wren's grammar* (Ros dhomhain). Samuel Wren finishes a grammar of Dia-thìris for the Mission, the house of the humans' Church on Dia-thìr. It is careful and true in most things, and it gives the word for the vein's custodians as "keepers of the coal."
- <a id="ev-EV-2012"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, AE 12** — *Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Wren's grammar to the custodians* (Cathair dhearg). At the Samhain sitting of the council at Cathair dhearg, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Samuel Wren's grammar aloud to the custodians of the hills and puts it into Dia-thìris. She tells them that in the humans' tongue a keeper is one who has a thing and holds it until paid. Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr enters in her roll that the strangers' book calls the custodians keepers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0042"><em>Wren's grammar</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0043"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, AE 13** — *The hawk-priests read Wren* (Cnoc bheag). The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag ask the Mission for a copy of Wren's grammar, to read what the humans write of them. The Mission sends one. Of all the copies that survive it bears the most notes in the margins.
- <a id="ev-EV-2013"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, AE 13** — *A hawk-priest's note beside the three words* (Cnoc bheag). In the copy of Wren's grammar kept by the hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag, a priest writes in the margin beside the humans' name for the custodians, in Dia-thìris, that Wren writes as a man counts sacks, and signs it with a hawk's head.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0043"><em>The hawk-priests read Wren</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, AE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0042"><em>Wren's grammar</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2012"><em>Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Wren's grammar to the custodians</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, AE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2014"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, AE 13** — *The custodians of the hills called on the contracts* (Cathair dhearg). At the dark of the year the council at Cathair dhearg calls the custodians of the hills to say what their villages make of the contracts coming up from Muileann chrom. It hears four days of talk of iron, lamp-oil and the ton, and makes no ruling.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0039"><em>The first mining contracts</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0044"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13** — *The Mission chapel* (Ros dhomhain). The Mission raises a timber chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain, the first church on the island. Its bell is the first iron bell on the island, and the custodians ask that it not be rung before the fishing fleet is out.
- <a id="ev-EV-2001"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13** — *The bell rung once before the fleet was out* (Ros dhomhain). On the morning of its hanging the iron bell of the chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain is rung for the first service while the fishers are loading their boats in silence, as the rule of that quay requires. The crews unload and go home. Three boats of more than twenty go out on the lake that day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0044"><em>The Mission chapel</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EV-2015"><em>The chapel bell kept until the fleet is out</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2015"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13** — *The chapel bell kept until the fleet is out* (Ros dhomhain). At the chapel door the custodian of Ros dhomhain tells the minister, with Samuel Wren putting it into the humans' tongue, that a bell over the water before the boats are out is the bell for the drowned. The minister agrees at once, and the bell is rung thereafter only when the last boat is clear of the harbour mouth.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0044"><em>The Mission chapel</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2001"><em>The bell rung once before the fleet was out</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2016"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13** — *The contract carried up to Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). A boy of Muileann chrom carries a contract of A' Chompanaidh up to Doire mhòr, naming the south slope of its hill under the oaks for a working. Beathag Dhubh has it read to her twice in the mill-house at Muileann chrom by the young man of Ros dhomhain who puts A' Chompanaidh's words into Dia-thìris.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0039"><em>The first mining contracts</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0045"></a>**29 am Màrt, AE 14** — *The first refusal*. One mining settlement will not sign a contract. For the present it is passed by, not punished.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2016"><em>The contract carried up to Doire mhòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2002"></a>**12 an Giblean, AE 14** — *Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth* (Doire mhòr). On the evening the day for the marks goes by, Beathag Dhubh calls the seven households of Doire mhòr to her fire and has the contract told to them. They talk of iron, oats and sheep. The oldest woman of the hill says that the hill is not theirs, and the households give the answer to the custodian to give.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0045"><em>The first refusal</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0046"></a>**27 an Giblean, AE 14** — *Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). The settlement that refused was Doire mhòr, in the hills above Muileann chrom, and its custodian was Beathag Dhubh. Her answer to the Company's agent is known only in his words: that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2002"><em>Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2017"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, AE 14** — *The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The agent of A' Chompanaidh who climbed to Doire mhòr writes that night at the pit-office by the mill that the custodian heard him out in the rain, did not ask him in, and answered that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy. He sends it to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir with the week's figures and advises that the working be opened elsewhere.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0046"><em>Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2002"><em>Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0047"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 15** — *The road around Doire mhòr* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The Company opens its next working at Cnoc fhiadhaich instead, and runs its cart-road round the fields of Doire mhòr and not through them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2017"><em>The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2018"></a>**16 am Màrt, AE 15** — *The road pegged across Doire mhòr's fields and moved* (Doire mhòr). Surveyors of A' Chompanaidh peg the line of the new cart-road from Cnoc fhiadhaich straight across the three best fields of Doire mhòr. Beathag Dhubh sends word to the custodian of Muileann chrom that the fields are in no contract. Five days later the surveyors pull their pegs and lay the line round the foot of the field walls, a mile the longer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0047"><em>The road around Doire mhòr</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2017"><em>The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2019"></a>**23 am Màrt, AE 15** — *Fenn's lens carried to Tobar dhearg* (Ros dhomhain). The great glass for the new tower on the southern cape, ground over the sea, is carried from Ros dhomhain to Tobar dhearg on a cart packed in straw. James Fenn sets it in the lamp-room of the tower Torcall Clachair has raised over the old fire-tower.
- <a id="ev-IV-0048"></a>**9 an Cèitean, AE 15** — *Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The first of the new beacons is finished on the southern headland at Tobar dhearg: a round tower of grey stone raised over the old fire-tower, paid for by the Company, with a Dia-thìreach keeper. Torcall Clachair builds it; James Fenn sets its lens.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2019"><em>Fenn's lens carried to Tobar dhearg</em>, 23 am Màrt, AE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2020"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, AE 15** — *The cart-road round Doire mhòr finished* (Doire mhòr). Hill men paid in iron finish the cart-road of A' Chompanaidh from Cnoc fhiadhaich round the fields of Doire mhòr to the quay at Ceann fhada, with a timber bridge at the lower ford of the Doire mhòr stream. The first loaded carts come round the bend in the autumn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0047"><em>The road around Doire mhòr</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2021"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, AE 15** — *The carters water their horses at Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). The carters on the new road ask Beathag Dhubh's leave to water their horses at the stream where the road crosses it below Doire mhòr, and she gives it. In wet weather they eat their bread under the oaks before the last pull down to the river.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0047"><em>The road around Doire mhòr</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0049"></a>**29 am Màrt, AE 16** — *The first keeper of Tobar dhearg* (Tobar dhearg). The first keeper of the southern beacon is Anna nic Dhòmhnaill of Tobar dhearg village, a fisherman's widow, who climbs the tower twice a night for the rest of her life. The village holds the keepership as a trust and keeps it in its own families through the age.
- <a id="ev-EV-2003"></a>**30 am Màrt, AE 16** — *Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). Anna nic Dhòmhnaill, keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, who cannot write, begins her count on the wall of the tower stair below the lamp-room: one stroke cut with a knife for every night the light is lit, and a stroke across every thirty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0048"><em>Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit</em>, 9 an Cèitean, AE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0049"><em>The first keeper of Tobar dhearg</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0050"></a>**10 an Giblean, AE 16** — *Raiders in the north-western waters* (Spùinneadairean-mara). A Company brig is boarded off the north-west coast and stripped of her cargo of tools. The raiders are never known. The Administration blames the custodians of the coast, and the custodians answer that those waters have always kept their own law.
- <a id="ev-EV-2022"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, AE 16** — *The answer of the coast read in the hills* (Cathair dhearg). The council at Cathair dhearg copies the answer of the custodians of the north-western coast to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir over the stripped brig, that those waters have always kept their own law, and sends it round the districts. It is read out at the mill at Muileann chrom.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0050"><em>Raiders in the north-western waters</em>, 10 an Giblean, AE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2023"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, AE 16** — *Beathag writes the road into the roll of Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). Under the sixteenth year Beathag Dhubh enters in the roll of Doire mhòr the answer of the coast word for word, and then the road round the village's fields, a mile the longer and well built, with two words after it: for now.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0047"><em>The road around Doire mhòr</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0046"><em>Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2024"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 16** — *The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins* (Cnoc bheag). Samuel Wren comes to Cnoc bheag at the hawk-priests' asking and is shown their copy of his grammar, written in along every margin in the stag-letters. Beside his words keepers of the coal they have set the island's word three times, which means those who have the care of the vein.
