Wren copies all their notes by the priest's fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0042"><em>Wren's grammar</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0043"><em>The hawk-priests read Wren</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, AE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0051"></a>**5 an Gearran, AE 17** — *The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Samuel Wren copies the writing on the obelisk near Cnoc bheag and sends it over the sea to the scholars of an Tìr Thall. No answer comes. The custodians tell him the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich and that none living can read it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2024"><em>The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2025"></a>**10 an Gearran, AE 17** — *The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). At Carragh Cnoc bheag the custodian of the town tells Samuel Wren what her house has told every asker: the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich, the old schools' letters matched nothing on it, and the four words below were cut later by one who could read no more of it. Wren copies the line three times in the rain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0051"><em>The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied</em>, 5 an Gearran, AE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2024"><em>The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0052"></a>**13 an Gearran, AE 17** — *The first coin*. The humans' coin is brought in beside the old barter, for ease, it is said. Within ten years nothing that needs a tool from over the sea can be had for anything else.
- <a id="ev-EV-2026"></a>**22 am Màrt, AE 17** — *Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). At Josiah Pell's asking Samuel Wren says a prayer over the new striking-press in its shed on the quay at Ros dhomhain, in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris for the fishers watching at the door. The first mark is lifted from the die with tongs and dropped ringing in the tray.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2025"><em>The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes</em>, 10 an Gearran, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0053"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, AE 17** — *The mark and its hundred pence* (Ros dhomhain). The coins are struck at Ros dhomhain from silver and copper shipped from an Tìr Thall: the mark and its hundred pence. The first striking bears a ship on one face, and nothing of Dia-thìr on either.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2026"><em>Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2027"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 17** — *Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft* (Cathair dhearg). Samuel Wren brings one of the first marks to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair in the long room of the council hall. Her niece Muireall takes a rubbing of both faces, writes beneath it that the island is on neither face, and the rubbing goes east that autumn with the season's copies to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0053"><em>The mark and its hundred pence</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, AE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2026"><em>Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0054"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, AE 18** — *Cathair mhòr refuses the mark* (Cathair mhòr). The market of Cathair mhòr, greatest below the hills east of the capital, refuses the humans' coin for a whole year. The custodians of the town give way when the Company's tool-sellers will not cross their bridge.
- <a id="ev-IV-0055"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, AE 18** — *Two books at the capital market* (Cathair dhearg). At the market of Cathair dhearg the tool-sellers take only marks, while cloth and fish still go by barter. The custodians' clerks begin to keep two sets of books, and complain of it in both.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2027"><em>Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2028"></a>**21 am Màrt, AE 18** — *The market-clerk's sentence in both books* (Cathair dhearg). Tadhg, the custodians' market-clerk at Cathair dhearg, keeps the dues of barter in one book and the dues in marks in another, and can make no single figure of them for the council. At the foot of each he writes that the one book cannot be added to the other, in the stag-letters and again in the humans' tongue.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0055"><em>Two books at the capital market</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2027"><em>Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2029"></a>**15 an Cèitean, AE 18** — *The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren* (Dùn thais). The masters of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh at Dùn thais write to Samuel Wren at Ros dhomhain, in the stag-letters, asking him to come for the dark of the year and dispute with them. He goes east with the carriers at the end of an t-Samhain, five days on the road through Cathair mhòr and the hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2028"><em>The market-clerk's sentence in both books</em>, 21 am Màrt, AE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0056"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 18** — *Wren's winter at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). The masters of the druid school at Dùn thais receive Samuel Wren for a winter of disputation. He asks them why the vein should be holy; they ask him why his fuel should be burned. Neither telling of that winter names a winner.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2029"><em>The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren</em>, 15 an Cèitean, AE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2004"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 18** — *Wren's letter home on the druids* (Dùn thais). From Dùn thais, in the last days of the year, Samuel Wren writes to the house of his order over the sea by the packet of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. He sets down a tale the eldest master told at the hearth of a holy man's voyage west in a boat of hides, very like the voyage of Naomh Breandan as an Eaglais tells it, told from the other shore.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0056"><em>Wren's winter at Dùn thais</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0057"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 19** — *Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Company masons rebuild in dressed stone the old bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg, wide enough for coal-carts to pass two abreast.
- <a id="ev-EV-2030"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, AE 19** — *Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). When the masons of A' Chompanaidh take down the parapets of Drochaid Cathair dhearg, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks the master mason to keep the block cut with Queen Sìleas's name. He has it dressed on its back and sides, its face left as it was, and sets it again in the new downstream parapet near the middle of the bridge.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0057"><em>Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0057a"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, AE 19** — *The Commissioner's carriage* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Company wheelwrights build a closed carriage for Josiah Pell, and he drives in it over the new bridge from the Residency to the council at Cathair dhearg. It is the first carriage on the island. The custodians still walk to the council, and say so.
- <a id="ev-EV-2031"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, AE 19** — *Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). Josiah Pell's carriage stops beside Tormod mac Ailein and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair on the new bridge, and Pell offers Ceann a' Chùraim a seat as far as the council hall. Tormod thanks him and answers aloud that they will walk, and the two custodians come up the hill on foot long after the carriage.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0057a"><em>The Commissioner's carriage</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, AE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2030"><em>Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2032"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, AE 19** — *Gormshuil reads the harbour articles to the council* (Cathair dhearg). Before the signing of Puingean a' Chalaidh, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads the eight sheets aloud to the council at Cathair dhearg, each clause first in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas asks to hear the clause on the anchorages twice.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2031"><em>Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0058"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, AE 19** — *The Harbour Articles* (Ros dhomhain). A second compact, the Harbour Articles, fixes the dues and anchorages of Ros dhomhain in the Company's favour. Like the first treaty it is written in the humans' tongue only, and this time two custodians refuse to sign.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2032"><em>Gormshuil reads the harbour articles to the council</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2005"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 19** — *Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh* (Cathair dhearg). Gormshuil nic Fhearchair passes the sheet of Puingean a' Chalaidh on unsigned, and tells Josiah Pell in his own tongue that she will not put her name under what she has read. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas refuses with her. The council's roll names the two, the first custodians to refuse a writing of the strangers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0058"><em>The Harbour Articles</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0059"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, AE 20** — *The fishermen of Baile ghlas* (Baile ghlas). The fishermen of Baile ghlas, whose boats had anchored free at Ros dhomhain time out of mind, are charged anchorage under the Harbour Articles. They take their catch to their own small harbour and sell it there to anyone but the Company.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2005"><em>Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0060"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, AE 20** — *The northern concession* (Muileann àrsaidh). The council grants the Administration upland pasture in the north-west about Muileann àrsaidh, for human families who will not work in the pits. The grant is for grazing; the families build houses of stone.
- <a id="ev-EV-2033"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20** — *The council's letter on the grazing* (Cathair dhearg). At Tormod mac Ailein's sickbed Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads him the letter from Muileann àrsaidh. At his word she writes to the families on the grazing, in both tongues, that the council granted summer grazing and shielings, and sends it north the next morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0060"><em>The northern concession</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, AE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2005"><em>Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0061"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20** — *Death of Tormod mac Ailein* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod mac Ailein, the high custodian who signed the first treaty, dies at Cathair dhearg. The council chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh after him, who had never met a human before the Crossing and has dealt with little else since.
- <a id="ev-EV-2006"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20** — *Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Six custodians carry Tormod mac Ailein to the ground behind the council hall, with the bells of the capital ringing, and the mourners lay their stones on the grave going round sunwise. Josiah Pell walks up from the bridge-foot bareheaded to stand at the edge of the ground. Samuel Wren stands at the gate.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0061"><em>Death of Tormod mac Ailein</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2034"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20** — *Tormod mac Ailein waked three nights* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod mac Ailein is waked three nights in his house below the temple at Cathair dhearg, by the old custom. On the second night the council, meeting below, chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh in a single evening, and the roll enters the choice as unanimous.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0061"><em>Death of Tormod mac Ailein</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2006"><em>Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 21 – 30

- <a id="ev-IV-0062"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, AE 21** — *Harrow lost at sea* (Muir Mhanannain). Edmund Harrow's ship does not come back from the crossing. The Company passes wholly into Thomas Pike's hands, and the humans' letter-books mourn Harrow as the man who found Dia-thìr.
- <a id="ev-EV-2035"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, AE 21** — *Harrow's name read in the chapel at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A' Chompanaidh's men at Ros dhomhain give up Harrow's ship a month past her day. The chapel bell is rung slowly, the flag over the warehouse is lowered to half its pole, and Thomas Pike reads Harrow's name and the names of his crew at the humans' prayers, with Samuel Wren's help.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0062"><em>Harrow lost at sea</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2036"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, AE 21** — *Pike's letter to the council* (Cathair dhearg). The humans' clerks write to the council at Cathair dhearg, in their own tongue and under seal, that A' Chompanaidh has passed wholly to Thomas Pike. Coinneach Glas reads the letter to the sitting and it is entered in the roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0062"><em>Harrow lost at sea</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0061"><em>Death of Tormod mac Ailein</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2035"><em>Harrow's name read in the chapel at Ros dhomhain</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2037"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, AE 21** — *The counters' fee held over* (Cathair dhearg). At its autumn sitting the council, its share of the vein-dues now paid in marks by A' Chompanaidh and fewer than before, finds it cannot meet every fee. The fee of the counters who keep the boards of the measured handful is held over to the next sitting.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <em>The Small-Burning Law</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0027">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 142</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2036"><em>Pike's letter to the council</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2038"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, AE 21** — *Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board* (Dùn dhearg). At Samhain only the old households of Dùn dhearg bring their sacks to the counters' board in the old granary. The young households have bought their coal by the sack at the market of Cathair mhòr off A' Chompanaidh's carts. Pàdraig Cam counts the season without a fee.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0052"><em>The first coin</em>, 13 an Gearran, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0063"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21** — *The Small-Burning Law lapses*. Centuries of measured burning end within one generation. The Law is never repealed; once its keeping no longer pays, it is no longer kept.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2037"><em>The counters' fee held over</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, AE 21</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2038"><em>Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0064"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21** — *The last count at Doire mhin* (Doire mhin). The custodians of Doire mhin keep the old count of the Small-Burning Law, the measure of coal that might be burned in a year, one season longer than any others. They enter it in their roll with the note that no one asked for it.
- <a id="ev-EV-2039"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21** — *The counter of Dùn dhearg dies* (Dùn dhearg). Pàdraig Cam, counter of Dùn dhearg for forty years, dies in an Gearran. His son is at the pits of Muileann chrom and does not take the board, which hangs in the old granary with the pegs of the last Samhain in their holes. Fionnghal nic Artair begins her letter to the council.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0063"><em>The Small-Burning Law lapses</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2038"><em>Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0065"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22** — *A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Fionnghal nic Artair, a custodian of Dùn dhearg, writes to the council in defence of the Small-Burning Law, the only such defence that survives. She holds that the Law was never for the coal's sake but for the people, who would become whatever the burning made them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2039"><em>The counter of Dùn dhearg dies</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2007"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22** — *The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Fionnghal nic Artair reads her letter standing to the council at Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas thanks her and bids it kept with the rolls, and the roll enters it as read and filed. The same sitting grants Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir leave to widen the road to Muileann chrom for the coal-carts.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0063"><em>The Small-Burning Law lapses</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2040"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, AE 22** — *Fionnghal nic Artair rides to Cathair dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). In an t-Ògmhios Fionnghal nic Artair rides west from Dùn dhearg with her letter in defence of Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig sewn in calfskin. She lodges at Doire mhin, where the custodian Anndra mac Eòin shows her the last count of the valley, and reads him the letter by his lamp.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0064"><em>The last count at Doire mhin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2007"><em>The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2041"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, AE 22** — *A fair copy of the defence for the loft* (Cathair dhearg). At Gormshuil nic Fhearchair's asking Fionnghal nic Artair makes a fair copy of her letter in her own hand. Muireall nic Fhearchair sends it to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, where the custodians' papers are kept dry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2040"><em>Fionnghal nic Artair rides to Cathair dhearg</em>, 26 an t-Iuchar, AE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0066"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, AE 22** — *Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Murchadh Seabhag preaches that Mòd, the Hungry Hawk of Acaill, starves those who eat faster than the land can feed them. The sermon is copied and carried to the camps, and it is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich that the Company's agents are told to seize.
- <a id="ev-EV-2042"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, AE 22** — *The hawk sermon carried south in the bird-bags* (Seann Skell). A scribe of the hawk-shrine at Seann Skell writes Murchadh Seabhag's sermon down from his mouth. Fowlers taking birds to the autumn markets carry copies south, and from the markets carters and pedlars bring them into the camps of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, where readers are given their supper to read them aloud.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0066"><em>Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, AE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0067"></a>**16 am Màrt, AE 23** — *The hearths of Achadh naomh* (Achadh naomh). The households of Achadh naomh, in the hills north of the workings, who keep Na Seann Spioradan, will not light their hearths with coal bought of the Company. They burn peat as their grandparents did, and their elders teach that coal burned for wages is burned without the ancestors' leave.
- <a id="ev-EV-2008"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 23** — *A' Chompanaidh's agents seize the hawk sermon in the camps* (Muileann chrom). A' Chompanaidh's agents at Muileann chrom go from hut to hut through the crews' camp with a basket and take every copy of Murchadh Seabhag's sermon they find, eleven in one morning. One woman burns her copy on her hearth before them, and her name is written down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0066"><em>Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, AE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2043"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, AE 23** — *Fionnghal nic Artair at the hearths of Achadh naomh* (Achadh naomh). Bidden by the elders of Achadh naomh, Fionnghal nic Artair rides north through the hills in an Giblean and reads her letter at the hearth of Sìleas nic Uilleim to the whole village. Asked what burns on her own hearth, she answers bought coal. She is sent home with a creel of peats.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0067"><em>The hearths of Achadh naomh</em>, 16 am Màrt, AE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2044"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 23** — *The custodians at the pump-house of Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Three custodians sent by Coinneach Glas, Fionnghal nic Artair among them, go down to Muileann chrom to ask that the tally of the hill be kept. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill takes them to the pump at the deep gallery, where the furnaces are fed by the cartload.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0064"><em>The last count at Doire mhin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2043"><em>Fionnghal nic Artair at the hearths of Achadh naomh</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0068"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, AE 23** — *Burning by the cartload* (Muileann chrom). The Company's furnaces at Muileann chrom burn coal by the cartload to drive the new pumps, and no heed is paid to the custodians' tally of what the hill may give in a year. Coinneach Glas's council asks that the tally be kept, and is sent a copy of the Company's accounts.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2044"><em>The custodians at the pump-house of Muileann chrom</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2045"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, AE 23** — *A' Chompanaidh's accounts filed beside the defence* (Cathair dhearg). The copy of A' Chompanaidh's half-year accounts, sent in answer to the council's asking, is read aloud in its totals by Coinneach Glas and laid in the press of the council hall on the shelf that holds the letter of the custodian of Dùn dhearg.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0068"><em>Burning by the cartload</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, AE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2044"><em>The custodians at the pump-house of Muileann chrom</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0069"></a>**15 an Gearran, AE 24** — *Henry Maddox Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Josiah Pell sails home to an Tìr Thall and does not return. After him comes Henry Maddox, bidden to double the yield, with a letter from the Company promising him a share of it.
- <a id="ev-EV-2046"></a>**1 am Màrt, AE 24** — *Maddox greets the council* (Cathair dhearg). Henry Maddox comes before the council at Cathair dhearg in An t-Àrd-mhaor's carriage, greets each custodian in Dia-thìris learned on the ship, and tells them his orders are to double the yield of the pits. He does not speak of A' Chompanaidh's letter promising him a share of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0069"><em>Henry Maddox Commissioner</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0057a"><em>The Commissioner's carriage</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, AE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2045"><em>A' Chompanaidh's accounts filed beside the defence</em>, 17 an t-Samhain, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0070"></a>**12 am Màrt, AE 24** — *The oaks of Cathair fhada* (Cathair fhada). Maddox buys the oak woods about Cathair fhada for pit-props. The town had cut them sparingly for generations; they are gone within the working lives of the men who fell them.
- <a id="ev-EV-2009"></a>**4 an Giblean, AE 24** — *The last oak of Cathair fhada's own cutting* (Cathair fhada). Before A' Chompanaidh's fellers come, the woodreeve of Cathair fhada and his men fell with axes the one oak the spring lot had fallen on, as the town had cut since An Aois Naomh, and plant six acorns in the ring of its roots. The fellers begin with long saws on the morning after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0070"><em>The oaks of Cathair fhada</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2047"></a>**20 an Giblean, AE 24** — *The woodreeve of Cathair fhada before the council* (Cathair fhada). Eòghann mac Phàdraig, woodreeve of Cathair fhada, asks the council to undo the sale of the town's oak woods to Maddox. The council holds that the custodians of Cathair fhada, in debt to A' Chompanaidh's store for seed, had the right to sell, and the clerk enters it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0070"><em>The oaks of Cathair fhada</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2048"></a>**13 an t-Ògmhios, AE 24** — *The custodian of Dùn dhearg goes back to peat* (Dùn dhearg). Home from Cathair fhada in am Màrt, Fionnghal nic Artair has the coal raked out of her grate and lights it again with the peats of Achadh naomh. She sends to find a man of Dùn dhearg who still knows how to cut peat, and pays him what he asks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0065"><em>A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0067"><em>The hearths of Achadh naomh</em>, 16 am Màrt, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2049"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, AE 24** — *The heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich driven without props* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). Under Henry Maddox's order to double the yield, the new gallery at Cnoc fhiadhaich is driven north along the seam on the pay of the ton, and the oak props from Cathair fhada stop at the head of the carters' drift. The agent of A' Chompanaidh writes that the heading will be timbered when the yield allows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0069"><em>Henry Maddox Commissioner</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0070"><em>The oaks of Cathair fhada</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0071"></a>**26 an Giblean, AE 25** — *The first deaths of haste*. A tunnel worked faster than any Dia-thìreach crew would have worked it falls in and kills eleven. It is entered as an accident.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2049"><em>The heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich driven without props</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2501"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 25** — *The eleven buried at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The eleven dead of the fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich are buried in the ground above the mill at Muileann chrom on the fourth day after the fall. Marsaili nic Sheumais, keeper of the old cutting for Taigh na Fèithe, reads their names at the graves and writes each into the roll with father, mother and hearth, and the place as under the wild hill.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0071"><em>The first deaths of haste</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2510"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, AE 25** — *Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). When the eleven are brought out of the fallen heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich, Dòmhnall, an old hewer of the custodians' cutting and father of Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, says the words of the face at the mouth of the drift, and the old hewers take them up. They had not been said at that pit-mouth since it was opened.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0071"><em>The first deaths of haste</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2501"><em>The eleven buried at Muileann chrom</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2511"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, AE 25** — *The fallen heading cleared and timbered* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich is cleared by midsummer and the heading timbered pair by pair as it is cleared, with oak brought up from Cathair fhada in an t-Ògmhios. The crews are paid nothing for the days of digging, and the yield of the year is short.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0071"><em>The first deaths of haste</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2510"><em>Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth</em>, 2 an t-Iuchar, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0072"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, AE 25** — *The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The fall was at Cnoc fhiadhaich, in a gallery driven forward without the timbering the Dia-thìrich crews had asked for. The custodians' roll names all eleven dead. The Company's report names none, and calls the gallery "unsound ground."<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2501"><em>The eleven buried at Muileann chrom</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 25</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2510"><em>Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth</em>, 2 an t-Iuchar, AE 25</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2511"><em>The fallen heading cleared and timbered</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2512"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, AE 25** — *Raghnall asks three times for timber at the heading* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). Between an Gearran and an Giblean the crew-leaders Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill and Ailean mac Dhùghaill ask the agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich three times for props over the heading, where the shale roof has turned the colour the hewers read as bad ground. The agent writes the asking in his book and answers that oak will come in the summer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0071"><em>The first deaths of haste</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2511"><em>The fallen heading cleared and timbered</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0073"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 26** — *The coughing sickness* (Muileann chrom). A dry cough runs through the camps at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, worst among the boys who break coal at the pit-mouth, and thirty-eight die of it. The Mission's surgeon calls it a winter complaint. It lasts through the summer.
- <a id="ev-EV-2502"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, AE 26** — *Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth* (Muileann chrom). Dòmhnall, the six-year-old son of the crew-leader Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who had gone to the breakers' benches at Muileann chrom in the autumn, takes An Casad Tioram in am Màrt. He coughs nine nights on his father's knee and wakes well on the tenth morning, and goes back to the benches in the autumn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0073"><em>The coughing sickness</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2513"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, AE 26** — *The custodians ask that the breakers' benches be shut* (Muileann chrom). With An Casad Tioram running through the summer among the children who break coal, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe ask the agent of A' Chompanaidh to shut the benches at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich until it has passed. He writes the asking in his book, and the benches stay open to feed the pump furnaces.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0073"><em>The coughing sickness</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 26</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0068"><em>Burning by the cartload</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, AE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2514"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, AE 26** — *The hill crews go home to the harvest* (Muileann chrom). At the harvests after the fall and after An Casad Tioram the crews of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich go home to their oats, a third of them the first year and half the second, and many stay home through the autumn. The yield of A' Chompanaidh in the hills falls short three years together.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0069"><em>Henry Maddox Commissioner</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0073"><em>The coughing sickness</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0074"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, AE 27** — *The orphans of Cill thais* (Cill thais). The village of Cill thais takes in the children orphaned by the coughing sickness and keeps a house for them at its own custodians' cost. The Company, asked to give toward it, sends a crate of Mission primers.
- <a id="ev-EV-2515"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, AE 27** — *The orphans carried to Cill thais* (Muileann chrom). In an t-Iuchar Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill drives fourteen orphans of the fall and An Casad Tioram in a borrowed cart from Muileann chrom to Cill thais, two days west, with the crate of primers sent by A' Chompanaidh. The warden of Cill thais lifts each child down, has their names written, and sets the crate on a shelf of Taigh nan Dìlleachdan.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0074"><em>The orphans of Cill thais</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, AE 27</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0073"><em>The coughing sickness</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 26</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0071"><em>The first deaths of haste</em>, 26 an Giblean, AE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2516"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, AE 27** — *Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal* (Baile ìseal). The lime for the mortar of the tower at Baile ìseal is burned in a kiln on the shore with coal carted over the hills from Muileann chrom. The tower is built by the masons of the eastern coast of the grey stone of the cape, with a lamp sent by A' Chompanaidh.
- <a id="ev-IV-0075"></a>**4 an Lùnastal, AE 27** — *Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The second beacon is lit on the eastern shore at Baile ìseal. Torcall Clachair, now too old to climb, directs its building from a chair at the foot of the headland.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2516"><em>Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal</em>, 30 an t-Iuchar, AE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2517"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 27** — *The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches* (Baile ìseal). At the custodians' asking, the keeping of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal is given to the fishing households that had kept the driftwood fire on the cape. They draw lots for the watches at Samhain as they had drawn them for the fire, and the old fire is still lit beside the tower.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0075"><em>Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit</em>, 4 an Lùnastal, AE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0076"></a>**9 an Cèitean, AE 28** — *The keepers of Baile ìseal* (Baile ìseal). The keepers of the eastern beacon are drawn from the fishing families of Baile ìseal. The town's custodians ask for a rule, and get it, that the lamp be lowered on the nights the boats go out to the deep grounds, lest the fish take fright. When the rule lapsed no one wrote down.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2517"><em>The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2503"></a>**19 an Cèitean, AE 28** — *Torcall Clachair's last cairn* (Baile ìseal). Going home west from Baile ìseal in the spring after the lighting, Torcall Clachair has his cart stopped where the road tops the first rise of the moor and the tower first shows over the heather. Seated by the road, he lays a small cairn with his own hands from stones a boy brings from the ditch. He builds no more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0075"><em>Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit</em>, 4 an Lùnastal, AE 27</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0076"><em>The keepers of Baile ìseal</em>, 9 an Cèitean, AE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0076a"></a>**23 an Giblean, AE 29** — *Seòlaid Ceann òg* (Ceann òg). The traders' boats from the new quay at Ceann òg go down the Abhainn ìseal past Cnoc bheag and Inis bhàn to the north coast, west along it, round the western capes, and south past Inis thais into the capital's water. Their lane is called Seòlaid Ceann òg after the quay. Off the north-west it swings far out into the open sea, and there the ships bound for an Tìr Thall leave it for the passage north-about, and the ships coming down from the north come in.
- <a id="ev-EV-2518"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 29** — *Raghnall takes the leader's share* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a leader's share on every ton his three crews raise, paid to him alone, if he keeps them at the face through harvest and winter; otherwise men of the coast will be brought up. Raghnall puts his mark to the paper in an Cèitean and keeps his crews below through the harvest.
- <a id="ev-EV-2519"></a>**17 an Lùnastal, AE 29** — *Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg* (Ceann òg). In the autumn A' Chompanaidh gathers fishers and net-menders whose foreshores it has bought, ships them from the capital's quays in the traders' boats of Seòlaid Ceann òg round the western capes and up the Abhainn ìseal to Ceann òg, and walks them over the hills to the workings in companies of twenty with their families.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0076a"><em>Seòlaid Ceann òg</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0077"></a>**6 an Dàmhair, AE 29** — *The camp at Àth ìseal* (Àth ìseal). The Company builds a camp of timber huts at Àth ìseal, at the ford below the new workings, for crews brought in from the coast. It is the first settlement on Dia-thìr made for nothing but the pit.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2518"><em>Raghnall takes the leader's share</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 29</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2519"><em>Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg</em>, 17 an Lùnastal, AE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2520"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 29** — *The first crews in the huts at Àth ìseal* (Àth ìseal). The first companies from the coast move into the plank huts at Àth ìseal, three long huts with a stove in each, a store and a well, with more rows pegged out beyond. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe notes that the camp has no custodian and has asked for none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0077"><em>The camp at Àth ìseal</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, AE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0078"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30** — *Doire mhòr's water taken* (Doire mhòr). The Company turns the stream that watered Doire mhòr to wash coal at Cnoc fhiadhaich. No order is written; the stream is dammed one season and not let go. Beathag Dhubh's people carry water by hand for two summers, and then begin to leave.
- <a id="ev-EV-2521"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, AE 30** — *Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, goes down to the washing-floors at Cnoc fhiadhaich with the carter Seònaid Bhàn and asks the agent Amos Tanner to show her the order that took her village's stream. He has none. The washing needs water, he says, and the stream goes with the working; a complaint may be written and sent on to Ros dhomhain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0078"><em>Doire mhòr's water taken</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2522"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, AE 30** — *Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring* (Doire mhòr). With the stream penned behind the washing gang's bank, the households of Doire mhòr carry their water by yoke and pail from the cattle spring at the foot of the brae, the better part of a mile each way. Beathag Dhubh's roll names every household that carries, and among the carriers is Tormod, son of Ruairidh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0078"><em>Doire mhòr's water taken</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2521"><em>Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2523"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, AE 30** — *Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered* (Doire mhòr). The custodian of Doire mhòr writes to Comhairle a' Chùraim at Cathair dhearg of the taking of Doire mhòr's stream. Seònaid Bhàn carries the letter down the road in her cart and puts it into the hand of a custodians' clerk. The council enters it in its roll, and the stream is not let go that season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0078"><em>Doire mhòr's water taken</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2522"><em>Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring</em>, 9 an Lùnastal, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0079"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, AE 30** — *The short hunger in the hills* (Muileann chrom). The men drawn from the farms into the pits, the hill villages of Muileann chrom lose their oats to rain, with none at home to cut ahead of it. The Company sells meal at the camp stores for marks, and the villages have few.
- <a id="ev-EV-2504"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, AE 30** — *Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol* (Cuan chrom). Muireall nic Fhearchair drives her aunt Gormshuil's papers east in a hired pony-cart to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, away from the reach of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. Held by rain at Cuan chrom, she reads Clàr nan Dà Fhichead Dath aloud to the carter Seònaid Bhàn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0009"><em>Wren's word-lists</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2524"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, AE 30** — *The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter* (Àth ìseal). In the hungry autumn the store of A' Chompanaidh at Àth ìseal sells meal to the hill villages over its counter for marks only. Its clerk refuses cheese, wool and a woman's bronze brooch, having no book for them, and the women of the villages send their men back to the pits for coin.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0079"><em>The short hunger in the hills</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 30</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2504"><em>Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol</em>, 27 an Lùnastal, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2525"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 30** — *The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom* (Cuan chrom). Nine ox-carts of meal from the villages of Doire fhiadhaich, sent north to the hungry hills under Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte, reach the ford at Cuan chrom in the rain of an Dàmhair. The carter of Cuan chrom, Seònaid Bhàn's father, takes their drivers and oxen into his own house and byre for the night.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <em>The first recorded famine averted</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0179">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 2,473</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2524"><em>The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter</em>, 15 an t-Sultain, AE 30</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 31 – 40

- <a id="ev-IV-0080"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, AE 31** — *Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich* (Doire fhiadhaich). The villages of Doire fhiadhaich in the south send carts of meal north to the hill villages, as the old custom of the Holy Age bids in a hungry year. The Company's agents at Àth ìseal buy up two of the carts on the road.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2525"><em>The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2526"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, AE 31** — *Seven carts give their meal at the village doors* (Doire fhiadhaich). Of the nine meal-carts from Doire fhiadhaich, the seven that refuse the agents' marks at Àth ìseal go on into the hills and give their meal away sack by sack at the doors of the hill villages, as Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte bids. Their drivers come home by the carriers' road with empty carts.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0080"><em>Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich</em>, 15 an Dàmhair, AE 31</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The first recorded famine averted</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0179">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 2,473</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0081"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, AE 31** — *The mountain dug by the ton*. For the first time in the history of Dia-thìr the mountain is worked by the ton, and for ends no custom of the Dia-thìrich would have chosen.
- <a id="ev-IV-0082"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 31** — *Rope for the winding-gear* (Dùn chrom). The rope-walks of Dùn chrom, which had made cable for the fishing boats, turn wholly to winding-rope for the pit-heads. The Company pays well, and the town grows by half.
- <a id="ev-EV-2505"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, AE 31** — *Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg in the last days of an t-Sultain, in her seventy-first year. She had kept the council's list of the island's words since the ships came, refused to sign Puingean a' Chalaidh, and learned the humans' letters in her old age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0009"><em>Wren's word-lists</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0010"><em>One word for the coal</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0083"></a>**7 an Giblean, AE 32** — *The Company's second charter* (Ros dhomhain). The Company is chartered again in an Tìr Thall, with new money and a new name the Dia-thìrich never take up. Its agents at Ros dhomhain now outnumber the Administration's own clerks four to one.
- <a id="ev-EV-2527"></a>**9 an Giblean, AE 32** — *The first households leave Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). In the second summer of the carrying the first households of Doire mhòr leave the village. Most go down to the timber huts at Àth ìseal, others to Muileann chrom or the capital. Tormod, who had carried water up for two summers, goes down to Àth ìseal with the rest. Beathag Dhubh stays.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0078"><em>Doire mhòr's water taken</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0077"><em>The camp at Àth ìseal</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, AE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0084"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, AE 32** — *Barges at Cidhe Beag* (Cidhe Beag). Coal barges begin to load at Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine and float the black coal down to the coast. The old canoe landing, used since before the Sundering, is widened with cut stone, and its shrine is moved uphill.
- <a id="ev-EV-2528"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 32** — *The shrine-stone of Cidhe Beag set under a rowan* (Cidhe Beag). When the canoe landing at Cidhe Beag is widened into a coal quay, the old ferryman of the landing chooses a new place for its shrine-stone on the bank above, under a rowan within sight of the water. Four masons carry it up on a hurdle, and the ferryman puts meal in its hollow.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0084"><em>Barges at Cidhe Beag</em>, 16 an t-Sultain, AE 32</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0085"></a>**27 am Faoilleach, AE 33** — *Abhainn uaine silts black* (Abhainn uaine). The washing of coal upstream fills Abhainn uaine with black slurry, and within a few seasons the salmon runs at its mouth fail. The river keeps its name, the green river, and the fishermen speak it bitterly.
- <a id="ev-EV-2529"></a>**18 an Giblean, AE 33** — *The last salmon netted at the green river's mouth* (Ceann leathan). The fishermen of Ceann leathan net the last salmon taken at the mouth of the Abhainn uaine, a small hen fish found empty of eggs. The next spring no fish come in from the sea, the gravel of their spawning grounds lying under the grey slurry from the washing-floors.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0085"><em>Abhainn uaine silts black</em>, 27 am Faoilleach, AE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0086"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, AE 33** — *Baile Mòr dhomhain a barge town* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). As the coal comes down to it from Cidhe Beag, Baile Mòr dhomhain on the river road grows into the busiest barge town of the north. Its people double in number, most of the newcomers bargemen from the coast.
- <a id="ev-EV-2506"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 33** — *Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair* (Cuan chrom). Seònaid Bhàn, carter of Cuan chrom, marries Pàdraig mac Artair, a carter of Doire chaol. They live in her father's house at Cuan chrom beside the roofless carters' house at the quay, and their son Murchadh is born there the next winter.
- <a id="ev-IV-0087"></a>**10 am Faoilleach, AE 34** — *Baile dhomhain raised as a camp town* (Baile dhomhain). A Company surveyor lays out a second camp, Baile dhomhain, on a grid, the first town of the Dia-thìrich drawn on paper before it was built. Within two seasons it houses four hundred.
- <a id="ev-EV-2530"></a>**26 an Cèitean, AE 34** — *Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The custodians of Cuan chrom let the roofless carters' house at their quay to Seònaid Bhàn for a rent of one cheese a year. Twenty carters of Doire chaol give a week's work each towards the new roof for a year's lodging at half price, and its timber comes up from Doire fhiadhaich.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <em>The house at the middle of the road</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0037">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 172</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2506"><em>Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0088"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, AE 34** — *An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The old carters' house at the half-way stage of the coal road between the capital and the hills is built again, opens its doors at Lùnastal, and keeps the name An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. Its first keeper, Seònaid Bhàn, takes both marks and barter, the only innkeeper on the road who will.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2506"><em>Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 33</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2530"><em>Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2531"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, AE 34** — *Seònaid's rule of marks and barter* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). On the first night of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr Seònaid Bhàn takes a hill carter's cheese and fleece for his bed and supper at the same rate as marks. She has the rule cut on a board over the eastern hearth in the old strokes: Bonn no bathar, an aon bhobhla, coin or goods, the same bowl.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0088"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, AE 34</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2530"><em>Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0088a"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 34** — *Rathad na Mèinne* (Àth chiar). The Company's road-gangs finish metalling the carriers' road from Cathair dhearg by Doire chaol and the ford of Àth chiar to the workings at Achadh dhomhain, wide enough for coal-carts to pass both ways. The carters call it Rathad na Mèinne, the mine road. The posts with the crown's sign that had marked it since the Age of Sundering are left standing along it.
- <a id="ev-EV-2532"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 34** — *The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Through the winter some thirty carters of Doire chaol, Cuan chrom and the capital meet at the eastern hearth of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr over the lowered rate for hauling coal. On Pàdraig mac Artair's counsel they swear, with their hands on the board of Seònaid's rule, to go to Ros dhomhain together and haul nothing at the new rate.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2531"><em>Seònaid's rule of marks and barter</em>, 18 an Lùnastal, AE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0089"></a>**20 an Giblean, AE 35** — *The carters of Doire chaol* (Doire chaol). The carters of Doire chaol, on the road just east of the capital, band together in a guild to bargain with the Company over the rates for hauling coal. It is the first Dia-thìreach guild of the age, and the Company owns it because that is cheaper than breaking it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2532"><em>The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0090"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, AE 35** — *Seann Toll made a coal landing* (Seann Toll). The Company takes the river landing at Seann Toll, below the workings, and builds a loading stage there for the barges that carry the coal down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan. The town's fishing boats are moved to the next reach.
- <a id="ev-EV-2533"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, AE 35** — *Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Amos Tanner, agent of A' Chompanaidh for the carriage of coal, rides up Rathad na Mèinne to meet the carters' guild of Doire chaol at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. He tells them of the new coal stage at Seann Toll and the lesser hauling on the road, and they bargain over the rate into the night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0089"><em>The carters of Doire chaol</em>, 20 an Giblean, AE 35</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0090"><em>Seann Toll made a coal landing</em>, 3 an t-Iuchar, AE 35</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2532"><em>The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0090a"></a>**31 am Faoilleach, AE 36** — *The coal ships' lane* (Ceann leathan). From the landing at Seann Toll the coal barges go down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan, where the Company's ships load at the river mouth and go out by the southern lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, west along the south coast to the wild strait and the open sea. The fishers of the south coast, who had used the lane for five hundred years, learn to keep out of the coal ships' way.
- <a id="ev-EV-2534"></a>**6 an Giblean, AE 36** — *A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat* (Ceann leathan). A coal ship of A' Chompanaidh coming out of the river mouth on the ebb runs down a fishing boat of Ceann leathan off the bar and does not stop. The two men aboard are taken from the water alive by their neighbours. Within a season the town's boats keep inshore of the ships' track and lie to at the bar when a hull comes down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0090"><em>Seann Toll made a coal landing</em>, 3 an t-Iuchar, AE 35</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0090a"><em>The coal ships' lane</em>, 31 am Faoilleach, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2535"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 36** — *Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff* (Muileann chrom). In an Cèitean Enoch Pratt, agent of A' Chompanaidh at the pits of Muileann chrom, offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a staff of ash capped with brass, a weekly wage in marks and a house, to be set over all the crews of the hill and answer for them to the agent. Raghnall, forty-six years old, takes it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0091"></a>**19 an Cèitean, AE 36** — *The first Dia-thìreach overseer*. A Dia-thìreach is set over other Dia-thìrich miners, answerable to human masters. It is the first open crack within the Dia-thìrich themselves, and not only between them and the humans.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2535"><em>Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff</em>, 25 an Giblean, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0092"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 36** — *Raghnall Maor* (Muileann chrom). The first overseer is Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom, a crew-leader who had worked the pits since the first contract. He is given the Company's staff and a house with a slate roof, and from the office the Dia-thìrich give him his byname: Raghnall Maor, Raghnall the steward.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2535"><em>Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff</em>, 25 an Giblean, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2507"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 36** — *Raghnall's slate-roofed house* (Muileann chrom). A' Chompanaidh's masons from Ros dhomhain build Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a house of two rooms and a loft on common grazing above the mill at Muileann chrom, with glass windows and a roof of slate, the first slate roof in the town. The miller's wife names him Raghnall Maor as he goes by, and the crews take up the name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0092"><em>Raghnall Maor</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2536"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, AE 36** — *The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers* (Muileann chrom). Marsaili nic Sheumais, who keeps the roll of Taigh na Fèithe, enters the first four overseers of the hill by name, then puts the matter to the custodians of the vein. From then on the roll gives only their number under the date, seven in the first year, and says of them only that several are hawk-faithful.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2507"><em>Raghnall's slate-roofed house</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0093"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, AE 37** — *The overseers multiply* (Muileann chrom). Within a few years there are overseers at every working in the district, all Dia-thìrich, all answerable to the Company's agents. The custodians' roll no longer names them, and gives only their number.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2536"><em>The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2537"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, AE 37** — *Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr* (Cnoc mhòr). When A' Chompanaidh opens new pits at Cnoc mhòr and asks for an overseer, Raghnall Maor gives the name of Seumas Dubh, who came into his crews at fifteen. Seumas takes the staff and goes south with his household to a crew of Cnoc mhòr men new to the seam, and runs the haulage three tubs to the rope.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0093"><em>The overseers multiply</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 37</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2536"><em>The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2538"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 37** — *Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage* (Cnoc mhòr). The haulage rope at Cnoc mhòr parts under three full tubs, and the tubs run back into the gallery-mouth and crush Coinneach Beag, a boy of eleven coming up the rails with an empty. The custodians' roll of Cnoc mhòr gives his name, his age and his mother's name; A' Chompanaidh's report gives the cost of the rope.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2537"><em>Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, AE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0094"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, AE 38** — *Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr* (Cnoc mhòr). Seumas Dubh, overseer of the new pits at Cnoc mhòr, is killed by his own crew after a boy is crushed on a haulage he had ordered hurried. The Company hangs two men at Ros dhomhain, the first hanging done by the Administration on Dia-thìr.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2537"><em>Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, AE 37</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2538"><em>Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2508"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, AE 38** — *The two hanged named in the custodians' roll* (Cnoc mhòr). The roll of Cnoc mhòr names the two hewers hanged at Ros dhomhain for the killing of Seumas Dubh, Eòin Ruadh and Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, and records that their neighbours carried them home and buried them in the town's ground. The letter-book of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir gives them as two of the crew.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0094"><em>Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, AE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2539"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, AE 38** — *The overseers made to stand at the hanging* (Ros dhomhain). By Henry Maddox's order every overseer of the island stands in a row in front of the crowd at the hanging at Ros dhomhain, fourteen men with their staffs, inside a square of the soldiers of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The custodians' roll of Ros dhomhain enters in a line of its own that the overseers stood in front.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0094"><em>Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, AE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2540"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, AE 38** — *A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Riding home from the hanging, an overseer of Àth ìseal leaves his staff against the wall of Seònaid Bhàn's house at the half-way stage of Rathad na Mèinne, and in the morning it is gone. He tells the agent it is lost, and A' Chompanaidh gives him another.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0088"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, AE 34</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0094"><em>Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, AE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0095"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, AE 38** — *Hawk-priests barred from the camps* (Muileann chrom). Henry Maddox bars the priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig from the camps, for their preaching slows the work. The overseers enforce the order, though several of them are hawk-faithful, as the roll says. The Mission's chaplains, who keep a chapel in every camp, are not barred.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2536"><em>The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2541"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 38** — *The sermon in the road at Àth ìseal* (Àth ìseal). Turned back at the gate of the camp at Àth ìseal under Maddox's order by the hawk-faithful overseer Iomhar Bàn, an old priest of Òrd an t-Seabhaig sits down in the road outside the fence, and the crews come out to hear him there. When he is done Iomhar kneels in the road for his blessing. Raghnall Maor stands by.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0095"><em>Hawk-priests barred from the camps</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0096"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, AE 39** — *The pox at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A spotted pox comes ashore at Ros dhomhain on a Company ship and climbs the coal road into the camps. The Mission counts four hundred and six dead. The custodians count more, and write the difference in the margin of the Mission's list.
- <a id="ev-EV-2542"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, AE 39** — *The pox dead of the hill buried below Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). A' Bhreac Bhallach comes up Rathad na Mèinne into the camps of the hill in the last days of an Dàmhair, worst at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain. A' Chompanaidh keeps the pits working. The custodians will not let the pox dead lie among the old graves, and the crews bury them by lamplight in new ground below Achadh dhomhain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0096"><em>The pox at Ros dhomhain</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, AE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2543"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, AE 39** — *The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin* (Muileann chrom). Marsaili nic Sheumais goes from hearth to hearth on the hill in the spring and writes down the pox dead the chaplains had not found. The custodians borrow the chaplains' list, write their own names down both margins in the old letters with the total at the foot, and send it back to Ros dhomhain, where it is filed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0096"><em>The pox at Ros dhomhain</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, AE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0097"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, AE 40** — *The pox in the south* (Baile chiar). The pox spreads south from the harbour to Baile chiar and the villages about it. The custodians there cut the names of the dead into the stone lintel of the council house, and they can still be read.

## The Years AE 41 – 50

- <a id="ev-IV-0098"></a>**31 am Faoilleach, AE 41** — *Baile dhìreach loses its harbour dues* (Baile dhìreach). The Administration moves its customs house from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and ends the sharing of the harbour dues. The mixed council, left with half an income, cuts its members from six to four.
- <a id="ev-EV-2544"></a>**27 an Cèitean, AE 41** — *The hill buries Beathag Dhubh* (Doire mhòr). Some hundreds come up to Doire mhòr for Beathag Dhubh's burying, crews from the galleries unwashed among them, leaving A' Chompanaidh's cart-road at the bend to cross her fields by the old path. Raghnall Maor comes without his staff and stands at the back. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe writes her the last door of Doire mhòr that did not open.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0046"><em>Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-2543"><em>The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, AE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2545"></a>**17 an t-Iuchar, AE 41** — *Maddox's goods carried down to the ships* (Ros dhomhain). For a week A' Chompanaidh's carts go down Rathad na Mèinne to Ros dhomhain with Henry Maddox's goods, a tall clock lashed upright in a cart of its own among them, and all go aboard the ship that brought Arthur Lisle. The carters say that he came out with one chest.
- <a id="ev-IV-0099"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, AE 41** — *Arthur Lisle Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Henry Maddox leaves Dia-thìr a rich man. Arthur Lisle, a lawyer, comes after him, and his first act is to have every compact since the first treaty copied into one bound book.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-2545"><em>Maddox's goods carried down to the ships</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, AE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2509"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, AE 41** — *Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, who sent A' Chompanaidh's agent down the hill, dies in her own house in an Giblean at sixty-one, among the few hearths left lit after the stream was taken. She is laid out with Doire mhòr's own coal at her head and feet, and the whole hill comes up to her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0046"><em>Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0078"><em>Doire mhòr's water taken</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-2546"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, AE 41** — *Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill* (Muileann chrom). Under Arthur Lisle's first order a rider of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach takes the papers of the pits at Muileann chrom down to Ros dhomhain: the contract of the first thirty and the paper of Raghnall's leader's share. Asked for the agreement that gave the overseers their staffs, Enoch Pratt finds that there is none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0099"><em>Arthur Lisle Commissioner</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, AE 41</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0039"><em>The first mining contracts</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0091"><em>The first Dia-thìreach overseer</em>, 19 an Cèitean, AE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0100"></a>**2 am Màrt, AE 42** — *A customs house at Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Lisle opens a second customs house at Ros gheal on the northern coast, where hawk-faithful fishing towns had traded with Company ships without paying dues. The customs officer is twice chased out of the town in his first year.
- <a id="ev-EV-3013"></a>**15 an t-Ògmhios, AE 42** — *Lisle's clerks bind the agreements in one book* (Ros dhomhain). Arthur Lisle's two clerks spend the winter at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir copying every agreement made between the island and the strangers since the leave, with Cairt na Companaidh bound at the back. Lisle reads the book through with a pen and writes his queries in the margins; the letter-books keep forty pages of his notes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0099"><em>Arthur Lisle Commissioner</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, AE 41</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0100"><em>A customs house at Ros gheal</em>, 2 am Màrt, AE 42</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3014"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, AE 42** — *The hawk-faithful carry the customs officer out of Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Eleven days after the customs house opens, some thirty hawk-faithful of Ros gheal come down from the hawk-house at dusk, carry the officer's table, book and scale into the street, and walk him to the last house on the road south. He returns within the month with two clerks and a letter from Lisle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0100"><em>A customs house at Ros gheal</em>, 2 am Màrt, AE 42</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The hawk-house at Ros gheal</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_IV/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_Sundering.pdf#ev-III-0063">→ An Aois Scaraidh, LE 239</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3015"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, AE 42** — *Ros gheal rows the customs officer down the coast* (Ros gheal). At the autumn herring the fishing families of Ros gheal put the customs officer, his clerks, his table and his scale into a boat and set them ashore on a roadless beach two miles down the coast. The town's roll says only that he went away by water. Lisle writes that the town has broken no page, since none yet binds it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0100"><em>A customs house at Ros gheal</em>, 2 am Màrt, AE 42</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0101"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, AE 43** — *The silver of Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The humans seek to claim the silver seam at Muileann chiar as well. It is one of the few things the Dia-thìrich keep wholly in their own hands through all this age.
- <a id="ev-EV-3001"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, AE 43** — *Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg* (Muileann chrom). Reading the council's copies by rushlight at the inns of Rathad na Mèinne on her way home, Ùna nic Choinnich finds coal named on every page of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and no word of silver, nor of any metal but the iron the humans paid with. At the inn below Muileann chrom she tells her grandson that A' Chompanaidh holds no paper for the seam.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0029"><em>The first written treaty</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3016"></a>**31 am Faoilleach, AE 43** — *Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall* (Muileann chiar). The agent of A' Chompanaidh at Muileann chrom sends notice to Muileann chiar that surveyors will measure the silver seam in spring under the charter's first refusal. Ùna nic Choinnich reads the letter in both tongues to forty-one members of Comann an Airgid gathered in the guild hall by night, and resolves to ask the council what it holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0101"><em>The silver of Muileann chiar</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, AE 43</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0032"><em>The Company chartered</em>, 18 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3001"><em>Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3017"></a>**27 an Gearran, AE 43** — *Coinneach Glas lends Ùna the council's copies* (Cathair dhearg). Ùna nic Choinnich rides three days to Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim, aged sixty-eight and ailing, hears her out in the room of the rolls and gives her the council's own copies of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts, bidding her look for the silver before the humans do.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0101"><em>The silver of Muileann chiar</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, AE 43</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0029"><em>The first written treaty</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0058"><em>The Harbour Articles</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, AE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3016"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall</em>, 31 am Faoilleach, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0102"></a>**31 am Màrt, AE 43** — *Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver seam was held for the town by its guild of refiners, led by Ùna nic Choinnich. When the Company's surveyors came she met them at the adit with every member of the guild and all its ledgers, and bade them find the humans' name anywhere in either.
- <a id="ev-EV-3018"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 43** — *The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir* (Ros dhomhain). The chief surveyor reports to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the whole of Muileann chiar met him at the working, silent, and that he found no grant or payment to A' Chompanaidh in either of the guild's books and did not think it prudent to proceed. Lisle writes beneath it that he would not have found it either, and sends for the bound book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0102"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild</em>, 31 am Màrt, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3019"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 43** — *Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing* (Ros dhomhain). In a long letter to the master of A' Chompanaidh, Arthur Lisle sets out that Cairt na Companaidh is a promise made by its own masters and grants nothing on the island, where the only title is Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, which speaks of coal and says nothing of silver. The master of A' Chompanaidh protests; Lisle answers in two lines.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0102"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild</em>, 31 am Màrt, AE 43</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0032"><em>The Company chartered</em>, 18 an Cèitean, AE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0029"><em>The first written treaty</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3018"><em>The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3020"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, AE 43** — *The guild asks for the compact in both tongues* (Muileann chiar). Answering Lisle's proposal of a compact, Ùna nic Choinnich writes in the humans' letters that the guild will sign, that it must be signed at Muileann chiar where the seam lies, and that it be written in both tongues line against line. Lisle strikes out his clerk's query and agrees, and says he will come himself on Là Fhèill Brìde.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0102"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild</em>, 31 am Màrt, AE 43</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3019"><em>Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0103"></a>**1 an Gearran, AE 44** — *The Silver Compact* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Arthur Lisle, reading the treaties closely, finds nothing in them touching silver. On Là Fhèill Brìde he signs a compact with the silver guild leaving the seam to the town, the first writing of the age in which the Dia-thìrich keep the better terms.
- <a id="ev-EV-3002"></a>**7 an Gearran, AE 44** — *The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar* (Cathair dhearg). In the spring after the compact Ùna nic Choinnich sends the council's leaves of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts back to Cathair dhearg by her grandson Fionnlagh, wrapped in the same oilcloth they came in, with a bar of silver for the clerk who keeps the presses.
- <a id="ev-EV-3021"></a>**22 am Màrt, AE 44** — *The compact read in the guild hall* (Muileann chiar). On the evening of the signing, after Lisle's carriage has gone down the valley, Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud to Comann an Airgid in the guild hall of Muileann chiar from its Dia-thìris column, and read a second time for the apprentices. It is laid that night in the guild chest under three locks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0103"><em>The Silver Compact</em>, 1 an Gearran, AE 44</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3002"><em>The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar</em>, 7 an Gearran, AE 44</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3022"></a>**22 an Giblean, AE 44** — *Lisle sees the silver seam* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Before leaving Muileann chiar Arthur Lisle asks to see the seam, and Ùna nic Choinnich takes him into the adit with a lamp. He tells her he has never seen the colours in the coal but can see the silver; she answers that the Dia-thìrich see it the same, and that this is why silver is not holy.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0103"><em>The Silver Compact</em>, 1 an Gearran, AE 44</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>Silver is not holy</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0017">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 74</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3021"><em>The compact read in the guild hall</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 44</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3023"></a>**17 an Cèitean, AE 44** — *Death of Coinneach Glas* (Cathair dhearg). Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim since the death of Tormod mac Ailein, dies in his chair in the room of the rolls at Cathair dhearg, aged sixty-nine, after twenty-four years in the seat. He has had Cùmhnant an Airgid read to him twice and called it a better paper than any he signed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0061"><em>Death of Tormod mac Ailein</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0103"><em>The Silver Compact</em>, 1 an Gearran, AE 44</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3024"></a>**27 an Cèitean, AE 44** — *Alasdair Liath chosen Ceann a' Chùraim* (Cathair dhearg). Comhairle a' Chùraim chooses Alasdair Liath, aged forty-nine, to sit as Ceann a' Chùraim after Coinneach Glas. He has sat on the council since before Puingean a' Chalaidh and voted to sign them. The roll records his age and the number of voices and nothing more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0061"><em>Death of Tormod mac Ailein</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0058"><em>The Harbour Articles</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, AE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0104"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 44** — *Seann Bhral the silver port* (Seann Bhral). The silver guild sends its bars to the sea by the old port of Seann Bhral and not by the Company's quays, and pays the port's custodians in silver for the use of it. The Company finds no ground in the compact to object.
- <a id="ev-EV-3025"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, AE 44** — *The first silver carts go down to Seann Bhral* (Seann Bhral). Refusing the request of A' Chompanaidh that its silver pass through the quays of Ros dhomhain, Comann an Airgid sends its first carts of bar silver eighteen miles down the valley to Seann Bhral, and pays the port's custodians by the Muileann chiar weight on every bar. Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir tells the agent of A' Chompanaidh the compact gives no ground to object.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0104"><em>Seann Bhral the silver port</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 44</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>The Muileann chiar weight made law</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0153">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 1,750</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3026"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, AE 44** — *The guild's book of weighings filled* (Muileann chiar).
