In the summer after the compact the smelting-floors of Muileann chiar work from dawn to dark, and the guild's paper book of the weighings, begun in An Aois Scaraidh and kept in a dozen hands, is filled by the autumn and a new one begun.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0104"><em>Seann Bhral the silver port</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 44</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0105"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, AE 45** — *The carters of Baile gheal* (Baile gheal). The carters of Baile gheal in the south-west take up the carrying of Seann Warr brine-salt round the lake to the capital, a trade the Company does not trouble to claim. It keeps the town's folk out of the pits for the whole age.
- <a id="ev-EV-3003"></a>**5 am Màrt, AE 45** — *Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest* (Muileann chiar). On the day Comann an Airgid reckons its year, the three keyholders open the guild chest and Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud in both tongues. Ùna nic Choinnich, aged fifty-nine, lays it back on the new book of weighings beside the notched boards of the old ledger, and the three locks are turned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0103"><em>The Silver Compact</em>, 1 an Gearran, AE 44</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3027"></a>**26 am Màrt, AE 45** — *The guild enters the Baile gheal salt in its ledger* (Muileann chiar). A carter from the west brings word to Muileann chiar that the carters of Baile gheal have taken up the Seann Warr salt trade round the lake. Ùna nic Choinnich has it written into the guild's new ledger as a thing the humans did not take.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0105"><em>The carters of Baile gheal</em>, 21 am Faoilleach, AE 45</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3003"><em>Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest</em>, 5 am Màrt, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3028"></a>**14 an Giblean, AE 45** — *The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay* (Àth dhearg). The custodian of Àth dhearg calls the town's hearths to the room over the net-store. A' Chompanaidh will pay half the cost of a tower on the north-eastern cape in marks and send the lens and oil; the town is to find the stone and the hands, the other half of the pay being the promise that the light will bring its boats home. The town agrees.
- <a id="ev-EV-3029"></a>**22 an Giblean, AE 45** — *Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). The masons of Àth dhearg raise the tower over the old fire-shelf on the cape. They take down the cairn Torcall Clachair built there with James Fenn and set its stones in the footing, facing the sea, and turn a stair inside the wall. The old cut stair up the cliff is left as it was.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0027"><em>The beacon headlands walked</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3028"><em>The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay</em>, 14 an Giblean, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0106"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, AE 45** — *Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). The third beacon is lit on the north-east coast at Àth dhearg. Its keeper, Tormod mac Pheadair, keeps a daybook of every ship he sees, and from his book the number of human sailings in these years is known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3028"><em>The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay</em>, 14 an Giblean, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3030"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, AE 45** — *The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). On the night of the lighting Tormod mac Pheadair, keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, writes the first line in the grey-bound book of the humans' paper that A' Chompanaidh left him: lit at dusk, the wind west and light, and no ship. It is the first keeper's daybook kept on the island.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0106"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 45</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3029"><em>Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower</em>, 22 an Giblean, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3031"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 45** — *Two dates at the head of the daybook* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). A man of A' Chompanaidh, unable to tell the days of passing ships from the nights of the moon, writes out the humans' months for the keeper of Àth dhearg. Thereafter Tormod mac Pheadair heads every entry with the humans' day above and the night of the moon beneath, and writes the humans' days in over his first entries.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0106"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 45</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3030"><em>The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3032"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, AE 45** — *The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). A north-easterly gale catches four boats of Àth dhearg on the long lines beyond the reef. The keeper lights the lamp an hour before dusk. Three boats come home by the light through the night, one from the wrong side of the reef; the fourth returns at dawn a man short. Tormod mac Pheadair enters the boats and the lost man by name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0106"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, AE 45</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3031"><em>Two dates at the head of the daybook</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0107"></a>**28 an Cèitean, AE 46** — *Àth dhearg builds the tower* (Àth dhearg). The masons of the beacon at Àth dhearg are its own townsmen, paid half in marks and half in the promise that the tower will guide their own boats home. Tormod mac Pheadair, the keeper, is one of them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3028"><em>The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay</em>, 14 an Giblean, AE 45</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3029"><em>Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower</em>, 22 an Giblean, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3033"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, AE 46** — *The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg* (Àth dhearg). When A' Chompanaidh pays the eleven masons of the tower in marks at its foot, the custodian's clerk enters the payment in the town's roll, and beside it that the other half of their pay was made in the Bealltach gale, in four boats and three of them home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0107"><em>Àth dhearg builds the tower</em>, 28 an Cèitean, AE 46</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3032"><em>The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, AE 45</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0108"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 46** — *Pirates off the eastern coast* (Spùinneadairean-mara). Raiders in low black boats take a Company coal ship off the eastern coast and burn her to the waterline, cargo and all. The Company says the silver guild paid them. The silver guild says nothing.
- <a id="ev-EV-3004"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, AE 46** — *The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). Two nights after entering a laden collier of A' Chompanaidh going south, Tormod mac Pheadair sees a red light low in the south under the cloud from the middle watch until near dawn, and writes that he does not know what it was. The carters bring word four days later that raiders have burned her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0108"><em>Pirates off the eastern coast</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 46</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3005"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, AE 46** — *The keeper will not write the black boats* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). In Dubhlas a clerk of A' Chompanaidh rides to Àth dhearg to read the daybook and asks the keeper to write in black raiding boats seen going south before the burning. Tormod mac Pheadair answers that he saw none and will write no boat he has not seen. The clerk reports the book of no assistance.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0108"><em>Pirates off the eastern coast</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 46</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3006"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, AE 46** — *The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). In Teasach of the forty-seventh year a black two-masted ship of war of A' Chompanaidh, a gun in her bows under canvas and more men on deck than any trader carries, comes round the north coast and south past the cape. The keeper of Àth dhearg enters her with more care than any ship before.
- <a id="ev-EV-3034"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, AE 46** — *The collier's crew fed near Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). The raiders who burn the collier of A' Chompanaidh put her crew into their own boat and set them rowing for the land. The crew come ashore alive at a fishing village near Ceann leathan, where the households feed and shelter them until a rider can carry word south to Seann Bhral.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0108"><em>Pirates off the eastern coast</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 46</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3035"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 46** — *A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning* (Seann Bhral). Within a month of the burning the agents of A' Chompanaidh say at Seann Bhral and Ros dhomhain, and write to Arthur Lisle, that Comann an Airgid paid the raiders in spite for the surveyors turned back from the adit at Muileann chiar. The guild makes no answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0108"><em>Pirates off the eastern coast</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 46</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0102"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild</em>, 31 am Màrt, AE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0109"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, AE 47** — *A cove burned near Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). A Company gunboat hunts the raiders to a cove near Ceann leathan and burns every boat drawn up on the shingle, most of them belonging to the town's fishermen. The raiders are not found.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3006"><em>The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, AE 46</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3036"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, AE 47** — *Àth dhearg lends two boats to Ceann leathan* (Àth dhearg). A fisherman of Ceann leathan walks north nearly forty miles with two sons to ask Àth dhearg for a boat after the gunboat burns the cove. The households talk into the night and lend two, to be returned when Ceann leathan has built its own, and the three sail them south in Lùghnas.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0109"><em>A cove burned near Ceann leathan</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3037"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, AE 47** — *The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). Promised timber by A' Chompanaidh, the yard-master Daniel Lusk asks the council of four at Baile dhìreach for a dry-stone wall up the town's shingle and lays its footing while they argue. The town's members hold that the shingle is kept and not built on. On the third night the stones are carried below the wrack-line.
- <a id="ev-EV-3038"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, AE 47** — *The shingle clause read from both books* (Baile dhìreach). Nathan Cobb reads the compact of Baile dhìreach from the humans' book, where the shingle is the town's property; Iain Hale reads it from the Dia-thìris book, where the shingle is kept for the town. Asked by both sides which book is right, Iain Hale closes the book and says nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0022"><em>Baile dhìreach under one council</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, AE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0110"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, AE 47** — *The end of the joint council* (Baile dhìreach). The mixed council of Baile dhìreach breaks up in a quarrel over a boundary wall and never meets again. The human families go to Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain; the Dia-thìrich families stay. Households that were both split or fell silent, and which did which is not told.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3037"><em>The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, AE 47</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3038"><em>The shingle clause read from both books</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3039"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, AE 47** — *The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). When the council breaks and the human families leave for Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain, Samuel Hale, Eilidh nic Ruairidh and their son Iain stay in their house by the well at the head of the street. They take neither side on the wall and speak of other things when it is mentioned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0110"><em>The end of the joint council</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, AE 47</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0028"><em>A marriage in two tongues</em>, 26 an Cèitean, AE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3038"><em>The shingle clause read from both books</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3040"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, AE 47** — *Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom* (Baile dhìreach). Daniel Lusk offers Iain Hale the foreman's place in the yard going to Inis chrom, for more marks than the yard has ever paid. After a night on the shingle and a talk with his father, Iain Hale refuses, and that winter builds the town's boats on the old slip by the town's leave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3039"><em>The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0111"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, AE 47** — *The boatyard moves to Inis chrom* (Inis chrom). The human boatbuilders of Baile dhìreach move their yard to Inis chrom, a day's sail east, where the Company has promised them timber. The town takes them in without a joint council or any other compact, and within a generation they fade from its rolls.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3040"><em>Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3041"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, AE 47** — *The humans' book set back on the shelf* (Baile dhìreach). When the yard has sailed for Inis chrom, Iain Hale finds the council's book in the humans' tongue left open on the mending-table in the net-loft at Baile dhìreach, at a page with a date and nothing under it. He closes it and sets it back on the shelf beside the Dia-thìris book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0111"><em>The boatyard moves to Inis chrom</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, AE 47</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0110"><em>The end of the joint council</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, AE 47</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3040"><em>Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3042"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 47** — *The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). Through the spring and summer of the forty-eighth year the daybook of Àth dhearg records dry winds night after night, the fields inland yellow before midsummer, a heath fire of three days, and the burn below the town stopped, which it has never done in memory. Rain is written once in four months.
- <a id="ev-IV-0112"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, AE 48** — *The dry year in the east* (Achadh shean). For a single season the rain fails over the eastern farmlands about Achadh shean. It is a warning, and no one heeds it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3042"><em>The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3043"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, AE 48** — *Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh* (Baile ruadh). Called by his wife's kin, the keeper of Àth dhearg walks to Baile ruadh and reads to its council, figure by figure, the terms in the humans' figures by which A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn lends seed corn for grain over five harvests. He finds the figures as the interpreter gave them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3042"><em>The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 47</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0113"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 48** — *Baile ruadh loses its seed* (Baile ruadh). At Baile ruadh in the east the drought kills the seed corn in the ground, and the town borrows seed from the Company's store at Seann Dunn, at a price paid back over five harvests. It is the first Dia-thìreach town to owe the Company a debt in grain.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3043"><em>Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, AE 48</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3044"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, AE 48** — *Baile ruadh's seed debt entered* (Baile ruadh). The custodians' roll of Baile ruadh enters the town's debt of seed corn to A' Chompanaidh under the night of the moon, with the measure and the five harvests, the first debt in grain to the strangers in any roll of the island. The clerk writes beside it the name of the keeper who read the figures.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0113"><em>Baile ruadh loses its seed</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 48</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3043"><em>Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, AE 48</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0114"></a>**19 an t-Ògmhios, AE 49** — *Aonghas mac Coinnich's question* (Dùn thais). At Dùn thais the druid master Aonghas mac Coinnich puts to his students a question the school's register calls new: why the humans cannot see the colour in broken coal that every Dia-thìreach child sees. He does not answer it, and the register notes that he called it the wrong question.
- <a id="ev-EV-3045"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, AE 49** — *Three students carry the question west* (Dùn thais). In the autumn three students of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais walk over the high moor to Baile Mòr uaine, carrying Aonghas mac Coinnich's question with a sealed copy in the register-keeper's hand. The masters of Baile Mòr uaine take it up at the dark of the year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0114"><em>Aonghas mac Coinnich's question</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, AE 49</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0115"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 49** — *The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine* (Baile Mòr uaine). Students of Aonghas mac Coinnich carry his question to Baile Mòr uaine and teach it in the town's hall of disputation. The hall's record of the argument runs to four hundred leaves, and ends, like his, without an answer.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3045"><em>Three students carry the question west</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, AE 49</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3046"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 49** — *The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais* (Baile Mòr uaine). The record of the argument at Baile Mòr uaine comes back to Dùn thais leaf by leaf with the carriers, four hundred leaves in all. Its last leaf lists those who spoke and notes that the hall adjourned because the peat was done. Aonghas mac Coinnich reads every leaf and names no argument the best.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0115"><em>The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 49</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3045"><em>Three students carry the question west</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, AE 49</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0116"></a>**28 an Cèitean, AE 50** — *Cathair gheal in the northern concession* (Cathair gheal). The human families of the northern concession found a market town at Cathair gheal, with a stone hall for their magistrate and a chapel. The Administration issues its charter without asking the custodians.
- <a id="ev-EV-3007"></a>**25 an t-Ògmhios, AE 50** — *Eachann Mòr loses his seat* (Ceann àrsaidh). The council at Cathair dhearg protests Cairt Chathair gheal, which names no custodian, and receives an answer in the humans' tongue that none of its members can read with confidence. At the autumn choosing at Ceann àrsaidh the households put out Eachann Mòr, who has no letters of that tongue, and choose Dùghall Òg of the carting families, who worked five years at A' Chompanaidh's weigh-house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0116"><em>Cathair gheal in the northern concession</em>, 28 an Cèitean, AE 50</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0117"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 50** — *Human farms at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). Human farmers of the concession clear land beside the Dia-thìrich village of Cnoc ghorm in the upland north-west, and build a mill. The villagers sell them grain until the mill is working, and then stop.
- <a id="ev-EV-3047"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, AE 50** — *Cnoc ghorm stops selling grain* (Cnoc ghorm). Through the first winter the villagers of Cnoc ghorm sell grain at a fair price to the human farmers who have cleared land beside them, and carry it on their own ponies. When the farmers' mill turns in the spring, they sell no more, and give no reason. Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letters speak of a coolness at the old village.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0117"><em>Human farms at Cnoc ghorm</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, AE 50</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 51 – 60

- <a id="ev-IV-0118"></a>**14 am Màrt, AE 51** — *A fishing station at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). A few human fishing families of the concession settle at Ceann mhòr, the harbour under the north-western headland. They are the first humans to fish the island's waters for a living and not for the Company's table.
- <a id="ev-IV-0119"></a>**10 an Giblean, AE 51** — *The first Dia-thìreach child sent over the sea*. One family, hoping for better treatment, sends a son to be schooled in the humans' homeland. He is never known to return.
- <a id="ev-IV-0120"></a>**12 an Giblean, AE 51** — *The family of Eachann Mòr* (Ceann àrsaidh). The family that sent its son away was that of Eachann Mòr, a custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who had lost his seat on the council. The boy, Calum, sailed over the sea on a Company ship with a letter from the Mission and a purse of marks.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3007"><em>Eachann Mòr loses his seat</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, AE 50</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3048"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 51** — *Calum's ship sails north-about* (Ros dhomhain). Calum, son of Eachann Mòr, thirteen years old, goes aboard a ship of A' Chompanaidh at the quay below Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain with Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letter and a purse of marks sewn into his coat. A pilot of Caol leathan takes her down the Abhainn gheal on the evening tide, and she turns north up the west coast to go round by the north to the humans' land.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0119"><em>The first Dia-thìreach child sent over the sea</em>, 10 an Giblean, AE 51</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0120"><em>The family of Eachann Mòr</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 51</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0121"></a>**9 an Cèitean, AE 51** — *The Mission school* (Ros dhomhain). The Mission opens a school at Ros dhomhain for Dia-thìrich children, taught in the humans' tongue. It takes thirty pupils in its first year, most of them overseers' children, and among them the Mission counts its first Dia-thìrich converts.
- <a id="ev-EV-3008"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, AE 51** — *Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea* (Ceann àrsaidh). No letter comes from Calum by the autumn ships. In the winter Eachann Mòr writes to his son in Dia-thìris, pays a pupil of Scoil na Teachdaireachd to put it into the humans' tongue beneath his lines, and gives it with a mark to the master of the first ship going north. No answer comes to it, nor to the three he sends after it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0120"><em>The family of Eachann Mòr</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 51</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0121"><em>The Mission school</em>, 9 an Cèitean, AE 51</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0122"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 52** — *Schooling at Inis bhàn* (Inis bhàn). The custodians of Inis bhàn in the north open a school of their own in answer to the Mission's, and teach the old reckoning, the rolls and the names of the hills. The Mission complains that the pupils come to its school the next year already knowing how to argue.
- <a id="ev-EV-3049"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, AE 52** — *Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn* (Inis bhàn). Eachann Mòr sends his daughter Ciorstaidh, ten years old, to the custodians' new school at Inis bhàn. She comes home at midsummer able to name forty hills and to argue the boundaries of her father's parish. The custodians of Inis bhàn keep Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's complaint about their pupils as a testimonial.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0122"><em>Schooling at Inis bhàn</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 52</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3008"><em>Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea</em>, 3 an t-Iuchar, AE 51</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0122a"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, AE 52** — *Tobacco on the concession farms* (Ceann mhòr). Human farmers of the northern concession plant tobacco on the sheltered slopes behind Ceann mhòr and sell the dried leaf to the Company's ships. Of the crops the humans brought, it alone is still grown on Dia-thìr.
- <a id="ev-IV-0123"></a>**1 an Giblean, AE 53** — *Drochaid Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). The Company rebuilds the old bridge over the river at Ros fhionn to carry the eastern coal road. While the carts run it is the busiest crossing on that side of the island.
- <a id="ev-EV-3050"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, AE 53** — *The students at Drochaid Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). Aonghas mac Coinnich takes the students of Dùn thais to watch the first coal-carts cross the rebuilt bridge at Ros fhionn, forty in an afternoon. The island's drivers throw down lumps for them to name; the two human drivers look at their loads as at stones. Ailean Clachair's sign stays in the keystone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0123"><em>Drochaid Ros fhionn</em>, 1 an Giblean, AE 53</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0124"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, AE 53** — *Coal through Inis bheag* (Inis bheag). Coal from the eastern workings is carted over the new bridge and down to the river quays of Inis bheag, and goes by barge to Caol chrom at the river mouth for shipping. The Company deepens the river at the quays, and the town's old fish market is moved to make room for the coal stage.
- <a id="ev-IV-0125"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, AE 54** — *Baile mhin ships the eastern coal* (Baile mhin). The river quays of Baile mhin, below Inis bheag on the Abhainn bheag, take the eastern coal that Inis bheag cannot load. The townsfolk are paid by the barge, and with the gain the town builds its first stone houses.
- <a id="ev-EV-3009"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, AE 54** — *The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter* (Ros dhomhain). In the third year after his son sailed Eachann Mòr asks at A' Chompanaidh's counter at Ros dhomhain after the ship by name. She has come and gone twice since, under another master now. Against the day Calum sailed the clerk reads one line, a native boy, his fare paid in full, and says his book knows nothing more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0120"><em>The family of Eachann Mòr</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 51</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0125"><em>Baile mhin ships the eastern coal</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 54</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0126"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 54** — *Caol gharbh passed by* (Caol gharbh). The coal road to Inis bheag passes Caol gharbh by a mile, and the town, which had hoped for the traffic, gets only its dust. Its custodians write that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on.
- <a id="ev-EV-3051"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, AE 54** — *Caol gharbh's letter on the door at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). Aonghas mac Coinnich pins a copy of the letter of Caol gharbh's custodians, who wrote that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on, to the door of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais beside the carved lintel. It stays there until the rain takes it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0126"><em>Caol gharbh passed by</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 54</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0127"></a>**12 am Màrt, AE 55** — *The thing in the north-western sea* (Uilebheist na Mara). The crew of a Company brig see a beast greater than their ship off the north-western headlands. The Administration's clerk files their report with the complaints about pirates, and the Dia-thìrich sailors of the coast say they had wondered when the humans would see it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0127a"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, AE 55** — *A brig lost in the mist* (Caol bheag). A Company brig bound for the northern landing with tools is caught by a gale in sea mist off Eilean fhada and driven onto the skerries. Her crew wade ashore at low water and walk to the harbour at Caol bheag. Thereafter the Company's charts mark the northern passage closed to its ships from midwinter to the end of spring, the season of the gales.
- <a id="ev-IV-0127b"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, AE 55** — *Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn* (Àth fhionn). Human fishermen of the concession teach the boats of Àth fhionn to hunt whales with the hand-lance, and not wait for them to strand. The oil is sold to the Company for its lamps, and from this time whale-boats go out from the north coast every summer.
- <a id="ev-IV-0128"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, AE 56** — *Surveyors lost at Doire uaine* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). Two Company surveyors go up into the hills at Doire uaine against the villagers' counsel and are not seen again. The Company sends a search party, which comes back after a day and will go no further.
- <a id="ev-EV-3052"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, AE 56** — *The search party returns from Doire uaine* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). A' Chompanaidh's search party of eight men goes up into the hills of Doire uaine and comes down the same evening. They report the lost surveyors' chains laid out along a ridge and a ring of fire-stones with no ash in it, and refuse to go further for pay or threats. The agent writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the men are idle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0128"><em>Surveyors lost at Doire uaine</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, AE 56</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0129"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 56** — *The offerings at Doire uaine* (Doire uaine). After the surveyors are lost the villagers of Doire uaine leave salt and coal for the sìth at the foot of the hills, as their grandparents did after any death on the high ground. The Company forbids coal to be left lying and has the offerings gathered up, and the villagers leave salt alone.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3052"><em>The search party returns from Doire uaine</em>, 16 an t-Sultain, AE 56</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3053"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 56** — *Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). At the end of harvest Eachann Mòr rides two days from Ceann àrsaidh to Dùn thais and asks Aonghas mac Coinnich whether his son, five years among the humans, will see the colour in the coal when he comes home. The master puts a broken lump in his hand and will not answer. The register records that a man came to ask the question and the master did not answer it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0114"><em>Aonghas mac Coinnich's question</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, AE 49</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0129"><em>The offerings at Doire uaine</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 56</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0130"></a>**16 an Gearran, AE 57** — *The tithe raised*. The share of mined coal taken by the humans' Administration rises steeply. What the Dia-thìrich receive does not rise with it.
- <a id="ev-EV-3054"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 57** — *Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Anne Colby comes ashore at the Ros dhomhain quays at two and twenty, sent out by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise with a chest of linen and instruments she has scarcely been shown how to use, hoping to hear word of a brother lost years before on Harrow's ships. She finds no word of him; within the year she finds the flux.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0130"><em>The tithe raised</em>, 16 an Gearran, AE 57</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0131"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, AE 57** — *Lisle's tithe schedule* (Ros dhomhain). The new schedule goes out from the Residency under Arthur Lisle's hand and raises the Administration's share from one part in five to one part in three. The custodians receive a copy in the humans' tongue, with a rendering made by a Mission pupil.
- <a id="ev-EV-3055"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, AE 57** — *Barabal nic Dhùghaill reads the schedule at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). A pupil of Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise of fifteen, Barabal nic Dhùghaill, renders Lisle's three sealed sheets into Dia-thìris before the council, reading the new fraction twice over at the old custodian of Cnoc bheag's asking. The council has her rendering copied word for word into every coal town's roll, with her own name set at the foot of each copy.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0131"><em>Lisle's tithe schedule</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, AE 57</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0132"></a>**4 an Lùnastal, AE 58** — *Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich* (Dùn fhiadhaich). At Dùn fhiadhaich the tithe-gatherers begin to weigh grain as well as coal, saying the town's farms feed the pits and share in their gain. The custodians' roll calls it the tithe on the tithe.
- <a id="ev-EV-3056"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 58** — *The tithe on the tithe named at Dùn fhiadhaich* (Dùn fhiadhaich). Griogair Fada, the largest farmer under Cnoc naomh, asks the young tithe-gatherer who set the new weight on grain and gets no answer he can carry home. The custodians of Dùn fhiadhaich enter the weighing in their roll under a name of their own coining, deachamh an deachaimh, the tithe on the tithe.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0132"><em>Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich</em>, 4 an Lùnastal, AE 58</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0133"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59** — *The flux at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A bloody flux breaks out in the crowded quarters at the Ros dhomhain quays. The Mission's nurse, Anne Colby, makes a sick-house of the chapel, and it is said that she kept the dead below two hundred.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3054"><em>Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 57</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3010"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, AE 59** — *A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once* (Cathair dhomhain). A' Chompanaidh's own surgeon comes to the chapel door at Ros dhomhain, will not step past the threshold, and tells Colby she would do better to let the sick lie where they were found. He sends, before he leaves the harbour, a case of salts and does not come again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0133"><em>The flux at Ros dhomhain</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3057"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, AE 59** — *Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names* (Cathair dhomhain). Washing the chapel floor by lamplight on Colby's first night of nursing the flux, the widow Mòr nic Amhlaidh tells her that the dying want their own names said to them more than they want the fever broken. Colby is said to have kept the counsel from that night on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0133"><em>The flux at Ros dhomhain</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3010"><em>A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, AE 59</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3058"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, AE 59** — *Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house* (Cathair dhomhain). Anne Colby has Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's chapel at Ros dhomhain opened and its benches carried into the yard without asking anyone's leave, and with Mòr nic Amhlaidh and her daughter carries the flux-sick up from the harbour lodgings on a hand-barrow until the stone room and its yard hold as many as can lie down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0133"><em>The flux at Ros dhomhain</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3057"><em>Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, AE 59</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3059"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, AE 59** — *Colby's roll of the dead by name* (Cathair dhomhain). Each evening Anne Colby sits at the chapel door with the custodians' own roll open on her knee and a clerk's boy to read her the entries, and sets down against every name who lived and who died, in English, in a column she turns round on the table for the custodians to see is kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0133"><em>The flux at Ros dhomhain</em>, 6 an t-Iuchar, AE 59</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3058"><em>Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 59</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0134"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 60** — *The flux reaches Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). The coal barges carry the flux to Seann Vell, the river port east of the capital on the Abhainn fhionn. The custodians of the town shut the barge landing for a season, and the Company fines them for it.
- <a id="ev-EV-3060"></a>**20 an t-Iuchar, AE 60** — *A bargeman put ashore at Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). A bargeman on the coal run east from Ros dhomhain falls sick at his pole and is put ashore at the Seann Vell landing rather than carried on, the barge-master judging, wrongly, that dry land would serve him better than the water. Within the month the flux is in a dozen houses of the town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0134"><em>The flux reaches Seann Vell</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 60</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3061"></a>**20 an t-Sultain, AE 60** — *Seann Vell shuts its landing* (Seann Vell). The custodians of Seann Vell, led by Mairead nic Amhlaidh, close the only quay their river town has for the coal traffic that feeds it, and let no barge tie up there through a whole season, though the closing costs the town every fee that quay has ever earned it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0134"><em>The flux reaches Seann Vell</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 60</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3062"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, AE 60** — *A' Chompanaidh fines Seann Vell for the shut landing* (Seann Vell). A letter from the pay office fines Seann Vell for the season's lost landing fees and says nothing of the flux the closing was meant to check. Mairead nic Amhlaidh reads it to the town council on the landing steps within sight of that season's graves, and the town pays it from the same purse that buried its dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0134"><em>The flux reaches Seann Vell</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 60</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3061"><em>Seann Vell shuts its landing</em>, 20 an t-Sultain, AE 60</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 61 – 70

- <a id="ev-IV-0135"></a>**3 am Màrt, AE 61** — *Walter Crane Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Arthur Lisle dies at the Residency of a fever of the heart. Walter Crane, who had been the Company's chief agent at the pits, is made Commissioner after him, the first to hold both offices one after the other.
- <a id="ev-EV-3063"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, AE 61** — *Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir* (Ros dhomhain). Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain of a fever that settles in his chest and then his heart, a fortnight dying by inches and signing papers to the last. He is one and sixty, Àrd-mhaor twenty years, remembered by the custodians for a raised voice never once heard at their council table, though not forgiven the schedule.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0135"><em>Walter Crane Commissioner</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 61</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0136"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, AE 61** — *The pay office at Ceann mhin* (Ceann mhin). Crane moves the Company's pay office for the southern workings to Ceann mhin, and makes the crews walk there to be paid, a day each way, in place of sending the paymaster to them. The crews are not paid for the walk.
- <a id="ev-EV-3011"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, AE 61** — *Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin* (Muileann chrom). Uisdean Ruadh, a hewer of Muileann chrom, walks with forty of his gang before light on a morning of frost to stand in the pay line at Ceann mhin till near dusk, and walks home again in the dark. He keeps the cost of it afterward on a notched stick, kept still by his family three generations on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0136"><em>The pay office at Ceann mhin</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, AE 61</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0137"></a>**12 am Màrt, AE 62** — *Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor* (Muileann chrom). Raghnall Maor dies, and the Company gives his staff to his son Dòmhnall. The overseer's office, which the custodians had hoped would die with the man, becomes a family's inheritance.
- <a id="ev-EV-3012"></a>**12 an Giblean, AE 62** — *Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven* (Muileann chrom). Raghnall Maor is buried on the hill above Muileann chrom beside the eleven of his first gallery, in thin rain, with both shifts of the pit standing at the grave together, a thing not done for any death there before. Anne Colby stands at the grave's edge with her roll and adds, that evening, a line naming his office, the only such line the roll holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0137"><em>Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 62</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3064"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, AE 62** — *Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, called Raghnall Maor, dies at two and seventy in the slate-roofed house A' Chompanaidh built him above the pit he first walked as a guide. Anne Colby, sent for by his son, sits with him two nights before the end; he asks her once whether she writes her dead down by name and tells her it is a good thing to keep doing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0137"><em>Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 62</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3012"><em>Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven</em>, 12 an Giblean, AE 62</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3065"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 62** — *A' Chompanaidh gives Dòmhnall his father's staff* (Muileann chrom). Within the week of the burying a clerk from Ceann mhin brings Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill the office, the slate roof and the crews together as one paper needing only his mark. The custodians of Muileann chrom, who had hoped the office might die with Raghnall, see it pass from father to son as if it had always been meant to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0137"><em>Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor</em>, 12 am Màrt, AE 62</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3064"><em>Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, AE 62</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3066"></a>**24 an t-Sultain, AE 62** — *Edwin Lowe sent to Muileann bheag* (Muileann bheag). Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise sends the cleric Edwin Lowe up from Ros dhomhain to look into a complaint laid by the keepers of the new Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. He rides three days by mule-track and a fourth along the open coast, and finds the beacon burning coal, the first of the island's lights to do so.
- <a id="ev-IV-0138"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 63** — *Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit* (Taigh-solais Muileann bheag). The fourth beacon is lit on the northern shore at Muileann bheag, the first to burn coal and not oil. Its keepers say the flame throws a colour on the water that no oil lamp ever did.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3066"><em>Edwin Lowe sent to Muileann bheag</em>, 24 an t-Sultain, AE 62</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3510"></a>**10 am Màrt, AE 63** — *Ailig mac Griogair shows Lowe the coloured water* (Muileann bheag). The keeper Ailig mac Griogair takes Lowe up the beacon stair and points out a green colour he says lies on the water beneath the flame, further than the beam itself should carry. Lowe looks a long while and sees only firelight on the swell, and writes that he cannot see what the keeper sees.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0138"><em>Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 63</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0139"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, AE 64** — *The fishermen of Muileann bheag* (Muileann bheag). The fishermen of Muileann bheag complain that the colour the coal flame casts on the water drives the herring off. The keepers do not change the lamp. Within a season the herring come back, and the complaint is withdrawn in a letter the Company keeps.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3510"><em>Ailig mac Griogair shows Lowe the coloured water</em>, 10 am Màrt, AE 63</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3501"></a>**8 an Giblean, AE 64** — *The keeper's son answers Lowe on the point* (Muileann bheag). Ailig's young son stands the watch beside Lowe on two further nights and tells him the colour is not a thing looked for but a thing seen, as rain is felt before it falls. Lowe records the boy's answer as the most honest, and the least useful, given him in eleven years on the island.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0139"><em>The fishermen of Muileann bheag</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0140"></a>**27 an Giblean, AE 64** — *The dig at Làrach an Teampaill* (Làrach an Teampaill). The Mission cleric Edwin Lowe digs for a season at Làrach an Teampaill with Company labourers, seeking proof of an older faith on the island. He finds cut stone, burnt bone and marks he cannot read, and writes that the ruin's builders "were not the present race." The custodians agree, and add nothing.
- <a id="ev-EV-3502"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, AE 64** — *Griogal Odhar on Mòd and the older ground* (Làrach an Teampaill). Asked whether any order of the island's faiths claims the ruin, Griogal Odhar tells Lowe that Mòd himself is said not to claim ground older than the vein, for a god who eats the hill can only eat what grew in the hill's own time. No order has ever asked for the ground, and none has been refused it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0140"><em>The dig at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3511"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, AE 64** — *The shepherds of Àth mhòr turn their flocks off the mound* (Làrach an Teampaill). Before the digging begins the shepherds of Àth mhòr move their flocks off the mound of Làrach an Teampaill, which they have grazed every other season, saying only that it is the custom to keep beasts from a grave while the grave stands open.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0140"><em>The dig at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3512"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, AE 64** — *Tormod Ruadh sets down his spade* (Làrach an Teampaill). The eldest of Lowe's labourers, Tormod Ruadh, refuses to dig further once burnt bone is found beside the altar stone, saying he will cut coal for his wage but not dig a man from his own grave for a stranger's paper. The rest of the crew stop with him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0140"><em>The dig at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3513"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, AE 64** — *Four custodians view the pit at Làrach an Teampaill* (Làrach an Teampaill). Custodians of Doire ghlas, Doire fhiadhaich and Àth mhòr walk out together to the opened pit, judge that the stone, the bone and the flints beside it are of no people or craft they know, and have Lowe cover the pit again with the word said over any grave whose kin cannot be found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0140"><em>The dig at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 27 an Giblean, AE 64</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3512"><em>Tormod Ruadh sets down his spade</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3514"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 64** — *Martha Gale reads the partnership at Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Martha Gale brings A' Chompanaidh's offer of partnership to Comann an Airgid hall at Muileann chiar. A clerk reads it in the humans' tongue and a guild boy puts it into Dia-thìris sentence by sentence, at Ùna nic Choinnich's insistence, so that no hand voting on it can say it did not understand.
- <a id="ev-IV-0141"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, AE 65** — *The pillar at Cnoc chiar* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Edwin Lowe copies the writing on the pillar near Cnoc chiar and sets it beside Wren's copy of the obelisk at Cnoc bheag. He judges that the two scripts are not the same, and that neither is of the Dia-thìrich. His notes stop there.
- <a id="ev-EV-3515"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, AE 65** — *Lowe sets Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Wren's copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Lowe lays his rubbing of Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Samuel Wren's old copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag and judges the two hands are not the same, though something in the shapes of both puts him in mind of a single idea, as two strangers' faces can share an expression without sharing a feature.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0141"><em>The pillar at Cnoc chiar</em>, 9 an Lùnastal, AE 65</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0051"><em>The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied</em>, 5 an Gearran, AE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3516"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, AE 65** — *Voss stays behind at Baile Mòr dhìreach* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). When his glazing of A' Chompanaidh contract ends, Peter Voss does not take passage home, telling the muster clerk only that he has found white sand below Baile Mòr dhìreach the like of which he never found in three counties of an Tìr Thall, and means to see what it will make in a furnace.
- <a id="ev-IV-0142"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 66** — *The column at Cnoc ghorm* (Calbh Cnoc ghorm). Lowe's last copy is of the column near Cnoc ghorm, and beside it he writes that its marks are like the pillar's, but not near enough to help. He leaves Dia-thìr the next year and takes his notebooks with him.
- <a id="ev-IV-0142a"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, AE 66** — *The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Peter Voss, a glazier left behind when his Company contract ended, builds a glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach and melts the white sand of Cuan ruadh with charcoal from the hills. It is the first glass made on Dia-thìr. Within a generation his Dia-thìrich apprentices carry the craft to the towns of the capital shore.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3516"><em>Voss stays behind at Baile Mòr dhìreach</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, AE 65</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3503"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, AE 66** — *Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Voss's fourth firing gives a pale green pane clear enough to see a gull through. His apprentice Cairistìona nic Griogair, who carried sand for him all that summer, laughs at the sight of it, the first laugh heard in the glass-house yard since the furnace was raised.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0142a"><em>The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, AE 66</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3517"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, AE 66** — *The first three firings give only slag* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Voss's first three firings of white sand and charcoal give only a black glassy slag, which the town's children carry off for luck and the custodians' clerk records as Voss's first stones, being none. Voss breaks each batch himself and changes the fire and the sand before trying again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0142a"><em>The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, AE 66</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3503"><em>Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, AE 66</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0143"></a>**29 am Màrt, AE 67** — *The silver guild refuses again* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Martha Gale, an agent of the Company, offers the silver guild of Muileann chiar a partnership, on terms the guild's ledger calls generous. Ùna nic Choinnich, now very old, has the offer read aloud twice in the guild hall, and it is refused by show of hands.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3514"><em>Martha Gale reads the partnership at Muileann chiar</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3518"></a>**1 an Giblean, AE 67** — *Lowe sails for home* (Ros dhomhain). Edwin Lowe takes ship at Ros dhomhain the year after copying Calbh Cnoc ghorm, his notebooks sealed under his berth. No answer is ever recorded as coming back over the sea to the stone he copied or the bone he uncovered and covered again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0142"><em>The column at Cnoc ghorm</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 66</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3519"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 67** — *Ùna nic Choinnich questions A' Chompanaidh's beam* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Ùna nic Choinnich, some eighty winters old, has the paragraph on A' Chompanaidh's weighing-beam read a third time and asks twice what the weight would be measured against, unsatisfied with the clerk's answers both times, before putting the offer to the guild's hands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0143"><em>The silver guild refuses again</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3520"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 67** — *The guild's hands refuse the partnership* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The guild hall at Muileann chiar refuses A' Chompanaidh's partnership by every hand but one, an old silversmith too deaf that year to have followed the second reading. Martha Gale takes the count without argument and thanks the hall in a careful, correct Dia-thìris never heard from her again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0143"><em>The silver guild refuses again</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 67</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3519"><em>Ùna nic Choinnich questions A' Chompanaidh's beam</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0144"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *The camp at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). A new camp is opened at Achadh dhomhain for the deep galleries under the hill, and within a few seasons it is the most crowded place in the district. Its houses are built of spoil.
- <a id="ev-EV-3521"></a>**6 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). Beitris Bhàn walks up from Àth ìseal in the camp's first winter with her mother's knife and takes the end room of a house of spoil, next the well, to lay out the camp's dead. Within the week the first bodies are brought to her table.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0144"><em>The camp at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3522"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *The nine of the first winter* (Achadh dhomhain). Achadh dhomhain buries nine in its first winter: two hewers dead of the damp, a child crushed under a runaway cart of spoil, and six of the camp cough. Beitris Bhàn cuts the turf for each grave herself, the camp having no man yet spared from the pit for the work.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0144"><em>The camp at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3521"><em>Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 6 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0145"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, AE 68** — *Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar* (Dùn chiar). The weavers of Dùn chiar take a Company contract for canvas for the camp tents and sacks for the coal, and the town thrives on it. Its custodians note that never before had the town made anything for a use it did not approve.
- <a id="ev-EV-3523"></a>**3 an Gearran, AE 68** — *Dùn chiar votes to weave for the camps* (Dùn chiar). The town council of Dùn chiar votes twenty-six to nine to take a contract of A' Chompanaidh for camp canvas, against the eldest weaver Ealasaid Bhuidhe, who signs the roll of dissent and then weaves canvas with the rest once the custodian has ruled.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0145"><em>Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3524"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, AE 68** — *Cormag mac Ailein raises the first house of spoil* (Achadh dhomhain). The hewer Cormag mac Ailein builds the first house of Achadh dhomhain's camp from stacked spoil chinked with clay and roofs it with Dùn chiar's first bolts of canvas before the frost, tarring the seams himself, his household under it before the year's shortest day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0144"><em>The camp at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0145"><em>Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 68</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0146"></a>**7 am Màrt, AE 69** — *The first of the undying generation*. A girl is born in the mining camps who takes more raw coal into her body over her life than any Dia-thìreach in living memory, and she does not age as the folk about her age. Her name is Aisling.
- <a id="ev-IV-0146a"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, AE 69** — *The coach to the camps* (Muileann chrom). The Company puts a coach on the road between the quay at Ros dhomhain and the camps at Muileann chrom, twice a week each way, changing horses at the old waypoint houses. Clerks and overseers ride in it. The crews walk.
- <a id="ev-IV-0147"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *The coal weighed at the quay* (Ros dhomhain). The Company sets up a great steelyard at the Ros dhomhain quay, and thenceforth the island's yield is known by the ton and the hundredweight. The custodians' old count, kept in seasons of labour, is no longer entered in the roll.
- <a id="ev-EV-3525"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *The steelyard changes the count* (Ros dhomhain). After A' Chompanaidh's great steelyard is hung at Ros dhomhain, the custodians' old count of the yield, kept in baskets and seasons of a crew's labour, is entered less and less in the rolls, until it is not entered at all. Ùna nic Choinnich says the island has let the wrong hill be written down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0147"><em>The coal weighed at the quay</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0148"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *Ros dhìreach the second coal port* (Ros dhìreach). The Company opens a second coal stage at Ros dhìreach on the southern coast for the workings south of the hills. Its first cargo is lost in a squall off the harbour mouth, and the fishermen moved to make room for the stage will not go out after it.
- <a id="ev-EV-3526"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *The wreck off Ros dhìreach* (Ros dhìreach). Ros dhìreach's first cargo goes down in a squall within a mile of the new coal stage, taking the boat and two of the crew who had gone out to trim her load. The fishermen whose grounds were given over for the stage will not put out past the wreck for a season after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0148"><em>Ros dhìreach the second coal port</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3527"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 70** — *Ùna nic Choinnich dies at Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). Ùna nic Choinnich dies in her own bed at Muileann chiar, eighty-five years old, having led Comann an Airgid since before Fiabhras nan Coigreach and twice put A' Chompanaidh's offers to a show of hands and twice seen them refused. Achadh dhomhain, which never saw her, mourns her by the sayings that came down the road ahead of the coach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0143"><em>The silver guild refuses again</em>, 29 am Màrt, AE 67</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 71 – 80

- <a id="ev-IV-0149"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, AE 71** — *The nameless change*. What is befalling the child born two years before has as yet no name in any tongue spoken on the island. Decades pass before anyone tries to make one.
- <a id="ev-EV-3504"></a>**25 an Gearran, AE 71** — *The women's rule of silence* (Achadh dhomhain). Beitris Bhàn tells the women who sat the night of the telling that a charge laid on a man by a spirit is not theirs to spend on the camp's talk, whatever they make of the child in their own kitchens. No meeting is called and no vote taken, but the rule holds among them for years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0149"><em>The nameless change</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3505"></a>**20 am Màrt, AE 71** — *The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness* (Achadh dhomhain). Season on season the women who handle the camp's dying notice, before anyone else in Achadh dhomhain, that Aisling is not changing as a growing child should, and keep what they notice among themselves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0149"><em>The nameless change</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0149a"></a>**26 an Cèitean, AE 71** — *The first steamer* (Ros dhomhain). The first ship driven by an engine comes into Ros dhomhain, a Company paddle-steamer out of an Tìr Thall. The fishermen row out to look at a ship going against the wind with no sail set. Within a generation the Company's coal goes out in nothing else.
- <a id="ev-EV-3506"></a>**15 an t-Ògmhios, AE 71** — *The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table* (Achadh dhomhain). At a laying-out in the camp's fourth winter, Donnchadh mac Thormoid's wife tells the sitting women, for the first time outside her own house, what her husband met in the deep gallery and what it charged him to keep, and what passed the night their daughter was born. She says the words are his and she will change none of them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0146"><em>The first of the undying generation</em>, 7 am Màrt, AE 69</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0149"><em>The nameless change</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, AE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0150"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 72** — *The shrine at Cill dhìreach* (Cill dhìreach). At Cill dhìreach, a village at the edge of the workings, the custodians keep a small shrine where the pit crews leave the first piece of coal from each new gallery. The Company suffers the custom, for it costs a stone a gallery.
- <a id="ev-IV-0151"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 72** — *The keepers of Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). The custodians of the shrine at Cill ghlas, in the hills among the workings, keep the old rites at the mouth of the oldest cutting while the Company's pits deepen about them. It is the last shrine in the district that the pit crews still visit on the old feast days.
- <a id="ev-EV-3528"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, AE 72** — *Beitris Bhàn's first climb to Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). Beitris Bhàn climbs the hill path to Cill ghlas for the first time at Lùnastal and sets a single piece of coal by the flame at the mouth of the oldest cutting, more from the habit of a hard winter's laying-out than from any settled custom of her own people. She says nothing to the custodian, and the custodian says nothing to her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0151"><em>The keepers of Cill ghlas</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 72</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3506"><em>The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table</em>, 15 an t-Ògmhios, AE 71</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0152"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 73** — *A' Phlàigh Uaine*. The Green Death goes through the mining camps. The coal dust is blamed, though no study of it is ever finished. Twenty-six settlements have cases.
- <a id="ev-IV-0153"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73** — *The first cases at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). The Green Death is first marked at Achadh dhomhain: a greenish pallor, then a cough that brings up dark dust, then weakness. The camp buries forty in the first month, in a field beyond the spoil-heaps still called the green acre.
- <a id="ev-EV-3529"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73** — *The first grave dug in An Acair Uaine* (Achadh dhomhain). Beitris Bhàn helps dig the first grave in the stony field beyond Achadh dhomhain's spoil-heaps, on a day the camp's own grave-diggers are themselves too sick to work. Within weeks the whole camp is calling the field an Acair Uaine without anyone having named it so on purpose.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0152"><em>A' Phlàigh Uaine</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 73</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0153"><em>The first cases at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3530"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73** — *Sìne Ruadh orders the huts of Àth ghlas burned* (Àth ghlas). The custodian of Àth ghlas, Sìne Ruadh, orders every hut where a death has occurred burned to the ground with its bedding before the next nightfall, over A' Chompanaidh's agent's written protest at the loss of its property. She burns nine huts before the summer ends.
- <a id="ev-EV-3531"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73** — *The clerk leaves a line blank after the twenty-sixth settlement* (A' Phlàigh Uaine). The custodian's clerk who keeps the roll of settlements with cases of A' Phlàigh Uaine leaves a blank line after the twenty-sixth name. It is still blank when a different hand takes up the roll the following spring, and no twenty-seventh name is ever entered in it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0154"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, AE 74** — *Twenty-six settlements* (A' Phlàigh Uaine). The sickness spreads along the coal roads from the camps at Muileann chrom, Àth ìseal and Cnoc fhiadhaich, and falls hardest on Ros dhìreach, Ceann òg, Inis ìseal, Baile dhomhain, Achadh fhada, Cnoc bheag, Muileann uaine, Cuan àrsaidh and Inis bhàn. The custodians' roll lists the twenty-six settlements that had cases, and leaves a blank line after the last, as though waiting for another.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3531"><em>The clerk leaves a line blank after the twenty-sixth settlement</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0155"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 74** — *The Green Death at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). The Green Death comes to Baile chrom in the hills, not the town of that name in the north-west. The scribes keep the two apart with care, for in later tellings of the island's hungers they are confused.
- <a id="ev-IV-0156"></a>**12 am Màrt, AE 74** — *Àth ghlas burns its huts* (Àth ghlas). At Àth ghlas the custodians order every hut where a death has been burned with its bedding. The Company protests the loss of its property. The custodians note that the sickness stops sooner at Àth ghlas than anywhere else.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3530"><em>Sìne Ruadh orders the huts of Àth ghlas burned</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, AE 73</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0157"></a>**10 an Giblean, AE 74** — *The dead of Cnoc naomh* (Cnoc naomh). At Cnoc naomh the dead of the Green Death are laid in the burial ground of the town's old shrine until it is full, and then in a field outside. The field is never ploughed again.
- <a id="ev-EV-3507"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, AE 74** — *Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). Àrd-mhaor Crane walks the worst of the sickness's second summer at Achadh dhomhain and does not walk faster past the bad huts than the ordinary ones, a thing the custodians and Beitris Bhàn both note and remember afterward in his favour.
- <a id="ev-EV-3508"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, AE 74** — *Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door* (Achadh dhomhain). After laying out the fortieth body of the season, Beitris Bhàn nails a hawk's feather above her own door at Achadh dhomhain. The overseer's boy finds it and reports his father, and she pays the week's pay it costs her and nails up another within the month.
- <a id="ev-EV-3532"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, AE 74** — *Nathaniel Bright opens his table of weighings* (Muileann chrom). At Muileann chrom, Nathaniel Bright begins keeping a ruled black-bound book of the lungs he weighs from A' Phlàigh Uaine's dead, with the custodians' leave and a custodian standing by at each opening. Anne Colby brings her own sick-house tally to set beside it that winter.
- <a id="ev-IV-0158"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, AE 75** — *Doctor Bright's study* (Muileann chrom). Nathaniel Bright, physician to the Administration, begins to study the sickness at Muileann chrom, weighing the dust in the lungs of the dead. In the second season of the work he falls ill, and his notebooks break off in the middle of a table.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3532"><em>Nathaniel Bright opens his table of weighings</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, AE 74</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0159"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 75** — *Walter Crane dies of the Green Death* (Ros dhomhain). Commissioner Crane, who had walked the camps in the worst of the sickness, dies of it at the Residency. Martha Gale, the Company's agent at Ros dhomhain, holds his seal for the months until another comes.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3507"><em>Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, AE 74</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3509"></a>**1 am Màrt, AE 75** — *Anne Colby comes to Beitris Bhàn's door* (Achadh dhomhain). Anne Colby, unsent by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise and unasked by any custodian, comes to Achadh dhomhain to learn from the layer-out Beitris Bhàn what her own hands have taught her of A' Phlàigh Uaine. The two begin washing the camp's dead together, a custom the camp comes to call An Dithis a Nigh Còmhla.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0152"><em>A' Phlàigh Uaine</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 73</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3533"></a>**20 am Màrt, AE 75** — *Bright's table breaks off mid-row* (Muileann chrom). Nathaniel Bright falls ill in the third season of his study. His last entry stops after the weight of a dead man's lung, with the column for the dust in it left empty and the pen, by the mark it leaves, set down and never taken up again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0158"><em>Doctor Bright's study</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 75</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0160"></a>**13 am Màrt, AE 76** — *George Tolley Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). George Tolley comes from an Tìr Thall with orders that the yield must not fall for the sickness. He does not visit the camps. His letter-book blames the dust, the Dia-thìrich custom of sleeping near the fire, and the custodians' shrines, in that order.
- <a id="ev-IV-0161"></a>**11 an Giblean, AE 76** — *Quarantine at Caol mhin* (Caol mhin). Tolley sets a quarantine station at Caol mhin on the northern coast for ships from an Tìr Thall, and holds them offshore until their crews are looked over. It is the first order of his rule the Dia-thìrich approve, and they say so.
- <a id="ev-IV-0162"></a>**10 an Cèitean, AE 76** — *The camps turn to the hawk* (Muileann chrom). The hawk-priests still barred from the camps, the crews carry their sermons in themselves. The overseers' reports of these years list hawk-feathers nailed above hut doors as a matter for punishment.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-3508"><em>Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, AE 74</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-3534"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, AE 76** — *Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom of the same sickness he had spent three seasons weighing in other men's lungs, and is buried by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise apart from An Acair Uaine and the field at Cnoc naomh. His book is filed at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and never taken up by any physician after him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0158"><em>Doctor Bright's study</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, AE 75</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-3533"><em>Bright's table breaks off mid-row</em>, 20 am Màrt, AE 75</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0163"></a>**17 an Giblean, AE 77** — *Anne Colby's sick-houses* (Ros dhomhain). Anne Colby opens sick-houses at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain and nurses there until the sickness ebbs. She is the only human the camp folk name in their own accounts of the plague, and they name her kindly.
- <a id="ev-EV-4001"></a>**21 an Giblean, AE 77** — *Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe* (Baile thais). Catrìona nic Eachainn, crew-leader of the seventh shift at Baile thais, asks the agent Silas Crewe to close the third and fourth galleries, where A' Phlàigh Uaine struck worst, until the surgeon rules on the dust. Crewe answers that the yield must not fall on a physician's guess, and says only that he will write it up.
- <a id="ev-EV-4002"></a>**23 an Giblean, AE 77** — *Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest* (Baile thais). Asked by Catrìona nic Eachainn whether any old law binds a hill's rest, the custodian Sìneag of Baile thais searches her rolls and finds none: Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig governs the coal burned, not the coal cut, and no custodian before this age had needed to write a law about men sickening below ground.
- <a id="ev-IV-0164"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 77** — *The huts of Cnoc gharbh* (Cnoc gharbh). After the sickness the people of Cnoc gharbh, who had worked the southern galleries, leave their camp huts and go back to the old village on the hill. The next year the Company builds the huts again and brings in crews from the west.
- <a id="ev-IV-0165"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *The first strike*. A whole mining settlement stops work for eleven days over conditions worsened by the plague two years before. The strike ends when the food, which the humans' Administration holds, runs out.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4001"><em>Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe</em>, 21 an Giblean, AE 77</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4002"><em>Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4010"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers* (Baile thais). A hewer's boy of seven, too young that year to be paid a man's wage, sets down his water-pail at the pit-mouth of Baile thais on the morning Catrìona nic Eachainn calls the halt, and stays through the yard's long quiet with the shift twice his age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0165"><em>The first strike</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, AE 77</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4002"><em>Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4011"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *The shrine women keep An Acair Uaine through the stoppage* (Baile thais). Through the eleven days no coal left Baile thais, the shrine women go on leaving dishes of meal on the mounds of An Acair Uaine where A' Phlàigh Uaine's dead were laid, finding a little to spare each day though A' Chompanaidh's store stood barer by the day beside them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0163"><em>Anne Colby's sick-houses</em>, 17 an Giblean, AE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4012"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona to end the stand* (Baile thais). On the tenth night of the stoppage, her bread gone and five children to feed, Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona nic Eachainn, plainly and without reproach, whether the crews should go back below rather than starve for galleries that would go on being worked regardless. Catrìona has no answer, and sits with her by the fire till morning.
- <a id="ev-IV-0166"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, AE 77** — *The strike at Baile thais* (Baile thais). The settlement was Baile thais, below Cill ghlas, and the crew-leader Catrìona nic Eachainn called the halt after the Company would not close the galleries where the Green Death had been worst. For eleven days no coal left the town. On the twelfth the Company's store, the only store, was empty.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4001"><em>Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe</em>, 21 an Giblean, AE 77</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4010"><em>Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers</em>, 15 an Dàmhair, AE 77</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4012"><em>Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona to end the stand</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, AE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0167"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, AE 78** — *The Company's granary* (Baile thais). After the strike the Company builds a granary of its own at Muileann chrom and forbids the camps to keep grain beyond a week's ration. The overseers enforce the order, and Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor signs it.
- <a id="ev-EV-4003"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, AE 78** — *Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage* (Baile thais). The custodian Sìneag writes in her rolls that she has never before read of a granary raised to answer a stoppage rather than a harvest, and sets the words down as they stand, without further comment, for whoever should read the roll after her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0167"><em>The Company's granary</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4013"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, AE 78** — *Dòmhnall Maor signs the granary order* (Muileann chrom). Within the month of the strike's end, Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, Steward at Muileann chrom, sets his mark to the order that forbids any camp household to keep more grain than a week's ration, the rest to be held under lock in A' Chompanaidh's new granary and drawn against a crew-leader's tally.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0167"><em>The Company's granary</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4014"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, AE 78** — *The overseers search the huts of Baile thais for hidden meal* (Baile thais). Enforcing the granary order with more zeal than it asks, the overseers at Baile thais search huts for grain kept back from the week's ration, and twice that autumn fine a household a day's wage for flour found under a bed, though in both cases the flour had come up from Ros gharbh by night and never passed A' Chompanaidh's scales.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0167"><em>The Company's granary</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4015"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, AE 78** — *Catrìona is given the surface work* (Baile thais). Before the winter after the stoppage is out, the seventh shift is given to a crew-leader loyal to Silas Crewe, and Catrìona nic Eachainn is set to sorting slate at the surface at half a hewer's pay, work she keeps eleven months before the sheds are said to have more hands than they need.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0166"><em>The strike at Baile thais</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 77</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0168"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, AE 79** — *Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh* (Ros gharbh). The fishermen of Ros gharbh carry salt fish up to the camps by night, past the Company's granary rule. The custodians' roll calls it the only trade of that decade that ran the right way.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4014"><em>The overseers search the huts of Baile thais for hidden meal</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4016"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, AE 79** — *Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). Turned off the sorting-sheds at Baile thais, Catrìona nic Eachainn walks first to Cnoc fhiadhaich and then to the timber camp beyond Àth ìseal asking for work, and is turned away at each gate before she has said her name twice, the agents already knowing her by sight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4015"><em>Catrìona is given the surface work</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4017"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, AE 79** — *Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar* (Baile thais).
