With her savings spent and refused work at every pit of A' Chompanaidh, Catrìona nic Eachainn takes what she owns and walks east from Baile thais over the hills to Muileann chiar, three days on foot, the black spoil of the coal country giving way at last to the grey of the silver town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4016"><em>Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0169"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, AE 79** — *Catrìona goes to the silver town* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Turned out of Baile thais and refused work at every Company pit, Catrìona nic Eachainn goes east to Muileann chiar, and the silver guild takes her on as a refiner. The Company asks that she be sent back. The guild's answer was filed and has not survived.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4016"><em>Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4017"><em>Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4018"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, AE 79** — *Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on* (Muileann chiar). Heard without interruption by the master of Comann an Airgid, Catrìona nic Eachainn's account of the stoppage at Baile thais is put to the guild's own hands rather than decided from above, and the hands vote by a wide margin to take her on as a refiner.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0169"><em>Catrìona goes to the silver town</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4017"><em>Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4019"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 79** — *A' Chompanaidh writes to Muileann chiar for Catrìona's return* (Muileann chiar). A' Chompanaidh's counting-house at Ros dhomhain writes to Comann an Airgid asking that Catrìona nic Eachainn, lately of Baile thais, be sent back to answer for the stoppage of two years before. The guild's clerk drafts an answer, read once in the guild hall and sent south; neither letter has survived.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0169"><em>Catrìona goes to the silver town</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, AE 79</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4018"><em>Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, AE 79</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0170"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, AE 80** — *The springs at Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The Administration builds a new bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh for its officers mending from fevers. Dia-thìrich who had bathed there for centuries are let in on certain days, and charged a penny.
- <a id="ev-EV-4004"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, AE 80** — *Three priests will not stand for the blessing* (Cathair dhearg). Three of the younger priests of Òrd Mhacha stand apart at the back of the temple hall rather than take their places for the blessing of the coin. Beathag Ruadh lets it pass unremarked before Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk, and tells Fearghas mac Mhuirich only that the order answers for the rite done rightly, not for the road a rightly blessed thing afterward walks.
- <a id="ev-EV-4020"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, AE 80** — *The order blesses Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's first coin* (Cathair dhearg). At Tolley's asking, Beathag Ruadh and the priests of Òrd Mhacha bless the new-struck coin in the temple at Cathair dhearg, naming both horses of the rite, Dubh Sainglenn and Liath Macha. Fearghas mac Mhuirich stands his place and says the words, though he watches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk carry the satchel out and finds he cannot say why the morning troubles him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4004"><em>Three priests will not stand for the blessing</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 80</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4021"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, AE 80** — *A penny at the door of Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The bath-house Riaghaltas nan Coigreach built at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh near Muileann ruadh opens to Dia-thìrich two days of the week, at a penny the door, for water the district had bathed in unasked since before any custodian's roll began. Catrìona nic Eachainn pays her penny and finds the water unchanged and only the door made new.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0170"><em>The springs at Muileann ruadh</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, AE 80</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 81 – 90

- <a id="ev-IV-0171"></a>**11 am Màrt, AE 81** — *Muileann chiar grows* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver town grows beside the coal workings, for the humans want both, and the digging goes faster than the old reverence would ever have allowed.
- <a id="ev-EV-4005"></a>**11 an Giblean, AE 81** — *Artair mac Iain seated after ten empty years* (Cathair dhearg). Comhairle a' Chùraim, unable to agree a head since Alasdair Liath's death, seats Artair mac Iain of the eastern shires as Ceann a' Chùraim, six-and-fifty years old, in the hall where Tormod mac Ailein once signed Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg. Fearghas mac Mhuirich says the order's blessing over him, both horses named.
- <a id="ev-EV-4022"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, AE 81** — *The guild raises a daughter town* (Muileann chiar). As Muileann chiar's lanes fill past holding, Comann an Airgid raises a second town a mile to the west for its carters and coal-breakers, under the old town's own name. The custodians' rolls thereafter call them the old town and the new, and do not always trouble to say which they mean.
- <a id="ev-IV-0172"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, AE 82** — *A second Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). The silver trade crowds the old town, and the guild settles its refiners and carters in the coal-breakers' mill town to the west, which is called by the silver town's name from then on. The rolls call them the old town and the new, and do not always say which they mean.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4022"><em>The guild raises a daughter town</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, AE 81</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4023"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, AE 82** — *The guild refuses A' Chompanaidh's price a third time* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). A' Chompanaidh asks a third time that Comann an Airgid sell at A' Chompanaidh's own price, naming a magistrate at Ros dhomhain who might rule the question. The seven refiners of the guild hall vote it down without one dissenting hand. Catrìona nic Eachainn, in the hall for the vote, counts it the one table on the island where the Dia-thìrich still set a price.
- <a id="ev-EV-4024"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, AE 82** — *The second cheapening cried at the market crosses* (Cathair dhearg). A crier of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir reads the second cheapening of the barter table at every market cross without a custodian's council having seen it beforehand. Word of it reaches Muileann chiar three days after Cathair dhearg, carried by a carter who had heard it cried at Baile Mòr fhionn.
- <a id="ev-EV-4025"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 82** — *The wool of Baile Mòr fhionn left to the moths* (Baile Mòr fhionn). Finding a fleece worth under the new table what half a fleece was worth before, the weavers of Baile Mòr fhionn stop bringing wool to the humans' market and load it for their own crossing instead. A' Chompanaidh, holding the only deep-water berths on that coast, refuses them the freight, and the wool sits two winters in the warehouses.
- <a id="ev-IV-0173"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, AE 83** — *Silver for marks* (Muileann chiar). The silver guild begins to sell bar silver to the Company for marks, at a price the guild sets. It is the only ware on Dia-thìr in this age priced by Dia-thìrich hands, and the guild's hall fills with human coin.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4023"><em>The guild refuses A' Chompanaidh's price a third time</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, AE 82</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4026"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, AE 83** — *Caol fhiadhaich sells eleven of its boats* (Caol fhiadhaich). Called for the first time in marks rather than in kind, the harbour dues at Caol fhiadhaich cannot be raised any way but by selling boats. Eleven of two-and-twenty go to A' Chompanaidh at its own asking price, and the men who sailed them go into the pits the following season under A' Chompanaidh's contracts.
- <a id="ev-IV-0174"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 84** — *Silversmiths at Muileann bhàn* (Muileann bhàn). Silversmiths settle at Muileann bhàn on the road to the silver town and live by working the guild's bar into ornaments for the humans' market. Theirs is the one Dia-thìreach craft sold in an Tìr Thall under a Dia-thìreach name.
- <a id="ev-EV-4027"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 84** — *The washing-women name nighean an rìgh* (Àth ìseal). At the stream below the camp of Àth ìseal, the eldest of the washing-women first says aloud what the wash-stones had for some seasons only thought: that a girl of the camp who does not age as other children age may be of the old line of kings, and names her nighean an rìgh. Most of the camp says they do not believe it and use the name anyway.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0146"><em>The first of the undying generation</em>, 7 am Màrt, AE 69</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0175"></a>**24 an Gearran, AE 85** — *Macha's priests bless the coin* (Cathair dhearg). At Tolley's asking the priests of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg, the order of the capital and the crown, bless the Residency's new coin. The priesthood of Macha teaches that the two horses of her rite, Dubh Sainglenn the black and Liath Macha the grey, each have their due; the dissenting priests say the coin is only one of them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4004"><em>Three priests will not stand for the blessing</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, AE 80</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4020"><em>The order blesses Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's first coin</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, AE 80</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4006"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, AE 85** — *Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided* (Cathair dhearg). Word of Fearghas mac Mhuirich's refusal reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir within the month. Tolley, near his own retiring, does not send for him; Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's letter-book records only that the order of Òrd Mhacha at the capital is divided on a religious nicety, and does not say what the nicety was.
- <a id="ev-EV-4028"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, AE 85** — *Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin* (Cathair dhearg). Asked to bless Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's larger second coin as the first was blessed, Fearghas mac Mhuirich, now eldest of the order at Cathair dhearg since Beathag Ruadh's death, tells the order he will not say the words, holding that a rite for a wheel cannot answer a road that turns only one way. None of the order says the words in his place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0175"><em>Macha's priests bless the coin</em>, 24 an Gearran, AE 85</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4006"><em>Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, AE 85</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0176"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, AE 86** — *The second change of coin*. The barter goods of the Dia-thìrich are marked down against the humans' coin a second time, on terms the humans' Administration alone sets.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4024"><em>The second cheapening cried at the market crosses</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, AE 82</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4006"><em>Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, AE 85</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4028"><em>Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, AE 85</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0177"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, AE 86** — *Wool marked down at Baile Mòr fhionn* (Baile Mòr fhionn). At Baile Mòr fhionn, where wool had been the measure of every bargain, a fleece is now worth by the Residency's table what a half-fleece was worth before. The town's weavers stop bringing wool to market and send it over the sea on their own account, until the Company refuses them freight.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4025"><em>The wool of Baile Mòr fhionn left to the moths</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 82</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0178"></a>**2 an Gearran, AE 87** — *The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold* (Caol fhiadhaich). The fishing fleet of Caol fhiadhaich, unable to pay the new harbour dues in marks, sells half its boats to the Company. The men who sailed them go into the pits under the next year's contracts.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4026"><em>Caol fhiadhaich sells eleven of its boats</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, AE 83</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0179"></a>**25 am Màrt, AE 87** — *The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Priests of Macha who refused the blessing leave the capital's temple and settle in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag. There they keep the older reading of Macha's two horses, and take in custodians who have lost their seats.
- <a id="ev-IV-0180"></a>**23 an Giblean, AE 87** — *Iain Maor* (Muileann chrom). Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor dies, and his son Iain takes the overseer's staff. Iain Maor is the first overseer schooled at the Mission; he keeps his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Dia-thìris.
- <a id="ev-EV-4029"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, AE 87** — *Dòmhnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, overseer of the coal country five-and-twenty years and signer of the granary order that stood against Catrìona nic Eachainn's strike, dies at Muileann chrom in his sixty-seventh year. Word reaches Muileann chiar by carter, and the guild hall names him a hard man gone before a harder trade going on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0180"><em>Iain Maor</em>, 23 an Giblean, AE 87</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0167"><em>The Company's granary</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, AE 78</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4030"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, AE 87** — *Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag* (Cathair dhearg). Fearghas mac Mhuirich walks north with eleven of the order who think as he does, to Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag. Griogair, eldest of those who stay at Cathair dhearg, walks with them as far as the north road and calls it two roads to the one rite rather than a falling-out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0179"><em>The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag</em>, 25 am Màrt, AE 87</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4031"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, AE 87** — *The dissenters' first fire under the oaks* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Custodians without seats and priests without a temple begin to gather at the forest of Cnoc bheag through the summer, until the grove holds near as many of one kind as the other. On the last evening of the spring Fearghas mac Mhuirich lights Teine a' Chlachair there and says the rite of the two horses whole.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0179"><em>The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag</em>, 25 am Màrt, AE 87</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4030"><em>Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, AE 87</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0181"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, AE 88** — *The Levy* (Ros dhomhain). Tolley issues an ordinance, the Levy, by which every farming village in the west and north must send one in five of its able grown folk to the pits for two years. The villages are paid in marks, at the new rate.
- <a id="ev-IV-0182"></a>**3 am Màrt, AE 88** — *Levy officers at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). The Levy's officers take their first tally at Caol mhòr in the north-west, reading the names of the chosen from a list in the humans' tongue. The custodians of the town write the names again in Dia-thìris, that they may know whom to look for.
- <a id="ev-IV-0183"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88** — *The Levy in the north-west* (Muileann àrsaidh). The Levy falls hardest on the villages about Baile chrom and the northern concession, which had never sent crews to the pits. The Dia-thìrich of the concession are taken; its human farmers are spared.
- <a id="ev-EV-4007"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88** — *An Togail read at Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). An Togail's officers read their list at Cnoc thais, and the mason Dùghall Clachair hears his own name and his whole crew's called for the pits. Two days into the eastward march they are turned out instead to the headland at Baile chrom, where the fifth and last coast beacon is begun.
- <a id="ev-EV-4032"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88** — *The wrong son taken at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). A guessed name is matched to the wrong face at Caol mhòr's reading, and a son is marched a day's walk east before the error is found. The right man is fetched in his place; the officers' own tally and the town's roll never afterward agree by one head.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0182"><em>Levy officers at Caol mhòr</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 88</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4033"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88** — *The concession's human farmers spared An Togail* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the northern concession An Togail falls on every Dia-thìreach household while Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's own leaseholders pay nothing, the officers' list giving the reason that the concession's tenants answer to Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's leave alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0183"><em>The Levy in the north-west</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0184"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 89** — *Baile ìseal sends its people* (Baile ìseal). Baile ìseal sends forty-one of its people to the pits under the Levy, and nineteen come back when their term ends. The custodians' roll names the other twenty-two and the camps they were sent to.
- <a id="ev-IV-0185"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89** — *Muileann naomh buys its way out* (Muileann naomh). The custodians of Muileann naomh pay the Levy's officers in silver to halve the town's tally. The officers take the silver and the whole tally. The complaint is lodged at the Residency and filed.
- <a id="ev-IV-0186"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89** — *The druid school's hall shut* (Dùn thais). George Tolley shuts the hall of the druid school at Dùn thais over a lecture on whether the humans' blindness to the coal's colour is a kind of sickness. The masters go on teaching in their own houses, to smaller rooms each year.
- <a id="ev-EV-4008"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89** — *A gale strips the beacon's scaffold* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). A two-day gale out of the north-west tears the scaffolding from the third course of the rising tower at Baile chrom. Dùghall Clachair climbs the bare walls alone in the wind to judge whether the stone has shifted; it has not.
- <a id="ev-IV-0187"></a>**30 an Giblean, AE 90** — *The last disputation at Doire chiar* (Doire chiar). At Doire chiar, a village of the druid schools north of the eastern workings, the masters hold the last open disputation of the school on the eve of Bealltainn, in the open air on the village threshing-floor. Its matter is whether a question may be forbidden. The Administration's clerk who attends writes that it may.
- <a id="ev-IV-0188"></a>**15 an t-Ògmhios, AE 90** — *Teaching in the sacred forest* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Druid masters who may no longer teach in a hall begin to teach under the trees in the sacred forest of Flidais near Muileann chiar, where the Administration has no building to shut.
- <a id="ev-IV-0189"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, AE 90** — *Building the last beacon at Baile chrom* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). Work begins on the fifth and last beacon, on the north-western headland at Baile chrom, with masons taken by the Levy from the very villages whose fields they leave untilled.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4007"><em>An Togail read at Cnoc thais</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4008"><em>A gale strips the beacon's scaffold</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4009"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, AE 90** — *Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). Uisdean mac Lachlainn of the headland villages is named the beacon's first keeper, on the recommendation of the very masons who built it: Dùghall Clachair among them, who signed the letter along with two of his crew.

## The Years AE 91 – 100

- <a id="ev-IV-0190"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, AE 91** — *The masons of Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). The Levy takes the masons of Cnoc thais to build the beacon at Baile chrom. Their foreman, Dùghall Clachair, cuts the names of his crew into the lintel of the lamp-room, the only writing on any of the five towers.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4007"><em>An Togail read at Cnoc thais</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 88</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0191"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, AE 91** — *The five beacons complete* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The ring of coast beacons is finished: Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Baile ìseal, Muileann bheag, Àth dhearg and Tobar dhearg. They serve a trade that is by now plunder in all but name.
- <a id="ev-IV-0192"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, AE 91** — *Cuan ruadh loses its trade* (Cuan ruadh). The ring of beacons finished, the Company's steamers round the island without putting in, and within a few years the old coasting trade of Cuan ruadh up and down the eastern shore dies.
- <a id="ev-IV-0193"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, AE 91** — *Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The beacon at Baile chrom is lit with a coal flame, and the ring is whole. The Company's ships can now round the island by night, and the keepers' daybooks show the sailings doubled within a few years.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4009"><em>Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, AE 90</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4034"></a>**7 an Cèitean, AE 92** — *The draft read at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). An Togail is read at the market cross of Baile chrom, first in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris by a clerk who stumbles over the numbers. It falls hardest on the coast and hill villages; the concession farms to the north, worked by the strangers' own people, send no one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0181"><em>The Levy</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, AE 88</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0194"></a>**3 am Màrt, AE 94** — *Gorta Baile chrom*. The Great Hunger follows a failed harvest across thirty-four settlements, made worse because the Levy has taken so many to the pits that too few are left to till the land.
- <a id="ev-EV-4501"></a>**9 am Màrt, AE 94** — *The first harvest short* (Baile chrom). The harvest round Baile chrom comes in at less than half the carts of the year before, the fields sown thin for want of hands and beaten further by two summer storms. Uisdean counts the carts against his own earlier tally and finds the shortfall for himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0194"><em>Gorta Baile chrom</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 94</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0195"></a>**1 an Giblean, AE 94** — *Baile chrom goes hungry* (Baile chrom). The hunger is worst at Baile chrom itself, whose people could see the new beacon from their empty fields. The custodians write that more died there than anywhere else, and the Administration, which kept its own count, does not gainsay them.
- <a id="ev-IV-0195a"></a>**22 an Cèitean, AE 94** — *The famine country* (Gorta Baile chrom). The custodians' roll draws the bounds of the famine country along the north-west shore and the hills behind it. Within them lie Baile chrom in its own shire; Ceann mhòr, Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg in the shire of Ceann mhòr; Muileann àrsaidh in the shire of Cnoc thais; and Achadh àrsaidh in the shire of Muileann àrsaidh. Thirty-four settlements are counted within the line, and the roll gives the dead of each.
- <a id="ev-EV-4502"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, AE 94** — *Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather* (Baile chrom). In his second spring keeping the daybook of Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Uisdean mac Lachlainn writes down more than the wind and the oil for the first time: that a farmer of his acquaintance ploughs alone, with none of the hands who worked beside him the year before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0193"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit</em>, 22 an t-Sultain, AE 91</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0194"><em>Gorta Baile chrom</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 94</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0196"></a>**30 an Giblean, AE 95** — *The hunger at Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). At Doire ghlas in the north the hunger takes the old and the very young first. The village sends its young folk to the camps for the Company's rations, and by the year's end it is half empty.
- <a id="ev-IV-0197"></a>**29 an Cèitean, AE 95** — *Inis mhin eats its seed* (Inis mhin). In the second winter of the hunger the townsfolk of Inis mhin on the north coast eat their seed corn. The Mission kitchen at the harbour feeds three hundred a day for a season.
- <a id="ev-EV-4513"></a>**12 an t-Ògmhios, AE 95** — *Mòr nic Aonghais sends her son south* (Doire ghlas). At Doire ghlas, a woman named Mòr nic Aonghais walks her fourteen-year-old son as far as the boundary stone and no further, by the coast's custom, and sends him to the camps for A' Chompanaidh's ration rather than keep him at a table with too little on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0196"><em>The hunger at Doire ghlas</em>, 30 an Giblean, AE 95</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4514"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, AE 95** — *The kitchen at Inis mhin's harbour* (Inis mhin). With its seed corn eaten and no crop sown, Inis mhin is fed through the second winter of the hunger by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's kitchen at the harbour, which serves three hundred a day on fish broth and biscuit brought by sea from Cathair gheal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0197"><em>Inis mhin eats its seed</em>, 29 an Cèitean, AE 95</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4515"></a>**1 an Dàmhair, AE 95** — *Anne Colby's letter to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir* (Ros dhomhain). With the relief ship idle at anchor, Anne Colby writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain asking only who should be told to unload it. Eleven days pass before an answer that names no one and settles nothing, noting only that Àrd-mhaor Tolley has heard her concern.
- <a id="ev-EV-4516"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, AE 95** — *The relief ship unloaded without an order* (Ros dhomhain). After a month idle in the roads at Ros dhomhain, the relief ship's holds are opened at last when a clerk of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and a clerk of A' Chompanaidh set men to the work themselves, without waiting for either office to settle the dispute between them.
- <a id="ev-EV-4517"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 95** — *Anne Colby takes the kitchen at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). Anne Colby goes north to Baile chrom to run Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's kitchen in a net-shed by the harbour, and keeps it through the worst of the hunger on the relief ship's grain and whatever the boats can add to it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0198"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, AE 96** — *The hunger reaches Seann Bhrenn* (Seann Bhrenn). The hunger reaches as far east as Seann Bhrenn, where the custodians open the old grain-pits of the Holy Age, unfilled in living memory. They hold only dust.
- <a id="ev-IV-0199"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96** — *The relief ship* (Ros dhomhain). A relief ship with grain from an Tìr Thall lies a month at Ros dhomhain while the Residency and the Company dispute who shall pay for its unloading. Meanwhile the Mission opens kitchens at Cathair gheal and Baile chrom, and Anne Colby, come back to the island, keeps the one at Baile chrom.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4515"><em>Anne Colby's letter to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir</em>, 1 an Dàmhair, AE 95</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4516"><em>The relief ship unloaded without an order</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 95</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4517"><em>Anne Colby takes the kitchen at Baile chrom</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 95</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4503"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96** — *Uisdean's hand on the valve* (Baile chrom). In the second winter of the hunger, Uisdean mac Lachlainn climbs to the lamp of Taigh-solais Baile chrom and stands a long while with his hand on the oil valve, weighing whether to let the light fail. He writes the thought into the daybook and lets the lamp burn on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0193"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit</em>, 22 an t-Sultain, AE 91</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4518"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96** — *Anne Colby's private roll of names* (Baile chrom). At the Baile chrom kitchen Anne Colby keeps a book of her own, apart from Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's, writing every name she feeds and crossing it through, gently, in the corner of the page, whenever that person does not come again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0199"><em>The relief ship</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4503"><em>Uisdean's hand on the valve</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0200"></a>**20 an Gearran, AE 97** — *The Levy set aside* (Baile chrom). The Levy is set aside in the famine districts, too late for the harvest. It is not repealed. The custodians note that it was never used again, nor needed to be, for the villages had learned what it meant.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4503"><em>Uisdean's hand on the valve</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0201"></a>**17 an Lùnastal, AE 97** — *Cnoc mhòr walks south* (Cnoc mhòr). Rather than starve, the families of Cnoc mhòr in the north walk south to the camps and take work under the Company. Their village stands empty for a generation.
- <a id="ev-EV-4519"></a>**26 an Lùnastal, AE 97** — *An Togail read ended at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). The clerk who first read An Togail at the market cross of Baile chrom returns to read that it is set aside in the famine districts, two harvests after the failure it caused. The custodians note it is not repealed, only set by, and expect no more of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0200"><em>The Levy set aside</em>, 20 an Gearran, AE 97</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4518"><em>Anne Colby's private roll of names</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 96</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4520"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 97** — *The grass in Cnoc mhòr's street* (Cnoc mhòr). A carter passing through empty Cnoc mhòr some weeks after its people leave finds every door shut but unbarred, and grass already coming up between the stones of the street, a sign that reaches the kitchen at Baile chrom before the village itself is spoken of again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0201"><em>Cnoc mhòr walks south</em>, 17 an Lùnastal, AE 97</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0202"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, AE 98** — *Robert Haskins Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). George Tolley retires with honours. Robert Haskins, who follows him, orders that the custodians' council be consulted on the tithe, and then sets the tithe before the council has met.
- <a id="ev-EV-4521"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, AE 98** — *Word of Tolley's retiral reaches Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). A carter brings Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, the worn word that George Tolley is going home with honours and that Robert Haskins, who follows him, means to ask the custodians' council its mind before he sets anything down. Peigi trims the shrine lamp and tells the flame, not the carter, what three such promises have been worth before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0202"><em>Robert Haskins Commissioner</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, AE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0203"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, AE 98** — *Customs at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Haskins opens a customs house at Seann Dunn on the eastern coast, and a Company store with it. The store sells the east its seed and its tools, and within a few years its ledgers hold the debts of half the district.
- <a id="ev-EV-4504"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, AE 98** — *The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). Custodians of nineteen settlements come in to Ceann àrsaidh through am Faoilleach, on foot and by cart, and camp along the inside of the town wall while they wait for the last of their number. Peigi Ghlas of Cill ghlas walks it in two days, carrying her cloak and her village's slate of An Togail's and the famine's dead rolled with it.
- <a id="ev-EV-4522"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 98** — *Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east* (Ceann àrsaidh). Once the tithe goes up on A' Chompanaidh's boards before any custodian's answer has reached Ros dhomhain, Aonghas Ruadh of Ceann àrsaidh sends riders to the settlements of the east and the hills, naming a day in am Faoilleach to draw up one grievance in one hand rather than let it be filed apart, settlement by settlement, as every single letter before it had been.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0202"><em>Robert Haskins Commissioner</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, AE 98</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4504"><em>The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, AE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4523"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 98** — *Coinneach Òg tells of the store's ledgers at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). At a fire inside the wall of Ceann àrsaidh, Coinneach Òg of the eastern coast tells the gathered custodians how A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn, opened as help against a bad year, now holds the debts of near half his district, entered against named households, and grows no smaller in any year, only more slowly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0203"><em>Customs at Seann Dunn</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, AE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0204"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, AE 99** — *The first petition*. For the first time the custodians of the Dia-thìrich act together, and not settlement by settlement, and lay a written grievance before the humans' Administration. It is not answered.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4504"><em>The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, AE 98</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4522"><em>Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4524"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 99** — *The drafting argued over three days* (Ceann àrsaidh). In the hall behind the market square at Ceann àrsaidh the nineteen custodians argue three days over how to set their grievance down. An old custodian of the hills wants every death named; Aonghas Ruadh argues for one plain page that might be read where a long roll would only be filed. The shorter paper carries, and the old man signs it all the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0204"><em>The first petition</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, AE 99</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4523"><em>Coinneach Òg tells of the store's ledgers at Seann Dunn</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 98</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0205"></a>**3 am Màrt, AE 99** — *The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). The petition was drawn up at Ceann àrsaidh by custodians of nineteen settlements, meeting for the first time as one body. Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, carried it to the Residency and handed it to a clerk.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4504"><em>The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, AE 98</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-4524"><em>The drafting argued over three days</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4505"></a>**6 an Cèitean, AE 99** — *Peigi Ghlas at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir* (Ros dhomhain). Peigi Ghlas carries the fair copy of the nineteen settlements' petition to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain, is turned back twice at the gate, and on the third day is shown into a stone passage smelling of lamp-soot to wait on a worn bench before a young clerk takes the paper, thanks her, and lays it on an unremarkable pile.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0205"><em>The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4506"></a>**24 an Cèitean, AE 99** — *Aonghas Ruadh's letters go unanswered* (Ceann àrsaidh). Through the year after the petition is filed, Aonghas Ruadh writes twice more to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir asking only whether the paper of am Faoilleach was received and read. The first letter gets no reply at all; the second, in the autumn, is answered in a strange clerk's hand that the matter remains under consideration.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0205"><em>The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4525"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, AE 99** — *Two days on the bench in the lamp-soot passage* (Ros dhomhain). Before the clerk receives her, Peigi Ghlas is turned back at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's gate once and kept waiting a second day in a yard and a windowless passage, on a stone bench worn pale in the middle by everyone who has sat there before her, with the boy of Ceann àrsaidh who carries the second copy standing at her shoulder.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0205"><em>The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4526"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, AE 99** — *Three more names cut into the slate at Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). In the year the petition waits unanswered, Peigi Ghlas adds three more names to the slate she keeps by the shrine door: two of a fall of stone at Baile thais, and an old hewer of Cill ghlas who does not come up from the gallery one evening in an t-Sultain, of nothing but the going down itself, done too many years too many times.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0205"><em>The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 99</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4525"><em>Two days on the bench in the lamp-soot passage</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4527"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, AE 99** — *Peigi Ghlas trims Brìde's lamp at the year's end* (Cill ghlas). On a frost-still evening near the close of an Dùbhlachd, with no answer yet come from Ros dhomhain, Peigi Ghlas climbs to the shrine at Cill ghlas and trims the flame called Brìde's square and clean, as she does every evening of her life, the one thing no clerk's pile can take out of her hands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0205"><em>The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 3 am Màrt, AE 99</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4526"><em>Three more names cut into the slate at Cill ghlas</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, AE 99</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0206"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 99** — *Àth fhionn signs* (Àth fhionn). Ruairidh mac Thormoid, custodian of Àth fhionn in the south-east, is the eldest of those who signed the petition. He was born before the humans' coin was struck, and says so beside his name.
- <a id="ev-EV-4528"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 99** — *Ruairidh mac Thormoid writes 'born before the coin'* (Ceann àrsaidh). Ruairidh mac Thormoid of Àth fhionn, who walked to Ceann àrsaidh on his own feet and remembers, by his own count, a world before the mark was struck, signs the petition last and slowest, and adds beside his name the only line any of the nineteen thought to add: born before the coin.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0206"><em>Àth fhionn signs</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 99</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 101 – 110

- <a id="ev-IV-0207"></a>**27 am Faoilleach, AE 101** — *Grievance first written*. From these years come the oldest writings of grievance among the Dia-thìrich that survive. No hand is yet raised in them; yet in them it is first written that something has gone wrong.
- <a id="ev-IV-0208"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, AE 101** — *Leabhar Baile thais* (Baile thais). The oldest of them is a book of complaints kept at Baile thais, set down by many hands over some years: wages, deaths, the granary, the stream at Doire mhòr. The custodians' copyists call it Leabhar Baile thais.
- <a id="ev-EV-4507"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, AE 101** — *Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it* (Muileann dhearg). Old Griogair mac Aonghais, who broke coal beside Fearchar's father before him, tells Fearchar that a column is for men who have given up hoping to be heard, and that he should sing the grievance instead of writing it. Fearchar carries the book back to Baile thais and begins working verses to the granary's short week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0208"><em>Leabhar Baile thais</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, AE 101</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4529"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, AE 101** — *Fearchar sits two nights over Leabhar Baile thais* (Muileann dhearg). A copy of the grievance book reaches Muileann dhearg folded in a meal-sack, and Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at the belt since boyhood, reads it by tallow light two nights running. He finds he can put nothing of his own into its columns, though he knows the granary's short week and the stream at Doire mhòr as well as any hand that wrote there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0208"><em>Leabhar Baile thais</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, AE 101</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4507"><em>Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it</em>, 24 an Dàmhair, AE 101</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0209"></a>**17 am Faoilleach, AE 102** — *The songs of Fearchar Bàrd* (Muileann dhearg). The poet Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at Muileann dhearg since boyhood, makes songs of the Levy and the famine, and they are sung in the camps. The overseers forbid them, and because they were forbidden several were written down.
- <a id="ev-IV-0210"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102** — *Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). The songs of Fearchar Bàrd are sung in the roadside houses of the east, and An Taigh-òsta Grianach becomes known for them. The Company's carters sing them too, the keeper writes, not always knowing what they sing.
- <a id="ev-EV-4508"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102** — *Fearchar repays the docked wage* (Baile thais). Fearchar Bàrd walks to Baile thais to repay out of his own wage the boy docked half a week's pay for singing his song, and the boy refuses the coin, saying he would rather have sung it than not. The song is sung again within the week, further than before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0209"><em>The songs of Fearchar Bàrd</em>, 17 am Faoilleach, AE 102</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4530"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102** — *Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth* (Muileann dhearg). Fearchar Bàrd sings his first finished song, four verses on An Togail and the famine, at the pit-mouth of Muileann dhearg while the crews wait out a stopped winding-gear. It is carried to Baile thais within the month by crews he never asked to carry it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0209"><em>The songs of Fearchar Bàrd</em>, 17 am Faoilleach, AE 102</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4508"><em>Fearchar repays the docked wage</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4531"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102** — *The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song* (Baile thais). An overseer at Baile thais has Fearchar's song taken down word for word from a boy of the crews so that it can be shown forbidden, and a docker's pay is cut by half a week for the singing of it. The clerk's copy, made to condemn the song, becomes the only complete written record of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0209"><em>The songs of Fearchar Bàrd</em>, 17 am Faoilleach, AE 102</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4530"><em>Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0211"></a>**15 an Gearran, AE 103** — *The Company's deep-water quay* (Ros dhomhain). The Company builds at Ros dhomhain a deep-water quay for the new iron steamships, which burn the island's own coal to carry it away. Fearchar Bàrd makes a song of that, the most quoted of all his songs.
- <a id="ev-IV-0212"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, AE 103** — *The deep quay at Ceann chaol* (Ceann chaol). A second deep-water quay is built at Ceann chaol in the south-east for the eastern coal. Its builders are brought from the coast, and the village of forty houses becomes a town of four hundred.
- <a id="ev-EV-4532"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 103** — *Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). Riding east on Comann an Airgid's business, Fearchar Bàrd sits unknown at An Taigh-òsta Grianach and hears six carters of A' Chompanaidh sing his granary song through, missing a line they cannot remember. He says nothing of whose it is, and finds the mis-singing harder to bear than the forbidding had been.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0210"><em>Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4531"><em>The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 102</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0213"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, AE 104** — *Baile thais walls its pithead* (Baile thais). The Company rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a gate, and pays a watchman to count who goes in. It is the first working on Dia-thìr walled against its own crews.
- <a id="ev-IV-0214"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town* (Baile thais). Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at Muileann chiar, a refiner of the silver guild to the end. The camp folk of Baile thais send men to her burying, and the Company docks each of them a day's pay.
- <a id="ev-EV-4533"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Fearchar Bàrd, at Ros dhomhain on Comann an Airgid's errand, watches A' Chompanaidh's first iron steamship take on coal through the night at the new deep-water quay, burning the island's own fuel to carry the rest away. He stands at the rail until past midnight, watching the loading by lamplight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0211"><em>The Company's deep-water quay</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 103</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4532"><em>Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 103</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4534"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *Fearchar makes the ship song* (Ros dhomhain). That same night, sitting on the new quay's coiled rope, Fearchar Bàrd makes the song of the ship that eats the hill to carry the hill away, the most quoted of all his songs. He sings it first to the loading gang he stood beside, too tired themselves to do more than nod.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0211"><em>The Company's deep-water quay</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 103</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4533"><em>The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4535"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *The wall rises at Baile thais* (Baile thais). A' Chompanaidh rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a single gate through the summer, and sets a lamed former hewer to keep the tally-book at the gate. Fearchar Bàrd, home from Ros dhomhain, walks the wall's length and makes no song of it that year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0213"><em>Baile thais walls its pithead</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, AE 104</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4534"><em>Fearchar makes the ship song</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4536"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104** — *Fearchar makes Catrìona's lament* (Muileann chiar). On the walk home from Muileann chiar, Fearchar Bàrd makes the lament for Catrìona nic Eachainn, naming the coal-tub and the empty shelves she counted and the guild's bench where she stood to the end, and ending it, as her life had ended, without complaint. The dozen who had known her weep at it on the road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0214"><em>Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4535"><em>The wall rises at Baile thais</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 104</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0215"></a>**4 an Giblean, AE 105** — *The quay fire* (Ros dhomhain). A fire starts in the Company's coal sheds at Ros dhomhain and burns three days, taking two streets of the harbour quarter with it. The Company's inquiry finds no cause; the harbour quarter's own account has several.
- <a id="ev-IV-0216"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, AE 105** — *The council without a high custodian* (Cathair dhearg). After the death of the last high custodian the Council of Custodians cannot agree on another, and sits for years with the seat empty. Robert Haskins writes to an Tìr Thall that this makes the council easier to deal with.
- <a id="ev-EV-4509"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, AE 105** — *Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Artair mac Iain, Ceann a' Chùraim for twenty and four years, dies at Cathair dhearg at eighty years old. Word of his death reaches Fearchar Bàrd on the road home from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, carried faster than either fire or song by a rider changing horses at every post-house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0216"><em>The council without a high custodian</em>, 22 an t-Sultain, AE 105</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4537"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 105** — *The carters sing the ship song for their own quay* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). At An Taigh-òsta Grianach, Fearchar Bàrd hears the fire-ship's carters sing his ship song louder and rougher than before, now that their own quay has burned, though none of them know the song or its maker. He sits again unknown, and does not tell them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0211"><em>The Company's deep-water quay</em>, 15 an Gearran, AE 103</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0215"><em>The quay fire</em>, 4 an Giblean, AE 105</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-4509"><em>Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, AE 105</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0217"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, AE 106** — *Tiormachd Achadh shean*. The Long Drought lies on the island's dry season three years together, and bears hard on a people already worn thin by the tallies of the pits.
- <a id="ev-EV-4538"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, AE 106** — *Iseabail begins her forty pages* (Àth mhòr). Understanding that her petition will be answered with nothing but the words under consideration, Iseabail nic Leòid begins writing, over a winter, a full account of the drought's three years: the wells, the cattle, the fever's dead, the watchman recalled from Allt an Àigh, for whoever may someday want to know its cost.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0218"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 107** — *The wells of Achadh shean* (Achadh shean). At Achadh shean, whose name the drought bears, the wells fail in the second summer, and the cattle are driven west in a column the roll calls a day long. Fewer than half reach water.
- <a id="ev-IV-0219"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, AE 107** — *The dry country* (Tiormachd Achadh shean). The custodians' roll counts ten districts of the east as drought country, worst at Achadh shean, Àth uaine, Achadh àrsaidh and Muileann chiar, and reaching down to Cuan ruadh and west toward Baile chaol. The Administration keeps no count of its own.
- <a id="ev-IV-0220"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, AE 107** — *The cattle of Baile chaol* (Baile chaol). At Baile chaol the herds are slaughtered in the second summer of the drought, rather than watched as they die. The salt meat is sold to the Company for the camps, at a price the Company names.
- <a id="ev-IV-0221"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, AE 107** — *Doire fhionn walks for water* (Doire fhionn). At Doire fhionn in the east the women walk each day to the spring at Àth ruadh and back for water, half a day's journey. The custodians record it for the three dry years, and then cease.
- <a id="ev-EV-4510"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, AE 107** — *Baile chaol slaughters its herd* (Baile chaol). With no grazing left within four days' driving, Baile chaol's custodian Ealasaid Ruadh orders the town's whole herd killed and the meat salted rather than risk the loss of it on the road. The town loses fewer of its people to hunger that winter than any other of the ten drought districts.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4539"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, AE 107** — *Iseabail drives Àth mhòr's beasts west and counts the dead* (Àth mhòr). Iseabail nic Leòid leads the herds of Àth mhòr and Achadh shean on a day-long drive west to the tarn above Doire fhionn. Fewer than half the beasts reach water on their own legs; she keeps a private count of the fallen, ninety-eight marks by the drive's end, and of the eleven calves among them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0222"></a>**1 an Cèitean, AE 108** — *Pilgrims at Allt an Àigh* (Allt an Àigh). The spring of Allt an Àigh, said never to have failed, runs on through all three dry years. Pilgrims who keep Na Seann Spioradan come to it from all the east, the first of them at Bealltainn, and the Administration sets a watchman to charge them for the water. He is called back after one season.
- <a id="ev-IV-0223"></a>**30 an Cèitean, AE 108** — *The pilgrims' road at Inis uaine* (Inis uaine). Pilgrims bound for Allt an Àigh gather at Inis uaine, and the townsfolk feed them freely, as the Old Spirits require. The town's own wells are low, and it gives away more water than it keeps.
- <a id="ev-EV-4540"></a>**17 an t-Iuchar, AE 108** — *Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's watchman recalled from Allt an Àigh* (Allt an Àigh). Riaghaltas nan Coigreach posts a watchman at Allt an Àigh to charge a set rate for the water. He is refused by an old woman of Achadh àrsaidh who will not pay a stranger for water that has run free since before his people came, and is called back before the season is out; the spring's keepers enter the word restored under his going.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4541"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, AE 108** — *Achadh chaol's households go down to the pits* (Achadh chaol). With its grazing gone two years running, Achadh chaol sends its young to sign hewers' contracts at Cnoc fhiadhaich and elsewhere in numbers its custodian has never before had to record, families who had kept beasts and small fields for generations going down into the galleries for a wage that a dry year cannot touch.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0224"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 109** — *Drought-fever at Baile Mòr ruadh* (Baile Mòr ruadh). A fever of foul water follows the drought into the towns, worst at Baile Mòr ruadh, where the wells had been deepened into the old middens. Seventeen die. The Mission's report is the first to name the cause rightly.
- <a id="ev-IV-0225"></a>**3 an Cèitean, AE 109** — *The fever at Cnoc shean* (Cnoc shean). The drought-fever spreads to Cnoc shean, whose one well is found tainted. The custodians close it, and for a year the town drinks from carts.
- <a id="ev-IV-0226"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, AE 109** — *The Mission's wells* (Achadh shean). The Mission sinks deep wells at Achadh shean and Àth chrom with a boring-rig brought from an Tìr Thall, and they hold. The custodians of the east set down the Mission's wells and the Company's tallies on facing pages, without comment.
- <a id="ev-EV-4511"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, AE 109** — *Coll's report names the drought-fever's true cause* (Baile Mòr ruadh). Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's physician at Baile Mòr ruadh, a young man named Coll, tests the town's water and finds it fouled by the old midden ground its deep wells were sunk through. His report to Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's house at Cathair dhearg is the first that autumn to name the fever's cause rightly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4512"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, AE 109** — *Every custodian of the drought country petitions Haskins* (Àth mhòr). Each of the ten drought districts' custodians petitions Àrd-mhaor Haskins in her own hand, unknown to the others, asking that A' Chompanaidh's quota be set aside until two seasons of ordinary rain are counted. Iseabail nic Leòid rides her own petition to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and is told, as every other has been told, that the matter is under consideration.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-4542"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, AE 109** — *Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise bores wells that hold at Achadh shean and Àth chrom* (Achadh shean). Following Coll's report, Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise bores new wells at Achadh shean and Àth chrom, dug deep and clean of old ground. The wells hold, and the drought-fever does not follow them; the custodians of the drought country begin entering Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's wells and A' Chompanaidh's unmoved quota on facing pages of their rolls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0227"></a>**16 am Màrt, AE 110** — *Achadh chaol goes to the pits* (Achadh chaol). Their fields burned out by the drought, the people of Achadh chaol in the north-east go to the pits for wages, the first villagers of the eastern farm country to do so. Their custodian writes it down as the end of the village, not a flitting.
- <a id="ev-IV-0228"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, AE 110** — *The tally not lowered* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). The coal tally is not lowered in the drought. The custodians of the east, their joint petition unanswered, each write to Haskins alone; to each he answers that the matter is under consideration.
- <a id="ev-EV-4543"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, AE 110** — *Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's rig strikes water at Achadh shean* (Achadh shean). A third well bored by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's rig on the moor above Achadh shean strikes clean, running water deeper than any well the drought country has dug, marking the drought's end there. Iseabail nic Leòid rides out to see it and adds the day to her forty pages.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0217"><em>Tiormachd Achadh shean</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 106</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 111 – 120

- <a id="ev-IV-0229"></a>**3 an Gearran, AE 111** — *The petition of Àth mhòr* (Àth mhòr). Iseabail nic Leòid, custodian of Àth mhòr, writes the longest of the single petitions, forty pages listing her town's dead beasts. Haskins answers in two lines. Both survive, bound together by a later clerk.
- <a id="ev-EV-5010"></a>**9 an Gearran, AE 111** — *A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting* (Baile dhìreach). A' Chompanaidh's surveyors, working out a new gallery above Baile dhìreach, mark the narrow customary cutting held by Eilidh nic Ruairidh's line for four generations. The agent Pryce offers Thomas Hale a small sum to sign it over rather than test A' Chompanaidh's claim.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0229"><em>The petition of Àth mhòr</em>, 3 an Gearran, AE 111</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5011"></a>**10 an Gearran, AE 111** — *Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain* (Baile dhìreach). Thomas Hale walks the three days from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and files a claim at A' Chompanaidh's court, a copy of his grandmother's marriage roll in his coat and no other paper. The clerk gives a hearing date a full season off, at the back of the court's list.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5010"><em>A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting</em>, 9 an Gearran, AE 111</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5012"></a>**11 an Gearran, AE 111** — *Mairead nic Aoidh copies the marriage roll* (Baile dhìreach). The custodian of Baile dhìreach copies, under her own seal, the roll's page of the second year recording the marriage of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale in two tongues, so that Thomas Hale may carry proof of the line to A' Chompanaidh's court.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5011"><em>Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain</em>, 10 an Gearran, AE 111</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0230"></a>**15 an Gearran, AE 111** — *The first inheritance of mixed blood*. A suit over whether the grandchild of a marriage between a Dia-thìreach and a human may inherit the customary rights of mining is decided, and the Administration makes the ruling wholly to its own gain.
- <a id="ev-IV-0231"></a>**4 am Màrt, AE 111** — *The case of Thomas Hale* (Ros dhomhain). The child was Thomas Hale, grandson of the marriage at Baile dhìreach of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale, who claimed a share in a customary cutting through his Dia-thìrich grandmother. Oliver Dunstan, magistrate at Ros dhomhain, ruled that customary rights descend only through the line the Administration owns, and that it owns only its own.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5010"><em>A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting</em>, 9 an Gearran, AE 111</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5011"><em>Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain</em>, 10 an Gearran, AE 111</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5012"><em>Mairead nic Aoidh copies the marriage roll</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 111</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5013"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, AE 111** — *Dunstan's ruling read at A' Chompanaidh's counter* (Ros dhomhain). Oliver Dunstan's ruling against Thomas Hale is posted at the Ros dhomhain counter among a dozen others of the same list. It holds that no marriage entered in a custodian's roll, however old, creates a line Riaghaltas nan Coigreach recognises, and confirms the cutting to A' Chompanaidh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0231"><em>The case of Thomas Hale</em>, 4 am Màrt, AE 111</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5012"><em>Mairead nic Aoidh copies the marriage roll</em>, 11 an Gearran, AE 111</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0232"></a>**2 an Giblean, AE 112** — *Dunstan's rule applied* (Ros dhomhain). Within a few years Dunstan's ruling is used to pass eleven customary cuttings to the Company, each because some holder in the line had married a human or been born of one. The custodians stop entering such marriages in the roll.
- <a id="ev-EV-5001"></a>**19 an Giblean, AE 112** — *Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll* (Baile dhìreach). The custodian of Baile dhìreach ceases to enter marriages between Dia-thìrich and humans in her roll, judging that under Riaghailt Dunstan such an entry has become a paper a family's enemies may use against it rather than one that protects anything.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0232"><em>Dunstan's rule applied</em>, 2 an Giblean, AE 112</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5014"></a>**25 an Cèitean, AE 112** — *The cutting at Seann Bhral taken* (Seann Bhral). A second magistrate at Ros dhomhain, citing Thomas Hale's case by name, decides a claim on a customary working at Seann Bhral against a cooper's daughter's line, married three generations back to a human pilot. The ruling runs to a single page.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0231"><em>The case of Thomas Hale</em>, 4 am Màrt, AE 111</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0232"><em>Dunstan's rule applied</em>, 2 an Giblean, AE 112</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5001"><em>Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll</em>, 19 an Giblean, AE 112</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5015"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, AE 112** — *The coast's custodians follow Baile dhìreach's example* (Baile dhìreach). Within the year other custodians of the western coast quietly stop entering two-tongue marriages in their own rolls, without any word agreed between the districts. The marriages go on; only the writing of them fails.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0232"><em>Dunstan's rule applied</em>, 2 an Giblean, AE 112</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0233"></a>**25 an t-Ògmhios, AE 113** — *A cutting at Cnoc dhubh taken* (Cnoc dhubh). Among the cuttings taken under Dunstan's rule is the old customary working at Cnoc dhubh, held by one family since the Holy Age. A great-grandmother of the line had married a human sailor; that is enough.
- <a id="ev-EV-5016"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, AE 113** — *Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol* (Cnoc chaol). Griogair mac Ailein, a breaker of the Cnoc chaol sorting-floor, is taken up by A' Chompanaidh's constables over a dispute at the pay office and refuses to sign for a short-weighted cartload he did not cut. He is held in A' Chompanaidh's lock-up pending a hearing never set.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0233"><em>A cutting at Cnoc dhubh taken</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0234"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113** — *The Lamp-Watch* (Baile thais). A fellowship of pit crews calling itself the Lamp-Watch begins to meet at Baile thais and Cnoc chaol under cover of a burial club. Its first known deed is to pay for the burying of an old breaker who had died in the Company's lock-up.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5016"><em>Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5002"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113** — *Griogair mac Ailein dies in the lock-up* (Cnoc chaol). Griogair mac Ailein dies in A' Chompanaidh's lock-up at Cnoc chaol of a fever A' Chompanaidh's own surgeon records as already advanced when he was taken. He has no family living to claim him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5003"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113** — *Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note* (Baile dhìreach). Dòmhnall Ruadh, a crew-leader of Baile thais, carries a letter to Baile dhìreach asking Thomas Hale, known along the coast for his hard-won knowledge of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's law, to stand at Griogair mac Ailein's graveside and read A' Chompanaidh's surgeon's note releasing the body.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EV-5017"><em>The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5017"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113** — *The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box* (Baile thais). Comann an Adhlacaidh newly begun among the pit crews of Baile thais and Cnoc chaol, calling itself Faire nan Lòchran among its own members, gathers its members' wages to buy Griogair mac Ailein's grave-ground and coffin, meaning his burying to be seen done properly in A' Chompanaidh's own eye.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5003"><em>Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EV-5018"><em>Thomas Hale reads the surgeon's note at the grave</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5018"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113** — *Thomas Hale reads the surgeon's note at the grave* (Cnoc chaol). At a grave dug on the bare hill above the Cnoc chaol pit-head, Thomas Hale reads Griogair mac Ailein's release aloud in A' Chompanaidh's own tongue before some thirty of the fellowship, so that no clerk may afterward say the burying was done without A' Chompanaidh's leave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5017"><em>The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0235"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 114** — *Edward Vane Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Robert Haskins is called home after a quarrel with the Company over the price of steamship berths, and Edward Vane follows him. Vane is the first Commissioner born on Dia-thìr, at the Residency, and he speaks Dia-thìris, badly, but he speaks it.
- <a id="ev-EV-5019"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, AE 114** — *Robert Haskins leaves Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Robert Haskins, sixty-nine years old and Àrd-mhaor nine years, sails from Ros dhomhain after a quarrel with A' Chompanaidh over the price of a steamship berth. He never once, in nine years, spoke a full sentence of Dia-thìris without a clerk at his elbow to mend it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0235"><em>Edward Vane Commissioner</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 114</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5020"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, AE 114** — *Edward Vane answers the port custodian* (Ros dhomhain). Edward Vane, come up the same quay eleven days after Haskins sails, answers the custodian's customary greeting in Dia-thìris, badly and unprompted, the first Àrd-mhaor in living memory to do so without a clerk beside him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0235"><em>Edward Vane Commissioner</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 114</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0236"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, AE 115** — *The tram-road to Ros dhìreach* (Ros dhìreach). Vane lays an iron tram-road, drawn by mules, from the southern workings down to the coal port at Ros dhìreach. It halves the cost of shipping coal, and ends the carting trade of the villages on the old road.
- <a id="ev-EV-5004"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, AE 115** — *Vane speaks Dia-thìris before the council at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Edward Vane goes up to Cathair dhearg unsummoned and speaks three sentences of Dia-thìris to Comhairle a' Chùraim before finishing through Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's interpreter, telling the council he has come home. The clerk enters the word exactly, wrong tense and all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0235"><em>Edward Vane Commissioner</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 114</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0237"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, AE 116** — *The night-shift order*. For the first time the digging is made to run without ceasing, day and night, and the mountain is given no season of rest at all.
- <a id="ev-IV-0238"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, AE 116** — *The night crews at Cnoc chaol* (Cnoc chaol). The order falls first on Cnoc chaol, where the Company's newest galleries are opened to crews working by coal-lamp in two shifts. The custodians' roll writes that the hill was given no silence at all, and leaves the rest of the page blank.
- <a id="ev-EV-5021"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, AE 116** — *The custodian of Cnoc chaol writes the bare page* (Cnoc chaol). Vane's Àithne na h-Oidhche is read at every pit-mouth from Cnoc chaol to Muileann chiar. The young custodian of Cnoc chaol enters it in her roll and writes beneath it a single line, that the hill is given no silence at all, and leaves the rest of the page blank.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0237"><em>The night-shift order</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, AE 116</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0238"><em>The night crews at Cnoc chaol</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, AE 116</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5022"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, AE 116** — *The day shift stands in the yard at Cnoc chaol* (Cnoc chaol). Three hundred hewers of the day shift refuse to go down for the night change and stand in the yard through the last light, saying nothing to the overseer who twice asks their meaning. No chant is raised and no threat made; they simply do not move.
- <a id="ev-EV-5023"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 116** — *New crews replace the standing shift within the week* (Cnoc chaol). A' Chompanaidh brings crews up the tram-road from the coast towns within a week, humans and Dia-thìrich both, and sets them to the night shift before the stand at Cnoc chaol is a fortnight old. The camp's own crews go back to the day shift they still have.
- <a id="ev-EV-5024"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, AE 116** — *Muileann dhomhain shuts every door* (Muileann dhomhain). The milling town of Muileann dhomhain refuses to house or feed the strikebreaking crews sent up from the coast. Every inn and counter turns them away, and the well at the crossroads is found blocked with stones on the second morning, by no hand the custodian troubled to guess at.
- <a id="ev-EV-5025"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 116** — *Baile ghorm's potteries take the lamp-body contract* (Baile ghorm). The potteries of Baile ghorm take A' Chompanaidh's contract for clay coal-lamp bodies, thousands fired in a season on the same wheels that once turned bowls for the coast trade. Their own book notes them the first lamps made on the island for work commanded in the dark.
- <a id="ev-IV-0239"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, AE 117** — *The night-shift strike* (Cnoc chaol). The crews at Cnoc chaol refuse the night shift, and within a week are replaced by crews brought from the coast under the Company's new contracts. The Lamp-Watch keeps the strikers' families for a season, and then its money is gone.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5022"><em>The day shift stands in the yard at Cnoc chaol</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, AE 116</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5023"><em>New crews replace the standing shift within the week</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, AE 116</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0240"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 117** — *The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain* (Muileann dhomhain). The crews that replace the strikers at Cnoc chaol are brought through Muileann dhomhain, where the townsfolk turn them from every door. They sleep in the Company's barns, and several go home the next season.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5024"><em>Muileann dhomhain shuts every door</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, AE 116</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5005"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 117** — *Faire nan Lòchran's purse runs dry* (Cnoc chaol). Faire nan Lòchran, keeping the households of the crews who stood at Cnoc chaol, empties its purse by the second winter. Its own reckoning, kept in an unnamed hand, closes the year's account at nothing, and beneath it notes only that the hill was not given back its silence.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0239"><em>The night-shift strike</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, AE 117</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0241"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 118** — *Matthew Dunne's sermon* (Ros dhomhain). Matthew Dunne, the Mission's minister at Ros dhomhain, preaches against the night-shift order from the chapel pulpit, saying the Dia-thìrich are right that even the ground must rest. The Company complains to the Mission, and Dunne is called back to an Tìr Thall. The Lamp-Watch copies the sermon and reads it in the camps.
- <a id="ev-EV-5026"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, AE 118** — *Matthew Dunne preaches the fallow year* (Ros dhomhain). Matthew Dunne preaches at Ros dhomhain that the Dia-thìrich are right, and that ground owed no season of rest was owed the same fallow year the humans' own scripture asks of a field. He does not name A' Chompanaidh; the chapel knows his meaning without it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0241"><em>Matthew Dunne's sermon</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 118</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5027"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, AE 118** — *Matthew Dunne sails for an Tìr Thall* (Ros dhomhain). Recalled within the season on A' Chompanaidh's complaint, Matthew Dunne, three-and-thirty, preaches a last, ordinary sermon to a full chapel and goes down to the Ros dhomhain quay in the rain. Faire nan Lòchran has a copy of his fallow-year sermon within the week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0241"><em>Matthew Dunne's sermon</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 118</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5026"><em>Matthew Dunne preaches the fallow year</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, AE 118</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5028"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 118** — *The camps begin saying Casad Dhonnchaidh* (Cnoc chaol). Among the Dia-thìrich hewers of Cnoc chaol Grodadh nan Scamhan spares more than it takes, unlike among the humans of the night crews. The old women of the camps, who know the telling of the hewer of Achadh dhomhain whose cough stopped on the night his daughter was born, call any such cough among their own Casad Dhonnchaidh, and say no more.
- <a id="ev-IV-0242"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, AE 119** — *The lung-rot at Cnoc chaol* (Cnoc chaol). A wasting sickness of the lungs spreads among the night crews at Cnoc chaol and Baile thais. Unlike the Green Death it kills slowly. The Company pays the widows a pension for a year, then stops.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5028"><em>The camps begin saying Casad Dhonnchaidh</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 118</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0243"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, AE 119** — *Iain Maor and the night shift* (Muileann chrom). Iain Maor, overseer at Muileann chrom, writes to the Company that the night shift is killing his crews faster than it is paying for them. The letter survives because the Company filed it with his dismissal, which was undone a month later for want of anyone else.
- <a id="ev-EV-5006"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, AE 119** — *Iain Maor dismissed and restored* (Muileann chrom). Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir answers Iain Maor's letter with a notice relieving him of the overseer's staff for conduct unbecoming his office. His daughter Mòrag reads it to him by lamplight. Within a month, the crews having slowed the galleries to nothing, an unsigned notice restores him with no mention of the first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0243"><em>Iain Maor and the night shift</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 119</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0243a"></a>**22 am Màrt, AE 120** — *The coal line* (Muileann chrom). The Company opens its railway from the pits at Muileann chrom down by Cathair dhearg to the deep-water quay at Ros dhomhain. Its engines burn the island's own coal, as the steamships do, and the tram-road to Ros dhìreach is left to the mules. Within a year the carters' guild of Doire chaol, which had hauled the coal on Rathad na Mèinne for eighty years, loses the long haul. From the first day the Dia-thìrich call the engine carbad-iarainn, the iron chariot, and the railway the coal line.
- <a id="ev-IV-0244"></a>**18 an Giblean, AE 120** — *Coal-lamps from Baile ghorm* (Baile ghorm). The potteries of Baile ghorm take a contract for clay lamp-bodies for the night crews, thousands in a year. The potters' own book notes that they are the first lamps made on the island for work in the dark by command.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5025"><em>Baile ghorm's potteries take the lamp-body contract</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 116</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5029"></a>**22 an Cèitean, AE 120** — *The first coal train runs to Ros dhomhain* (Muileann chrom). A' Chompanaidh's iron road opens from the pits at Muileann chrom, past the hill below Cathair dhearg, to the deep-water quay at Ros dhomhain. Iain Maor and his daughter Mòrag watch the first loaded train take the grade at a pace no mule ever kept; the crews name it carbad-iarainn before the day is out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0243a"><em>The coal line</em>, 22 am Màrt, AE 120</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5006"><em>Iain Maor dismissed and restored</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, AE 119</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 121 – 130
