- <a id="ev-IV-0245"></a>**21 an Gearran, AE 121** — *Fionnan born*. A second child is born bound to the coal as Aisling was, half a century after her. So it is known that the thing is no chance of one birth: it comes of the digging, and it will go on.
- <a id="ev-EV-5030"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, AE 121** — *Fionnan's birth reaches the cellar* (Muileann chaol). The birth of Fionnan, entered by an eastern custodian among the ordinary births of the year, reaches Seilear Muileann chaol folded into a roll like any other. No hand marks the line for what it is; the copyists learn to find it again only once the word for the thing exists to look for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0245"><em>Fionnan born</em>, 21 an Gearran, AE 121</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0246"></a>**19 an Cèitean, AE 122** — *The Administration's count of the people* (Ros dhomhain). The Administration counts the people of Dia-thìr by district for the first time. Its figures for the humans are true to the household; for the Dia-thìrich they are rounded to the hundred, and in the hill districts to the thousand.
- <a id="ev-EV-5007"></a>**29 an t-Ògmhios, AE 122** — *Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar* (Muileann chaol). Cailean mac Eachainn, a turf-cutter's son of Muileann chaol with a plain hand at his letters, is taken on by Na Trì Teaghlaichean of the cellar when Seònag Bhàn's eyes fail her past close work. He is asked first not whether he can write fair, but whether he can hold his tongue.
- <a id="ev-EV-5031"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, AE 122** — *The count of the people copied in the cellar* (Muileann chaol). Cunntas an Riaghaltais passes through the cellar among Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's business the custodians think worth keeping. Fearchar mac Ailpein remarks that it counts the Dia-thìrich the way a man counts trees, near enough for the timber and not near enough for the names.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0246"><em>The Administration's count of the people</em>, 19 an Cèitean, AE 122</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5007"><em>Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, AE 122</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0246a"></a>**20 an Giblean, AE 123** — *The district of the outer coasts* (Seann Vell). The Administration makes the outer coasts one district and rules it from the harbour office at Seann Vell on Eilean ruadh, where its revenue cutters lie: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the windy coast in the far north-west. Its surveyors walk to the edge of the great moss there, which no chain can cross, and go no farther. Beyond it the district map is left blank.
- <a id="ev-EV-5032"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, AE 123** — *The blank map of the outer coasts* (Seann Vell). A letter reaching the cellar notes that Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's surveyors, walking the edge of the great moss beyond Seann Vell, found no way across it and left the rest of the outer district's map blank, and that the custodians of those coasts were no readier to be counted than the moss itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0246a"><em>The district of the outer coasts</em>, 20 an Giblean, AE 123</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0247"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, AE 123** — *Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, last of the druid masters* (Dùn thais). Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, the last master of Scoiltean nan Draoidhean to teach openly in this age, dies at Dùn thais. No one is named after her, and the school's register ends with her death. It is taken up again only long after the humans are gone.
- <a id="ev-EV-5033"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, AE 123** — *Seònaid nic Dhùghaill's death entered at the cellar* (Dùn thais). Word reaches the cellar that Seònaid nic Dhùghaill has died at Dùn thais in her seventy-eighth year, and that the register of her school ends with her, there being none of her house or pupils willing to keep it in the open. Cailean copies the line as it stands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0247"><em>Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, last of the druid masters</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, AE 123</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0248"></a>**5 am Màrt, AE 124** — *The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). The custodians of the east begin to send copies of their rolls for safe keeping to the town of Muileann chaol, which still kept Beathag nic Thòmais's loft of papers, beyond the Residency's reach. The copying is done in the houses of three families, and the copies kept in a cellar.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5007"><em>Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, AE 122</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5034"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, AE 124** — *The cellar comes to know the eastern hills by heart* (Muileann chaol). Winter on winter Na Trì Teaghlaichean of the cellar copy the whole record of the eastern hills, every birth and burial and fine and fever, until between them they come to know the district better than any single custodian who keeps only his own corner of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0248"><em>The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol</em>, 5 am Màrt, AE 124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0249"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, AE 125** — *The second Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). Some of the copies bound for Muileann chaol go by mistake to the smaller town of that name further north, and are kept there for years before the mistake is found. The custodians note that they were kept just as well.
- <a id="ev-EV-5008"></a>**4 am Màrt, AE 125** — *Nothing of weight was lost* (Muileann chaol). By lamplight Fearchar mac Ailpein and Cailean mac Eachainn match the recovered northern rolls against the cellar's own patched record of the missing years, and find that little of any weight had truly gone missing, only kept for a time in the wrong cellar.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0249"><em>The second Muileann chaol</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, AE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5035"></a>**17 an Giblean, AE 125** — *The receipt for a delivery never made* (Muileann chaol). Fearchar mac Ailpein finds among the cellar's bundles a northern custodian's receipt for a delivery the cellar never received. Na Trì Teaghlaichean learn only then that a second town of the same name, some hours to the north, has for years been taking in copies meant for their own cellar.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0249"><em>The second Muileann chaol</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, AE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5036"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, AE 125** — *Cailean fetches the mis-sent copies* (Muileann chaol). Cailean walks north on foot to the smaller Muileann chaol and finds three years of missing rolls kept whole and dry by an old custodian who says only that a roll is a roll, and that he kept it well until someone came to say it was theirs. Cailean carries the chest home unopened.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0249"><em>The second Muileann chaol</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, AE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0250"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, AE 126** — *The word found at last*. With two children now known, the custodians agree on a word for what is befalling them: fuil-ghuail, "coal-blood", rendered in the humans' tongue as coal-touched. It is meant as a physician's word. It outlives that meaning.
- <a id="ev-EV-5037"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, AE 126** — *The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). By the light of Brìde's lamp at the mouth of the oldest cutting, the custodians gathered at Cill ghlas argue two hours over a name for the coal-blood before a show of hands settles it. Cailean mac Eachainn, come up from the cellar to write it fair, counts more hands raised than not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0250"><em>The word found at last</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5036"><em>Cailean fetches the mis-sent copies</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, AE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0251"></a>**21 an Gearran, AE 126** — *The custodians who named it* (Cill ghlas). The word was agreed at a meeting of custodians at the shrine of Cill ghlas, where the oldest cutting still stood open. They chose a plain word, fit for the physician's book. The roll gives the vote; who first put the word forward it does not say.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5037"><em>The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5009"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, AE 126** — *Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). Peigi Ghlas writes to every custodian within two days' walk, calling them to the shrine of Cill ghlas on the night of the coming full moon to settle a name for the change that has now come twice upon a child of the pits, and asks the cellar to send a hand who can write it fair on the spot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0250"><em>The word found at last</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5038"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, AE 126** — *Cailean writes the word into the physician's column* (Cill ghlas). At Peigi Ghlas's dictation, Cailean mac Eachainn writes the agreed word into a physician's register at the mouth of the cutting, then carries the leaf home to Muileann chaol for a second fair copy. His own hand is the first to set fuil-ghuail down among the ordinary births and burials of the roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0250"><em>The word found at last</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251"><em>The custodians who named it</em>, 21 an Gearran, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5009"><em>Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0251a"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, AE 126** — *The Line of Aisling found* (Muileann chaol). Cailean mac Eachainn, a copyist in the cellar at Muileann chaol, finds in the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal the marriage of Aisling's father, Donnchadh mac Thormoid, with his line written seven names back, as the custodians write a marriage. He carries the seven names up to Tobar dhìreach, to Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste, the last who says the lines, and she knows them for the line of Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr. She says Aisling's line to him backward, from her father to the mason who found the fire. So what the camps whispered at Aisling's birth is found to be true. Cailean writes the line in the margin beside her birth.
- <a id="ev-EV-5501"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, AE 126** — *The third mark beside a birth* (Muileann chaol). On the same page Cailean finds the birth of Aisling entered with a mark he has seen only three or four times in a year of copying, never explained in any book given him, and recognises it for the mark the camps' whisper had already fixed to one child in the settlement.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251a"><em>The Line of Aisling found</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5502"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, AE 126** — *Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). Rather than report to the cellar, Cailean walks the hill road to Tobar dhìreach with the seven names copied onto a scrap of paper inside his coat, to ask whether a line so old could truly be Donnchadh's own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251a"><em>The Line of Aisling found</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5510"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, AE 126** — *Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line* (Muileann chaol). Copying the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal in Seilear Muileann chaol, Cailean mac Eachainn reads past the first name of a marriage line for the first time in a year of copying, and finds Donnchadh mac Thormoid's line carried seven fathers back to a name far older than a hewer's line should hold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251a"><em>The Line of Aisling found</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5502"><em>Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5511"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 126** — *Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling* (Tobar dhìreach). Ealasaid, last of Clann na Ceiste who still says the old lines at Tobar dhìreach, hears the seven names Cailean brings and gives him Aisling's whole line back to Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr, the first king, telling him plainly that she has told him whose son the child's forebear was and no more than that.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251a"><em>The Line of Aisling found</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5510"><em>Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line</em>, 21 an t-Samhain, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5512"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 126** — *Cailean writes the line in the margin* (Muileann chaol). Cailean carries Ealasaid's recital back to Muileann chaol and writes it small in the margin of the Àth ìseal roll beside Aisling's birth, telling no one at the cellar what he has done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0251a"><em>The Line of Aisling found</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, AE 126</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5511"><em>Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 126</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0252"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, AE 127** — *The Administration's register* (Ros dhomhain). The Residency, hearing of the word, orders that any Dia-thìreach child showing the change be reported to the Commissioner's office. The custodians obey by reporting none.
- <a id="ev-EV-5513"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, AE 127** — *The custodians' first return to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir: none* (Ros dhomhain). When Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir orders every child with fuil-ghuail reported to An t-Àrd-mhaor's office, the custodians from Cathair dhearg to the coast make their first return and report none, though every roll among them keeps its own quiet note of such births in a physician's plain word.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0252"><em>The Administration's register</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, AE 127</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5514"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 127** — *A custodian of Cill ghlas answers A' Chompanaidh's agent* (Cill ghlas). Asked by an agent of A' Chompanaidh whether she knows of any child with fuil-ghuail in her district, a custodian of Cill ghlas answers that she keeps no roll of miracles, only of births and deaths, and that the office is welcome to search her books for either.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0252"><em>The Administration's register</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, AE 127</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5503"></a>**22 an Cèitean, AE 128** — *Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas, her petition still unanswered, having trimmed Brìde's lamp herself the week before her death and said that she had asked Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir once and meant to leave the asking there.
- <a id="ev-IV-0253"></a>**7 an Giblean, AE 129** — *The third change of coin*. The old barter of the Dia-thìrich is struck down as lawful payment altogether. Every bargain on the island now goes by the humans' coin.
- <a id="ev-IV-0254"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 129** — *The barter houses closed* (Ros dhomhain). The barter houses at Ros dhomhain and Cathair dhearg, where cloth and fish had changed hands without coin since before the Crossing, are shut by order. A clerk of the Residency writes that the ledgers are now "complete for the first time."
- <a id="ev-IV-0255"></a>**22 am Màrt, AE 130** — *The fishwives of Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). The fishwives of Inis mhòr, who had sold by barter at the river steps since before the Crossing, will take no coin for a week, in protest at the shutting of the barter houses, and give their fish away. The Company's clerks record it as a glut.
- <a id="ev-IV-0256"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 130** — *Marks borrowed at interest* (Cathair dhearg). Barter being struck down, the hill villages borrow marks at interest from the Company's stores to buy seed. Within a few years most of the villages of Muileann chrom owe the Company more than a year's crops.

## The Years AE 131 – 140

- <a id="ev-IV-0257"></a>**20 an Giblean, AE 131** — *The old market at Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). The old barter market at Muileann òg, where hill and coast had met to trade since the Holy Age, closes after its last season, and the ground stands empty.
- <a id="ev-IV-0258"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, AE 131** — *Mòrag nic Iain Maor* (Muileann chrom). Iain Maor dies, and his daughter Mòrag takes the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, the first woman to hold it. The Company approves her in a letter that calls her "a safe pair of hands."
- <a id="ev-EV-5515"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 131** — *Iain Maor buried at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Iain Maor, third of that name to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, dies in the same house he held it from and is buried within the week, the camp's custom allowing no longer delay for an office that cannot sit empty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0258"><em>Mòrag nic Iain Maor</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 131</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5516"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, AE 131** — *Mòrag hangs the staff over her hearth* (Muileann chrom). Mòrag nic Iain Maor, first woman to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, hangs it over her own hearth on iron hooks her father never had fitted, rather than keep it across her knees as he had.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0258"><em>Mòrag nic Iain Maor</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, AE 131</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0259"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, AE 132** — *Charles Merriman Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Edward Vane dies at the Residency. Charles Merriman comes after him with a small company of armed constables, the first standing force the Administration has kept on Dia-thìr.
- <a id="ev-IV-0260"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, AE 132** — *The constable post at Muileann shean* (Muileann shean). Merriman's first constable post is built at Muileann shean on the northern coal road, a stone house with a yard for horses. The townsfolk call it the humans' second Residency, and do not mean it kindly.
- <a id="ev-EV-5504"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, AE 132** — *Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch* (Ceann mhòr). At Ceann mhòr, an old net-mender named Ruth Pallant tells the field-worker Hannah Webb of a night watch her own people's fisher-forebears learned from the island folk, kept in silence under a grey goose said to hold the sea shut. Hannah carries the telling of it home to the concession.
- <a id="ev-EV-5505"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, AE 132** — *Hannah Webb's first vigil* (Baile chrom). In a field behind her landlord's byre near Baile chrom, Hannah Webb keeps the silent watch for the first time, and sees, or believes she sees, a pale shape cross the night sky before she sleeps through a whole night for the first time in ten years on the island.
- <a id="ev-EV-5506"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, AE 132** — *The watch spreads along the concession's edge* (Baile chrom). Word of Hannah Webb's night vigil passes among the human labourers of the concession after a field hand sees her keeping it. Within a season a handful of others try it, and by autumn six or seven keep the field together on clear nights, spaced apart and silent.
- <a id="ev-EV-5517"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, AE 132** — *Edward Vane dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir* (Ros dhomhain). Àrd-mhaor Edward Vane, born at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain, dies there in the bed he was born in. The custodians who come to acknowledge the change of stewards find, as they had all his rule, that they had liked him rather more than they meant to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0259"><em>Charles Merriman Commissioner</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, AE 132</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5518"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 132** — *The post at Tobar ghorm and the custodian's rent* (Tobar ghorm). A second constable post rises at Tobar ghorm. The village's custodian, Uilleam Glas, takes the rent paid for the ground and clears the village of every debt it owes A' Chompanaidh's own store, to the written complaint of A' Chompanaidh's agent.
- <a id="ev-IV-0261"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 133** — *A barracks at Tobar ghorm* (Tobar ghorm). A second post is raised at Tobar ghorm, near the northern workings. The village's custodian is paid rent for the ground, and with it buys the village out of its debts to the Company store.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5518"><em>The post at Tobar ghorm and the custodian's rent</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 132</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0262"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, AE 133** — *A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom* (Baile chrom). The Mission at Cathair gheal reports that human labourers near Baile chrom keep vigil by night in the fields, praying in silence under the sign of a grey goose, which they call the wild goose of the Spirit. The Mission cannot find whence the practice came, and calls it irregular, a superstition learned of the Dia-thìrich. The Dia-thìrich of Baile chrom disown it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5504"><em>Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, AE 132</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5505"><em>Hannah Webb's first vigil</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, AE 132</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5506"><em>The watch spreads along the concession's edge</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, AE 132</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0262a"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, AE 133** — *Manannan's priests on the grey night* (Ceann mhòr). The priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ceann mhòr answer the Mission's report of the grey-night vigils. The practice owes something to the Dia-thìrich, they say, but to their own harbours and not to Baile chrom: the human fishing families of Ceann mhòr learned from them the night prayer to keep the sea shut, and the labourers inland keep it as a vigil of their Church, a night of silence under the wild goose of the Spirit in place of a prayer to Manannan. The priests call it Manannan's prayer gone astray, and do not admit its keepers to their house.
- <a id="ev-EV-5519"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, AE 133** — *Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular* (Cathair gheal). Obadiah Renn, Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's minister at Cathair gheal's chapel, questions Hannah Webb about the watch and, finding no scripture that knows a goose, writes to Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's house that the practice is irregular and its origin uncertain, though he does not call it wrongdoing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0262"><em>A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, AE 133</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5520"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 133** — *Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch* (Baile chrom). The custodian of Baile chrom's lower row refuses any part of the human labourers' vigil, saying the town's own name should be left out of the keeping of it. The field folk, who had hoped to call the watch a thing shared between the two peoples, learn to call it their own alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0262"><em>A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, AE 133</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5519"><em>Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, AE 133</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0263"></a>**1 an Giblean, AE 134** — *The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The dockers of Ros dhomhain, Dia-thìrich and human alike, refuse to load coal for nine days over the new berth charges. It is the only strike of the age in which human workers stand with Dia-thìrich. Merriman's constables break it, and the human dockers are shipped over the sea.
- <a id="ev-IV-0264"></a>**30 an Giblean, AE 134** — *Seann Vell's dockers stay out* (Seann Vell). The dockers of Seann Vell, the harbour next to Ros dhomhain, refuse to load the coal sent to them during the strike. When it ends they are not shipped over the sea, for there are no humans among them; but they are not hired again either.
- <a id="ev-IV-0265"></a>**29 an Cèitean, AE 134** — *Lorccan born*. A third such child is born, in a mining town and not a camp; the thing is no longer bound to any one place.
- <a id="ev-EV-5521"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, AE 134** — *Manannan's priest names the goose gone astray* (Baile chrom). A priest of the harbour temple at Ceann mhòr walks to Baile chrom, watches Hannah Webb's vigil through a night, and tells her the goose she keeps is an Gèadh Fiadhaich, wandered from Manannan's own harbours into a shape no longer entirely his people's to reclaim or to stop.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0262"><em>A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, AE 133</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5520"><em>Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 133</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5522"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, AE 134** — *The berth toll and the docker Tòmas Ruadh* (Ros dhomhain). A' Chompanaidh posts a new toll on every ton loaded at the Ros dhomhain coal berths. The docker Tòmas Ruadh, whom Daniel Webb once pulled clear of a falling beam, tells him of it, and the two speak for the first time of standing off the hooks together.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0263"><em>The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain</em>, 1 an Giblean, AE 134</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5523"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, AE 134** — *Merriman's constables break the stoppage* (Ros dhomhain). On the stoppage's tenth morning, Merriman's constables stand a rifle-line the length of the Ros dhomhain quay. The dockers, who had held nine days without a blow struck, go back to the hooks within the hour rather than test a tenth day against thirty grey coats.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0263"><em>The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain</em>, 1 an Giblean, AE 134</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5524"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, AE 134** — *The human dockers shipped over the sea* (Ros dhomhain). A' Chompanaidh takes the names of every human docker who struck and offers them passage over the sea within the week, once, with the plain understanding that it will not be offered twice. Hannah Webb watches her brother Daniel go up the gangway from the Ros dhomhain quay.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0263"><em>The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain</em>, 1 an Giblean, AE 134</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5507"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 134** — *Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas* (Baile thais). With his knees gone stiff for the low work at Baile thais and two grandchildren to feed, the ageing hewer Raghnall Breac walks two days to the new galleries at Cill ghlas, where the pay is better and the headings still stand tall enough for a man to work upright. He writes to his daughter Eilidh twice a year.
- <a id="ev-IV-0266"></a>**3 am Màrt, AE 135** — *Cian born*. A fourth is born within a year of the third. Never again do the children of the undying generation come so close together.
- <a id="ev-IV-0267"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, AE 136** — *Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). The Company begins to drive galleries under the hills about Cill ghlas with blasting-powder shipped from an Tìr Thall. The custodians of the shrine ask that no charge be set within sight of the old cutting. The Company's engineer marks their asking on his plan, and sets the charges below it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5507"><em>Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, AE 134</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0268"></a>**2 an Gearran, AE 136** — *Powder landed at Caol ìseal* (Caol ìseal). The blasting-powder for the new galleries is landed at Caol ìseal on the northern coast, away from the crowded southern harbours, and carted inland under guard. The town's custodians ask what is in the barrels and are told it is lamp-oil.
- <a id="ev-EV-5508"></a>**6 am Màrt, AE 136** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at Faire nan Lòchran's table* (Baile thais). The crew-leader Eilidh nic Raghnaill of Baile thais is asked, for the first time, to sit at the table where Faire nan Lòchran keeps its business, and copies its minutes into a second book kept in her own linen chest, where no clerk of A' Chompanaidh would think to look.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5525"></a>**28 an Cèitean, AE 136** — *Fairley marks the custodians' asking on his plan* (Cill ghlas). A' Chompanaidh's engineer Robert Fairley writes the custodians' request, that no charge be set within sight of the shrine at Cill ghlas, into the margin of his working plan. The plan shows the shrine as a bare shape with no depth drawn beneath it, and the numbered headings below are never measured against it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0267"><em>Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, AE 136</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5526"></a>**29 an Cèitean, AE 136** — *Beathag Ruadh's roll at Caol ìseal* (Caol ìseal). The custodian of Caol ìseal counts forty casks of blasting-powder off a ship of A' Chompanaidh, told to her carters as lamp-oil, and writes in her roll that the staves smelled of nothing when she put her hand to them. Her line goes unanswered into Seilear Muileann chaol with the rest of the year's roll.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0268"><em>Powder landed at Caol ìseal</em>, 2 an Gearran, AE 136</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0269"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 137** — *Scàineadh Cill ghlas*. The Rending: in the hills east of the capital, about Cill ghlas, the earth tears open along a fault beneath a common working. Dozens are killed, and a whole mining district is shut for a generation.
- <a id="ev-IV-0270"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, AE 137** — *The first open fight*. A mining death, which the Dia-thìrich workers lay at the door of the humans' carelessness, leads to the first bloodshed between the two peoples.
- <a id="ev-IV-0271"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, AE 137** — *The shrine at Cill ghlas lost* (Cill ghlas). The Rending swallows the old cutting at Cill ghlas, where the custodians had kept the rites through all the age, and its shrine with it. The custodians' roll sets down the loss of the shrine before the loss of the dead; a later copyist has put them in the other order.
- <a id="ev-IV-0272"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, AE 137** — *The district closed* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). The Company shuts the whole district of the Rending and fences it, leaving Cill ghlas, Àth chaol and their hamlets in the shires of Muileann dhearg and Muileann chiar without work. The villages empty toward Baile thais and Muileann dhearg, and the closed district is left to the thorn.
- <a id="ev-IV-0272a"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, AE 137** — *The meeting on the moor road* (Coinneachadh an Fhearainn). The folk turned out of the closed district send their eldest to the custodians of Muileann dhomhain, who meet them at a standing stone on the moor road below the town, lest the Company's clerks see them in the town hall. At the stone the custodians lend them the land at the edge of the fenced ground. The place is called Coinneachadh an Fhearainn, the meeting of the land.
- <a id="ev-IV-0273"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed* (Achadh chaol). Folk of the closed district build a new village at Achadh chaol, at the edge of the fenced ground, on land lent by the custodians of Muileann dhomhain. It is the only settlement of the age founded by Dia-thìrich for Dia-thìrich with no Company surveyor's hand in it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0274"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *The fight at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The death that began it was a flooded gallery at Muileann chrom, where seven died after the pumps were stopped to save fuel. When the Company's agent came to the pithead the crews stoned him and his constables, and the constables fired. Four Dia-thìrich and one constable were killed.
- <a id="ev-EV-5509"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground* (Cill ghlas). Eilidh nic Raghnaill walks to Cill ghlas to find her father's grave and finds instead the fence and the fallen headgear of the eighth heading. A constable turns her away from the closed ground. She writes nothing of the hour in Faire nan Lòchran's book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0272"><em>The district closed</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5527"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *Scàineadh Cill ghlas kills the thirty-one* (Cill ghlas). On the ninth of an t-Ògmhios the fault beneath Cill ghlas tears open and the ground above the eighth heading and the old shrine cutting comes down together. The custodians' roll names thirty-one dead, among them the hewer Raghnall Breac, and says four bodies more were never brought up.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0269"><em>Scàineadh Cill ghlas</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5528"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *A' Chompanaidh fences the closed district* (Cill ghlas). A' Chompanaidh's surveyors return within the week to fence the district from Cill ghlas to Àth chaol, and Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's order forbids any wage or working on any ground inside the fence. Households leave through the autumn and winter, first in twos and threes, then whole villages together.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0272"><em>The district closed</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5529"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The overseer Fionnlagh tells the new agent Edgar Holt that the flooded ground under one heading at Muileann chrom has never gone a night without its pumps, drawing as it does from an unmapped old working above it. Holt orders the pumps stopped regardless, to spare coal for the winding-gear until a delayed barge arrives.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0274"><em>The fight at Muileann chrom</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5530"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *The flooded gallery takes seven* (Muileann chrom). With the pumps idle overnight, the gallery at Muileann chrom fills to the roof, and seven men of the change of shift, Fionnlagh among them, do not come up. Mòrag nic Iain Maor stands at the pit-mouth as they are brought up and laid in a row on the wet boards.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0274"><em>The fight at Muileann chrom</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5529"><em>Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-5531"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137** — *Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry* (Ros dhomhain). At Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's inquiry at Ros dhomhain, the fourth Steward Mòrag nic Iain Maor carries A' Chompanaidh's own staff into the room and testifies that Edgar Holt ordered the pumps stopped against his overseer's warning. The commissioners rule her account improper and have the clerk strike it from the record.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-5530"><em>The flooded gallery takes seven</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0275"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, AE 138** — *Mòrag Maor at the inquiry* (Muileann chrom). At the Administration's inquiry into the fight the overseer Mòrag nic Iain Maor bears witness that the pumps were stopped on the agent's order. Her words are struck out. The Lamp-Watch gets a copy of them all the same.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-5531"><em>Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0276"></a>**2 an Gearran, AE 138** — *The grey fever* (Baile thais). A fever of the chest comes in on the ships and runs over the whole island, from the capital to the eastern farms. It kills the young and strong more than the old, the Mission notes in alarm. The camps, already hungry, bury more than the towns.
- <a id="ev-IV-0277"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, AE 138** — *The grey fever at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). At Cathair mhòr the grey fever shuts the market for the first time in the town's memory. The custodians' roll gives the dead by street, and the longest list is of the street where the carters lived.
- <a id="ev-IV-0278"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *The grey fever at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). At Dùn thais the fever takes the physician the Administration sent to treat it, and two of the Mission's nurses. The old houses of the druid masters are opened as sick-rooms.
- <a id="ev-EV-6010"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *Achadh chaol's first roll opened* (Achadh chaol). Aonghas Mòr, once keeper of the lost shrine, opens the first custodians' roll of Achadh chaol on the day the new village's well is finished, its first line giving the well's depth and naming no shrine and no dead. It is the only settlement of the age raised without any surveyor of A' Chompanaidh's hand in it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0273"><em>Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6011"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *Faire nan Lòchran keeps the struck copy* (Baile thais). A Dia-thìreach clerk who keeps A' Chompanaidh's own file copy of the inquiry's minutes has the struck-through page carried north to Baile thais folded inside sailcloth. Eilidh nic Raghnaill copies it a second time into Faire nan Lòchran's linen-chest book, the stricken line copied as stricken, and is given a full seat at the table that winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0275"><em>Mòrag Maor at the inquiry</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, AE 138</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0234"><em>The Lamp-Watch</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 113</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6001"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of Am Fiabhras Glas* (Baile thais). A boy not yet old enough for his first wage dies of Am Fiabhras Glas at Baile thais under Eilidh nic Raghnaill's sitting, having asked her, near the end, what month it was. His mother keeps his name from Comann an Adhlacaidh's book, and Eilidh does not ask for it twice.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0276"><em>The grey fever</em>, 2 an Gearran, AE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6002"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins Comann an Adhlacaidh's book* (Baile thais). Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins keeping a plain hand-written record for Comann an Adhlacaidh at Baile thais, answering to no custodian's roll, after watching her father Raghnall Breac carry twenty years of names in his memory and give none of them to paper. She means not to do the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0276"><em>The grey fever</em>, 2 an Gearran, AE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6012"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge* (Baile thais). In Comann an Adhlacaidh's room at Baile thais, Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge over three nights by a single coal lamp, with Griogal and two others reading each page back to her aloud. She writes its last sentence twice before settling the wording Griogal judges means it rather than asks permission to mean it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6002"><em>Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins Comann an Adhlacaidh's book</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0279"></a>**27 am Faoilleach, AE 139** — *The second petition*. This one carries a threat beneath its words, not a plea. It is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich the Administration troubles to answer, and it answers with more guards, not with concessions.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6012"><em>Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0280"></a>**12 an Lùnastal, AE 139** — *The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach* (Cnoc dhìreach). Coinneach Ruadh, custodian of Cnoc dhìreach, signs the second petition, and in the same week is turned out of his post as clerk to the Company store. He is one of eleven who sign and lose Company work for it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0281"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 139** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill* (Baile thais). The second petition was drawn up by Eilidh nic Raghnaill, a crew-leader of Baile thais and one of the Lamp-Watch, and signed by custodians and crew-leaders of thirty-one settlements. It ends with a sentence the Residency underlined: that the hill would not be worked by people who were not asked.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6012"><em>Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 138</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6013"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 139** — *A' Chompanaidh dismisses Coinneach Ruadh at his own store* (Cnoc dhìreach). A' Chompanaidh's agent at Cnoc dhìreach delivers Coinneach Ruadh's letter of dismissal at the store's door in front of the week's flour queue, the day his signature to An Dàrna Athchuinge dries. He is offered twice the chance to withdraw his name and twice declines it, saying a name once given is not the giver's to take back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0280"><em>The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach</em>, 12 an Lùnastal, AE 139</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6014"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 139** — *Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk underlines the petition's last sentence* (A' Phlàigh Uaine). A clerk of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir underlines in red ink An Dàrna Athchuinge's last sentence, that the hill will not go on being worked by people who are not asked, before passing the fair copy Eilidh nic Raghnaill made up the office. The custodians afterward agree it is the first sign Riaghaltas nan Coigreach has read a Dia-thìrich word and understood it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0279"><em>The second petition</em>, 27 am Faoilleach, AE 139</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0281"><em>Eilidh nic Raghnaill</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 139</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0282"></a>**25 an Gearran, AE 140** — *The constables tripled* (Ros dhomhain). Merriman answers by tripling the constables and posting companies at Muileann chrom, Baile thais, Ceann fhada and Cnoc chaol, each with a walled store. The constables are paid from the tithe.
- <a id="ev-IV-0283"></a>**26 am Màrt, AE 140** — *Barracks at Dùn chrom* (Dùn chrom). A barracks for the constables is built at Dùn chrom, on the capital side of the hills, with room for two hundred men. For most of its first year it stands empty, for want of constables to fill it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0284"></a>**24 an Giblean, AE 140** — *Ìomhar Seabhag* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Ìomhar Seabhag preaches that Mòd's hunger has turned on those who have eaten the hill. The hawk-shrines of the west begin to serve as meeting-houses for the Lamp-Watch, and the constables do not yet know it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0285"></a>**23 an Cèitean, AE 140** — *The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). At Ros gheal the hawk-faithful fishing families, who had chased out the Company's customs officers a century before, raise a shrine to Mòd on the harbour wall. The constables order it down. It is built again three times in a single season.
- <a id="ev-IV-0286"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, AE 140** — *The hawk and the druids at Inis bhàn* (Inis bhàn). At Inis bhàn the priests of the hawk and a few who still keep the questions of the druid school in private meet for a disputation, the first between them in living memory. It is written that it settled nothing, and that both sides afterwards signed the petition.
- <a id="ev-IV-0287"></a>**20 an t-Iuchar, AE 140** — *The grey fever in the north-west* (Baile chrom). The grey fever returns and settles in the north-west, about Baile chrom and the towns of the concession, where it kills humans as readily as Dia-thìrich. The Mission's hospital at Cathair gheal overflows, and for the first time Dia-thìrich and human sick lie in the same wards.
- <a id="ev-EV-6003"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, AE 140** — *The first constables' company reaches Baile thais* (Baile thais). Forty constables under an officer named Prosser march into Baile thais on the twenty-fifth of Gearran and wall the settlement's old open store within the fortnight, taking the camp's well inside the new wall. Eilidh nic Raghnaill and Comann an Adhlacaidh watch the company make camp on ground that had been common land that same morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0282"><em>The constables tripled</em>, 25 an Gearran, AE 140</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6015"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, AE 140** — *The fourth shrine stands at Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). After the constables tear down the hawk-faithful's shrine on the Ros gheal harbour wall three mornings running, unnamed hands raise it a fourth time and the constables stop trying. The shrine stands afterward as the ordinary furniture of a wall that had always carried something.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0285"><em>The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal</em>, 23 an Cèitean, AE 140</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6016"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, AE 140** — *An overman gives up his cot at Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). In the crowded shared ward at Cathair gheal a Dia-thìreach overman of the north-west galleries gives up his own bed to a human boy of the concession no more than nine years old, and sits the night on the floor beside him. Hannah Webb writes of it to Eilidh nic Raghnaill at Baile thais.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0287"><em>The grey fever in the north-west</em>, 20 an t-Iuchar, AE 140</a>.</span>

## The Years AE 141 – 150

- <a id="ev-IV-0288"></a>**6 am Màrt, AE 141** — *Muileann fhionn shut in* (Muileann fhionn). Muileann fhionn, a Dia-thìreach mill town in the north-west, shuts its roads against the fever and keeps them shut for a season. Human carters of the concession are turned back with their loads at the town's edge.
- <a id="ev-IV-0289"></a>**18 an Giblean, AE 141** — *The fever at Tobar fhiadhaich* (Tobar fhiadhaich). At Tobar fhiadhaich in the north the fever takes one household in three. The custodians of the village burn no huts; they had heard of Àth ghlas in their grandparents' time, but judge it too late.
- <a id="ev-IV-0290"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, AE 141** — *The road-houses make ready* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The road-houses along the old mining roads begin to serve as waystations for bands of armed men. The roads make ready for a war not yet declared.
- <a id="ev-IV-0291"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 141** — *An Taigh-seinnse Òir* (An Taigh-seinnse Òir). An Taigh-seinnse Òir, the great house on the eastern road beyond Dùn dhearg, digs a well in its yard and builds a wall round the well. The keeper tells the Company's carters it is against thieves.
- <a id="ev-IV-0292"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, AE 141** — *An Leòmhann Buidhe* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). An Leòmhann Buidhe, the road-house on the northern road through the druid country, takes on six new ostlers in a single season, none of whom know anything of horses.
- <a id="ev-EV-6017"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, AE 141** — *Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads Ìomhar Seabhag's sermon to Faire nan Lòchran* (Baile thais). A fowler leaves a written copy of Ìomhar Seabhag's Seann Skell sermon with Comann an Adhlacaidh's door-keeper at Baile thais, and Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads it aloud to the room by the same lamp she drafted An Dàrna Athchuinge by. For once she does not write anything in the club's book afterward.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0284"><em>Ìomhar Seabhag</em>, 24 an Giblean, AE 140</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6018"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, AE 141** — *Aonghas takes the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). A crew-leader from Baile thais asks Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr since Seònaid Bhàn's line came to him, whether the loft above his stable might hold men now and again with no questions asked. He agrees, and stops in time asking what they carry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0290"><em>The road-houses make ready</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, AE 141</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0293"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, AE 142** — *An Taigh-òsta Grianach walled* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). An Taigh-òsta Grianach, called the singing house since the songs of Fearchar Bàrd, raises a wall round its yard and sets a watch on its gate.
- <a id="ev-IV-0294"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, AE 142** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach barred* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Am Buabhall Fortanach, the great road-house on the south-western road, bars its gates at dusk and keeps a watch on the roof. Its keeper, Tormod Buabhall, keeps a list of travellers and sends it up the road each week, to whom is not told.
- <a id="ev-IV-0295"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, AE 142** — *The harbour of Doire shean* (Doire shean). The little harbour of Doire shean, below Am Buabhall Fortanach, becomes the landing for the goods the house cannot take by road. The fishermen of Doire shean are paid in silver from the east.
- <a id="ev-IV-0296"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, AE 142** — *An Taigh-seinnse Reòta* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). At An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the northern road the stables are rebuilt with a loft for sleeping men. The Company's carters mark that the loft is never empty, and never holds the same men twice.
- <a id="ev-IV-0297"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, AE 142** — *An Sligeanach Fad' às* (An Sligeanach Fad' às). An Sligeanach Fad' às, on the eastern road near the silver country, becomes the post-house through which the Lamp-Watch sends word from the camps to Muileann chiar. The silver guild pays its keeper's rent.
- <a id="ev-IV-0298"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, AE 142** — *The runners of Àth fhiadhaich* (Àth fhiadhaich). Runners from Àth fhiadhaich carry the Lamp-Watch's letters from An Sligeanach Fad' às to the silver town. They are boys of twelve and thirteen, too young for the constables to stop.
- <a id="ev-EV-6004"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, AE 142** — *A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door* (Àth fhiadhaich). A boy runner out of Àth fhiadhaich comes soaked from the ford into Aonghas's yard, asks for bread as any boy might, and leaves a folded scrap under the loose board by the stable door naming a date and nothing else. Aonghas burns it in the kitchen fire that night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0298"><em>The runners of Àth fhiadhaich</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, AE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6019"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, AE 142** — *The fishermen of Doire shean paid in eastern silver* (Doire shean). Old Coinneach nan Ràmh and the other fishermen below Am Buabhall Fortanach take to being paid, for certain nights never spoken of as work, in silver struck in an Tìr Thall rather than Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's coin. None of it is ever spent where a clerk of A' Chompanaidh might see it change hands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0295"><em>The harbour of Doire shean</em>, 30 an Lùnastal, AE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6020"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, AE 142** — *Coinneach nan Ràmh's word on the loft at the Reòta* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). The old fisherman Coinneach nan Ràmh tells Aonghas that the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta is never once found empty by A' Chompanaidh's carters passing through, and never once holds the same men two nights running: it comes and goes, he says, like the tide, and no man has ever caught the tide at its turning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0296"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, AE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6021"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 142** — *The Sligeanach's psalter* (Achadh mhòr). Marks for the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr travel up Rathad na Mèinne folded inside a psalter, as innocent on the road as any priest's book, sent on from the ledger kept in the roof-space above the shrine at Achadh mhòr.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0297"><em>An Sligeanach Fad' às</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, AE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0299"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, AE 143** — *Achadh mhòr keeps the ledgers* (Achadh mhòr). The Lamp-Watch's ledgers of the money it has from the silver guild are kept at Achadh mhòr, a village near the house on the eastern road, in the roof of the village shrine.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6021"><em>The Sligeanach's psalter</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, AE 142</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0300"></a>**26 an Gearran, AE 143** — *Seònaid's house* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, the carters' house on the coal road that Seònaid Bhàn opened again in the early years of the digging, is kept now by her great-grandson Aonghas. It is the busiest of the walled houses, the one the constables search most often and find least in.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6018"><em>Aonghas takes the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, AE 141</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0301"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *The first stoppage together*. For the first time the mining country stops work on one day in many places at once. Scattered as it is, the resistance of the Dia-thìrich can act as one when it chooses.
- <a id="ev-IV-0302"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *Muileann bheag in the north-east* (Muileann bheag). The workings at Muileann bheag in the north-east, among the druid villages, stop with the rest. The town's custodian writes that it is the first thing the town has done with the hills in a hundred years.
- <a id="ev-IV-0303"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *The northern pits at Àth dhomhain* (Àth dhomhain). The pits north of the hills at Àth dhomhain stop with the rest on the day of the stoppage, the word brought by a runner and not by the beacon. Their crew-leaders are among those shipped over the sea.
- <a id="ev-IV-0304"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *Ceann bheag stops* (Ceann bheag). The coal stage at Ceann bheag on the northern coast stops loading the same day. Its dockers had not been told; they stop because the coal stops coming.
- <a id="ev-IV-0305"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal* (Cnoc gheal). The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal in the north-east, who cut stone for the Company's buildings, lay down their tools on the day of the stoppage unasked. Why, no one says.
- <a id="ev-IV-0306"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *The day the pits stopped* (Muileann chrom). On the day of the stoppage every working in the Muileann chrom district halted at once, and with them Baile thais, Cnoc chaol, the silver town and the eastern pits at Ros fhionn. The sign was a beacon fire lit on the hills above Doire mhòr, which the Company took for a heath fire.
- <a id="ev-IV-0307"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 143** — *The coal ships wait* (Ros dhomhain). The Company's steamships lie six days at Ros dhomhain with empty holds. The agents at the quay write that they have never seen the harbour so quiet, and that it frightened them more than the crowds.
- <a id="ev-IV-0308"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 143** — *The stoppage broken* (Ros dhomhain). The stoppage ends when the constables shut the Company stores in every district at once. Forty crew-leaders are taken; thirty-two are let go without charge, and eight are shipped over the sea to an Tìr Thall for trial and never heard of again.
- <a id="ev-EV-6005"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 143** — *The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). On 27 am Màrt, Aonghas watches smoke rise thin from Cnoc an Rabhaidh in a hard north-west wind, and every wheel within sight of his yard stops within the hour. A carter in his own yard names it a heath fire before anyone learns otherwise.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0301"><em>The first stoppage together</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 143</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0306"><em>The day the pits stopped</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 143</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6022"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 143** — *The heather burned thin* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). The constables burn the heather of Cnoc an Rabhaidh to deny the hill a second beacon. It grows back thin and late the following spring, and three years pass before anyone on Rathad na Mèinne speaks openly of what the fire had truly been.
- <a id="ev-IV-0309"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, AE 144** — *Beacon hill at Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). Doire mhòr, which refused the first contract and then lost its water, has by now but a few households. The beacon of the stoppage was lit on its hill by the children's children of Beathag Dhubh's people, and the constables burn the heather of the hill to deny it to them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6005"><em>The fire on Cnoc an Rabhaidh</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 143</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6022"><em>The heather burned thin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 143</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0310"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 144** — *Fewer ships from over the sea* (Muir Mhanannain). The keepers' daybooks at the five beacons show fewer ships from an Tìr Thall each year, and the ships that come are older. The Company's letters speak of troubles at home and do not say what they are.
- <a id="ev-IV-0311"></a>**13 an Giblean, AE 145** — *Caol leathan's idle harbour* (Caol leathan). At Caol leathan the wool for the humans' market waits for room in ships that do not come. The merchants of the town begin to sell their wool inland again by barter, against the law.
- <a id="ev-IV-0312"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, AE 145** — *Caol bheag's empty quay* (Caol bheag). The Company's quay at Caol bheag on the northern coast, built for the eastern trade, sees one ship in a season. The Company's agent there writes that he has been forgotten.
- <a id="ev-EV-6006"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, AE 145** — *Tormod Buabhall's word on a house with nothing left to guard* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Meeting Aonghas at the horse-fair after the ships have thinned to nothing, Tormod Buabhall tells him a house with no custom left keeps its gates shut for a different reason than before: a house that guards everything still has, behind its locked door, something it means to keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0310"><em>Fewer ships from over the sea</em>, 25 an Giblean, AE 144</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6023"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, AE 145** — *The forgotten agent of Caol bheag* (Caol bheag). A' Chompanaidh's agent at the idle quay of Caol bheag sees one ship in a whole season and writes to Ros dhomhain that he has been forgotten. So far as Rathad na Mèinne ever hears, no answer comes back to him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0312"><em>Caol bheag's empty quay</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, AE 145</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0313"></a>**24 an Cèitean, AE 146** — *Leave no longer asked*. The humans' Administration begins to give commands without seeking the counsel of the Dia-thìrich at all. The pretence of leave asked and given is dropped.
- <a id="ev-IV-0314"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, AE 146** — *Lionel Strake Commissioner* (Ros dhomhain). Charles Merriman leaves Dia-thìr in ill health, and Lionel Strake, a soldier, comes after him. His commission, read aloud at the Residency, makes no mention of the Council of Custodians, and he does not call on it.
- <a id="ev-EV-6024"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, AE 146** — *Strake's commission read without the council's name* (Ros dhomhain). At Ros dhomhain, Aonghas stands in the market square while Lionel Strake's commission is read from Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's steps: it names A' Chompanaidh and Riaghaltas nan Coigreach in an Tìr Thall, and, for the first time in any Àrd-mhaor's commission, does not name Comhairle a' Chùraim at all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0313"><em>Leave no longer asked</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 146</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0314"><em>Lionel Strake Commissioner</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, AE 146</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0315"></a>**26 an Gearran, AE 147** — *The council locked out* (Cathair dhearg). Strake has the council hall at Cathair dhearg locked and its keys lodged at the Residency. The custodians meet instead in Macha's temple, whose priests, who had blessed the humans' coin, now shelter those who petitioned against it.
- <a id="ev-IV-0315a"></a>**27 am Màrt, AE 147** — *The iron bird* (Ros dhomhain). Strake brings a flying machine from an Tìr Thall in the hold of a Company steamship and has it flown from a field above the Residency over the coal country, to count the workings from the air. The Dia-thìrich call it eun-iarainn, the iron bird. The custodians enter it in the roll as the first thing seen over Dia-thìr that flew and was not alive.
- <a id="ev-IV-0316"></a>**25 an Giblean, AE 147** — *The edict of seizure*. The humans' Administration claims the right to take any dwelling of the Dia-thìrich it deems needful for the widening of the workings. Of all the grievances it is the one most often named in every surviving account of what followed.
- <a id="ev-IV-0317"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, AE 147** — *The seizure of Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). The first dwellings taken under the edict are those of Doire mhòr, for a new shaft beneath the hill, and constables carry out the last households. The village that refused the first contract is the first emptied by the last.
- <a id="ev-IV-0318"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, AE 147** — *Evictions at Baile dhomhain* (Baile dhomhain). At Baile dhomhain, the first camp laid out on paper, two streets are pulled down for a spoil-tip. The families are offered huts at Àth ìseal and marks for their timber; most go to kin in the hill villages instead.
- <a id="ev-EV-6007"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, AE 147** — *The old man of Doire mhòr* (Doire mhòr). An old man carried gently from his own doorstone by constables clearing houses under Àithne a' Ghlacaidh asks only that it be written down that they were gentle about it. Mòrag nic Iain Maor, come from Muileann chrom, carries the sentence home with no book to hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0316"><em>The edict of seizure</em>, 25 an Giblean, AE 147</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0317"><em>The seizure of Doire mhòr</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, AE 147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6025"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, AE 147** — *The iron bird seen over Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). A flying machine passes twice over the Muileann chrom valley without beating its wings, and the crews at the pit-mouth stop their barrows to watch it go. By evening the district has a name for it, eun-iarainn, borrowed from nowhere and understood at once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0315a"><em>The iron bird</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 147</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6007"><em>The old man of Doire mhòr</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, AE 147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6026"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 147** — *Mòrag's private book* (Muileann chrom). Mòrag nic Iain Maor sets down word of the iron bird in the private hand her father taught her, kept apart from A' Chompanaidh's own tally, the same hand in which her struck-out testimony at the pithead inquiry had first been copied for Faire nan Lòchran.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0315a"><em>The iron bird</em>, 27 am Màrt, AE 147</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0275"><em>Mòrag Maor at the inquiry</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, AE 138</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6025"><em>The iron bird seen over Muileann chrom</em>, 30 an t-Samhain, AE 147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0319"></a>**24 an Cèitean, AE 148** — *Mòrag Maor lays down the staff* (Muileann chrom). Mòrag nic Iain Maor, fourth of her line to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, will not carry out evictions in her district, and breaks the staff at the Company's door. Three other overseers give up their places in the same month, and the Company puts humans in them.
- <a id="ev-IV-0320"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, AE 148** — *The silver guild arms* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver guild of Muileann chiar, still holding its seam under the compact of a century before, begins to buy rifles through the eastern pirates. Its ledger enters them as refining tools.
- <a id="ev-IV-0321"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, AE 148** — *Rifles by way of the pirates* (Spùinneadairean-mara). The silver guild's rifles come ashore from the raiders' boats in the eastern waters, where no Company gunboat has sailed for years. The raiders take their pay in bar silver, by weight.
- <a id="ev-IV-0322"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, AE 148** — *The council in the forest of Cnoc bheag* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Custodians, crew-leaders of the Lamp-Watch and the dissenting priests of Macha meet in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag and make one council for the mining country, and choose Eilidh nic Raghnaill to speak for it. No human writing records the meeting.
- <a id="ev-EV-6027"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, AE 148** — *Sìneag's ride to Muileann chrom* (Baile dhomhain). Sìneag, custodian of the camp at Baile dhomhain, rides to the steward's house at Muileann chrom to ask whether the overseer's staff can answer for the two streets pulled down for the new spoil-tip. Mòrag nic Iain Maor can offer her nothing that year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0318"><em>Evictions at Baile dhomhain</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, AE 147</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6026"><em>Mòrag's private book</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, AE 147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6028"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, AE 148** — *The order for the third and fourth rows* (Muileann chrom). A printed order reaches Muileann chrom's overseer naming eleven households of the camp's third and fourth rows for clearance before the new gallery mouth. A' Chompanaidh's agent Osgood carries it to Mòrag nic Iain Maor's door, and carries her answer back unwritten.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0316"><em>The edict of seizure</em>, 25 an Giblean, AE 147</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0319"><em>Mòrag Maor lays down the staff</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6027"><em>Sìneag's ride to Muileann chrom</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, AE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6029"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, AE 148** — *Griogar Camshron breaks his staff*. Griogar Camshron, six years overseer of the north pit's eastern gallery, throws down his staff in his own yard within the week of Mòrag nic Iain Maor's refusal at Muileann chrom, rather than be the one overseer left holding wood A' Chompanaidh has marked for treachery.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0319"><em>Mòrag Maor lays down the staff</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6030"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, AE 148** — *The staff left standing*. The overseer at the silver country's edge walks away from his office without a word and leaves his staff propped against the counting-house wall, the third resignation of the season after Mòrag nic Iain Maor's and Griogar Camshron's, and word of it does not reach Muileann chrom until winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0319"><em>Mòrag Maor lays down the staff</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6031"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, AE 148** — *Coinneach Ruadh brings word of the guild's rifles* (Muileann chrom). Coinneach Ruadh, riding the district roads with unpaid news since his clerkship was taken, brings Mòrag nic Iain Maor word of Comann an Airgid's rifles and of a single council the custodians and priests mean to hold in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag before autumn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0320"><em>The silver guild arms</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, AE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0321"><em>Rifles by way of the pirates</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, AE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0322"><em>The council in the forest of Cnoc bheag</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, AE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6032"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, AE 148** — *Mòrag rides to the forest by night* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Mòrag nic Iain Maor rides twenty-eight miles by night off the ridge road to Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, and is among those who raise a hand for Eilidh nic Raghnaill to speak for the whole mining country's council.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0322"><em>The council in the forest of Cnoc bheag</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, AE 148</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6031"><em>Coinneach Ruadh brings word of the guild's rifles</em>, 17 an t-Samhain, AE 148</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0323"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, AE 149** — *The order to seize* (Ros dhomhain). Strake orders the taking of Eilidh nic Raghnaill and the members of the forest council. The constables go to Baile thais and find the house empty and the town silent.
- <a id="ev-IV-0324"></a>**20 an Gearran, AE 149** — *War*. The Dia-thìrich, acting together across the whole mining country for the first time, pass from grievance to open war.
- <a id="ev-EV-6008"></a>**23 an Gearran, AE 149** — *Coinneach Ruadh's ride of the twenty-eighth* (Muileann chrom). Coinneach Ruadh rides into Muileann chrom on the twenty-eighth of an Gearran with word that the grievance is called across every mining district at once, and that Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir has already had its answer that morning from Muileann chrom and Baile thais both.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0324"><em>War</em>, 20 an Gearran, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6009"></a>**25 an Gearran, AE 149** — *The beacons of the coal country answer* (Muileann chrom). On the night war is called, signal fires long kept secret are carried openly to every beacon height the mining districts hold, ridge answering ridge from Doire mhòr to the silver hills, the first time the whole coal country has shown itself lit at once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0324"><em>War</em>, 20 an Gearran, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0325"></a>**28 an Gearran, AE 149** — *The stores taken at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The war opens in the hills. At Muileann chrom crews under Mòrag nic Iain rush the walled store at first light, and its eleven constables yield without a shot. The rifles and the grain of the store are carried off before noon.
- <a id="ev-EV-6513"></a>**13 an Giblean, AE 149** — *Tòmas Odhar's hand on the gatepost* (Muileann chrom). At the fallen gate of the Muileann chrom store the old hewer Tòmas Odhar rests his hand flat on the gatepost and says he has carried coal out through it for six-and-thirty years and never thought to see rifles carried out through it instead. His words are repeated round the camp for a week after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0325"><em>The stores taken at Muileann chrom</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6514"></a>**4 an Cèitean, AE 149** — *Mòrag takes the sergeant's rifle herself* (Muileann chrom). Mòrag nic Iain Maor lifts the surrendered sergeant's rifle from the cobbles of the Muileann chrom store with her own hand rather than leave it to be gathered by another, the first weapon she has carried since she broke the overseer's staff the summer before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0325"><em>The stores taken at Muileann chrom</em>, 28 an Gearran, AE 149</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6513"><em>Tòmas Odhar's hand on the gatepost</em>, 13 an Giblean, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0326"></a>**24 an Cèitean, AE 149** — *The quay at Ceann fhada seized* (Ceann fhada). Crews from the camps take the Company's coal quay at Ceann fhada and sink two barges across its mouth. No coal leaves the hills by water again in this age.
- <a id="ev-EV-6501"></a>**26 an Cèitean, AE 149** — *Pàdraig Reamhar scuttles his own barge* (Ceann fhada). The boatman Pàdraig Reamhar, who built the larger of the two barges sunk at Ceann fhada with his own father twenty years before, knocks the plugs from her hull with his own hands and says afterward only that she had been a good boat.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0326"><em>The quay at Ceann fhada seized</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6515"></a>**30 an Cèitean, AE 149** — *Oswin Frayne rowed out from Ceann fhada* (Ceann fhada). A' Chompanaidh's harbour-master at Ceann fhada, Oswin Frayne, is rowed out past his own sunk barges and set aboard a boat for any harbour still flying Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's flag, unharmed, on the crews' own order.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0326"><em>The quay at Ceann fhada seized</em>, 24 an Cèitean, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0327"></a>**1 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149** — *The siege of the store at Baile thais* (Baile thais). At Baile thais the constables hold their walled pithead against the town for eleven days, as long as the first strike a lifetime before, and yield on the twelfth when their water fails. Eilidh nic Raghnaill sends them under guard to the coast unharmed. The Residency did not look for such mercy, and did not return it.
- <a id="ev-EV-6516"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149** — *Bread goes to the half-loaf at Baile thais* (Baile thais). By the seventh day of the siege of the walled store, the camp at Baile thais cuts its bread to a half-loaf a household, and the children who had at first jeered at the wall grow quiet and keep to their mothers' fires.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0327"><em>The siege of the store at Baile thais</em>, 1 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6517"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149** — *The constables of Baile thais sent to the coast* (Baile thais). On Eilidh nic Raghnaill's written order, carried down from Comhairle na Coille by a girl of fourteen, Seumas Ciar sends the thirty-one constables who yield the Baile thais store to the coast whole and fed, over the objection of hewers who have buried kin to the same walls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0327"><em>The siege of the store at Baile thais</em>, 1 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0327a"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149** — *The crews meet on the moor* (Coinneachadh a' Mhonaidh). Crew-leaders of Baile gharbh and the other northern pits meet by night on the moor above Cnoc naomh and fix the week of their rising. Each brings a stone of spoil from his own pit, and the stones are left in a cairn. The place is called Coinneachadh a' Mhonaidh, the meeting of the moor.
- <a id="ev-IV-0328"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, AE 149** — *The northern pits rise* (Baile gharbh). The crews at Baile gharbh and the northern pits rise in the same week, take the constable posts at Muileann shean and Tobar ghorm, and send the constables south on foot.
- <a id="ev-IV-0329"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *The coal road cut* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, shuts the gates of the house across the coal road, and the men in its loft come down armed. The road between the capital and the hills is cut at its half-way stage, and stays cut.
- <a id="ev-EV-6518"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *Uilleam Gobha's first grenades tried* (Muileann dhearg). On a moonless night behind his forge at Muileann dhearg, Uilleam Gobha tries the first of his tin-cased grenades, with only his eldest son holding a lamp a safe way off, and says it will do.
- <a id="ev-EV-6519"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *A finger lost before Uilleam Gobha's care* (Muileann dhearg). Before Uilleam Gobha takes up the crimping of the powder tins himself, another smith of Muileann dhearg loses three fingers to the work, a loss Uilleam afterward says he was determined it would not cost him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EV-6518"><em>Uilleam Gobha's first grenades tried</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0330"></a>**17 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *Uilleam Gobha's forge* (Muileann dhearg). At Muileann dhearg the smith Uilleam Gobha makes the Company's own blasting-powder into grenades cased in tin from the coal sheds, and forges pike-heads from rails torn up in the galleries. The rebels' council writes that without him it could not have fought its first season.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6518"><em>Uilleam Gobha's first grenades tried</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, AE 149</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EV-6519"><em>A finger lost before Uilleam Gobha's care</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0331"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *The capital rises* (Cathair dhearg). At Cathair dhearg the custodians break the Residency's locks on their council hall and sit in it again. The townsfolk hold Drochaid Cathair dhearg against the constables sent up from the harbour, and barricade the bridge built for the coal-carts with the carts themselves.
- <a id="ev-EV-6520"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *The council-hall lock broken with a coal-hammer* (Cathair dhearg). The custodians of Cathair dhearg break Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's locks on their own council-hall doors with a coal-hammer borrowed from the smithy across the square, and sit down again in the chairs shut from them for two years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0331"><em>The capital rises</em>, 18 an Lùnastal, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EV-6521"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *The coal-carts turned on their sides* (Cathair dhearg). The townsfolk of Cathair dhearg barricade the coal-cart bridge with A' Chompanaidh's own carts, turned on their sides and lashed together with ironmonger's chain, and hold it three days until the constables sent against it are called back to the harbour.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0331"><em>The capital rises</em>, 18 an Lùnastal, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0332"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, AE 149** — *Cathair dhomhain joins* (Cathair dhomhain). At Cathair dhomhain the townsfolk break open the Company's warehouse, the first building on Dia-thìr the Company ever owned, and carry off its tools for the council's companies.
- <a id="ev-IV-0333"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, AE 149** — *Muileann mhin takes sides* (Muileann mhin). At Muileann mhin, a river port just east of the capital, the townsfolk argue for three days, and then send boats to the council. Through the winter the boats carry food down the Abhainn fhionn to the capital.
- <a id="ev-IV-0334"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, AE 149** — *The Residency fortified* (Ros dhomhain). Lionel Strake draws the Administration back into the Residency above Ros dhomhain and fortifies the Company's quarter of the harbour. The city below, Dia-thìrich almost to a man, neither joins the rising nor withstands it, and the constables do not trust it enough to leave the walls.
- <a id="ev-EV-6522"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, AE 149** — *Strake's letter asking for a ship before winter* (Ros dhomhain). Lionel Strake writes to A' Chompanaidh's directors over the sea that the harbour town below Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir holds itself apart from the fighting only until it judges which side will leave it better off, and asks for more men, powder and a ship before the northern passage closes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-IV-0334"><em>The Residency fortified</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, AE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-IV-0335"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 149** — *The fight at the ford of Àth chiar* (Àth chiar). A column of constables and Company guards under Major Peter Ashdown marches up the coal road to relieve the hills, and is met at the ford of Àth chiar, where the rebels hold the far bank. Ashdown loses forty men and his baggage and turns back. The rebels lose nineteen, and the council's roll names them all.
- <a id="ev-EV-6523"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 149** — *The house swept at Baile thais* (Baile thais).
